themes.name: Inflammatory Disease & Immunology Biologics
themes.description: SYRE ORKA’s strength this week is primarily a continuation of the momentum from its recent positive Phase 2a psoriasis data for lead asset ORKA-001, which triggered major price target hikes and “strong buy” ratings in late April and established a high-conviction growth narrative. Investor focus remains on the favorable efficacy profile in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis and the expanded upside embedded in updated analyst targets, rather than any new discrete catalyst in the past few days. In short, the current move is an extension of the prior clinical-trial-driven rerating rather than a fresh news event.

themes.name: Franchise Auto Dealership Groups
themes.description: ABG, SAH, and PAG are all moving higher on the back of the Penske Automotive Group (PAG) take‑private proposal at $210/share in cash from Penske Corporation and Mitsui, which is repricing the entire auto dealer group on M&A/value-unlock read‑through. In PAG specifically, the non‑binding buyout offer and related arbitrage/setup dynamics are the direct catalyst, while peers like ABG and SAH are catching a sympathy bid as investors reassess private-market and strategic value across the franchise dealer space.

themes.name: U.S. Petroleum Refining & Downstream Processing
themes.description: Refining stocks are being driven higher by very strong crack spreads and refining margins, helped by tight global product supply and persistent geopolitical disruptions to refining capacity. Recent analyst actions have reinforced the theme: Raymond James highlighted mid-cap refiners DK, DINO and PARR as direct beneficiaries of record WTI 3‑2‑1 crack spreads, while Mizuho upgraded PSX and raised targets on PARR on improving refining operations and above-consensus Q2 earnings expectations. Index inclusion and ongoing analyst optimism around earnings and capital returns are adding incremental support for larger names like MPC and PSX.

themes.name: Hotel REIT Recovery & Re-Rating
themes.description: RLJ and XHR are moving higher on sector-specific and company-specific lodging REIT catalysts rather than a single headline event. RLJ is benefiting from continued strength and relative outperformance in hotel REITs over the past month, with the stock up roughly mid‑single digits in the last four weeks and over 60% year-on-year, as investors rotate into higher-beta real estate and travel plays. XHR’s bid is being supported by anticipation around its upcoming Q2 earnings release and dividend news flow, following solid prior quarters and the scheduled Q2 2026 earnings call timing, which is drawing incremental interest into the name.

themes.name: Casual Dining Restaurant Turnaround
themes.description: Brinker International (EAT) is trading higher this week mainly on continued momentum from early July media-driven enthusiasm, after Jim Cramer highlighted the name positively and called out upside in the story. That bullish commentary helped shift sentiment, and investors have been leaning into the casual dining recovery and EAT’s operating leverage as comps and traffic stabilize.

themes.name: Uniform Rental & Managed Workwear Services
themes.description: CTAS is being driven higher by a strong post-earnings reaction: the company reported robust Q4 and full-year results with higher sales, revenue, and net income, plus raised guidance for fiscal 2027, which the market is now pricing in more fully. In addition, Cintas has been in focus due to its UniFirst acquisition bid and a recent 8-K on results of operations, both reinforcing the growth and consolidation narrative around the name. I do not see a discrete, stock-specific news catalyst of similar magnitude for VST this week; its move appears more like a continuation of the recent uptrend tied to broader market and utility/power demand dynamics rather than a fresh headline.

themes.name: Enterprise Server, Storage & Data Infrastructure Hardware
themes.description: The main catalyst this week is Super Micro Computer’s blowout preliminary Q4 update, showing AI server gross margins roughly doubling prior guidance and a record ~$60B order backlog, which has re-rated the entire AI infrastructure complex and driven read-through buying in HPE, DELL, and broader server/storage peers. That sector-wide AI hardware optimism is being reinforced by Dell’s own strong AI server outlook and recent bullish analyst target hikes, keeping DELL particularly bid and pulling HPE along. STX and NTAP are moving largely on sympathy as investors rotate into data-center and storage names leveraged to the same AI infrastructure spend theme.

themes.name: U.S. Apparel & Fashion Recovery
themes.description: RVLV is being bid up on optimism around its upcoming earnings, with sell-side previews highlighting improving digital engagement, AI-driven personalization, and margin expansion as key drivers for better growth and profitability. CROX is rallying on strong post-earnings sentiment, multiple price target hikes (Needham, Williams Trading, Stifel, BoA) and confidence in North America DTC strength, Hey Dude’s second-half recovery, and potential buybacks. UA is moving with the broader footwear/apparel complex on sector rotation into consumer discretionary and positive sentiment around demand and capital allocation, even without a single dominant company-specific headline this week.

themes.name: Containerboard & Corrugated Packaging Producers
themes.description: IP and PKG are trading higher on the back of improving containerboard pricing and investor optimism around cost-cutting and footprint optimization initiatives at International Paper, alongside recent price hikes and cost reductions at Packaging Corp of America that support stronger near-term earnings. Sector sentiment has been reinforced by reports that containerboard prices used for shipping boxes and packaging are rising, which boosted both IP and PKG sharply late last week and is still being repriced by the market this week. There is no single new headline today; the move is largely a continuation of the rerating on better pricing, margin recovery, and restructuring narratives ahead of upcoming earnings.

themes.name: Office REIT Recovery & Re-Rating
themes.description: The main catalyst pushing SLG, BXP, HIW and CDP higher this week is renewed bullishness on U.S. office REITs driven by stronger leasing commentary and expectations that fundamentals are bottoming. SL Green has highlighted New York City office leasing as “the strongest I’ve seen in my career,” reinforcing the narrative of improving demand and de‑risking cash flows across the group. Positioning ahead of Q2 earnings for the office REIT complex is also contributing as investors rotate into higher‑beta real estate names.

themes.name: B2B Digital Financial Infrastructure & Payment Rails Modernization
themes.description: PAY (PayPal), QTWO (Q2 Holdings), and ACIW (ACI Worldwide) are all moving higher primarily on sector-wide strength in digital payments and fintech ahead of a heavy earnings week, with investors positioning for continued growth in electronic payments and digital banking demand. For QTWO specifically, the move is being supported by growing interest in its digital banking and fraud/AI solutions as banks accelerate digital transformation, which is seen as a driver of subscription revenue and platform adoption. ACIW’s bid is helped by recent positive developments in instant payments (Wero/EPI integrations, Rabobank partnership) and institutional accumulation, reinforcing the long-term real-time payments and open banking growth narrative.

themes.name: SMB & Workforce Business Services Platforms
themes.description: NSP is being bid up mainly on follow‑through from its SHRM26 conference exposure, where Insperity spotlighted its HR360, HRCore and HRScale platforms, driving fresh interest in its technology offering and valuation upside narrative. LZ is moving higher on the back of its better‑than‑expected Q1 results and raised full‑year revenue outlook, supported by recent insider buying that reinforces a confidence signal.

themes.name: IT Distribution & Technology Services Providers
themes.description: EFOR is being driven higher primarily by Truist Securities’ upgrade of Everforth to Buy from Hold and the accompanying price target hike to $36 from $33. The firm also raised its Q2 revenue and EPS estimates, citing stronger expected growth in commercial consulting services, which is feeding bullish sentiment into this week’s trade. INGM’s move is more anticipatory, with positioning ahead of its upcoming Q2 earnings release and recent recognition/partnership wins rather than a single fresh headline catalyst.

themes.name: Clinical-Stage Oncology Biotech
themes.description: TG Therapeutics (TGTX) is being driven higher by continued momentum after hitting a new 52-week high, reflecting strong investor demand for its multiple sclerosis franchise and expectations for further revenue growth. Enliven Therapeutics (ELVN) is moving higher on the back of recent positive Phase 1 ENABLE trial data in chronic myeloid leukemia, subsequent FDA-aligned development path, and multiple analyst price target hikes (including Goldman Sachs and H.C. Wainwright) following a large, successfully executed equity offering that strengthened the balance sheet.

themes.name: Professional Advisory & Business Services
themes.description: The main catalyst appears to be continued momentum from CRA International’s Q1 2026 results, which showed record revenue and came with recent positive commentary around the business. For CBIZ (CBZ), I do not see a matching company-specific catalyst in the provided results, so the move higher this week may be more sector- or market-driven than news-driven.

themes.name: Peptide & Hormone Therapies for Metabolic & Endocrine Disorders
themes.description: CORT is being driven higher by the resubmission of its NDA for relacorilant in Cushing’s syndrome, reviving expectations for an approval and commercialization path. PTGX strength is tied to its recent FDA approval and strong launch of Icotyde plus the NDA submission for rusfertide in polycythemia vera, reinforcing a multi‑asset value story. XERS and MBX appear to be moving largely on sector sentiment and speculative positioning rather than a single, clear company‑specific headline this week.

themes.name: Enterprise HR & Workforce Management SaaS
themes.description: WDAY is being driven higher by a rebound bid into large-cap software on the back of strong recent earnings, AI-related optimism, and multiple bullish pieces of research calling it undervalued and highlighting margin/AI momentum. PCTY is moving with the broader HCM/software complex, helped by positive commentary around product expansion, broker channel strength, and its efforts to deepen its HCM moat (including embedded retirement plans). ALIT’s strength is tied to company-specific news flow around cost-saving validation for its Healthcare Navigation offering, governance/leadership changes, and positioning ahead of its reverse split, all contributing to a re-rating in a thinly traded small-cap name.

themes.name: AI-Powered Enterprise Analytics & Intelligent Workflow SaaS
themes.description: INTA is higher on fresh customer-deal news around Intapp DealCloud/Celeste wins, which the market is treating as validation of its AI-driven relationship-intelligence platform. AVPT is moving on positive AI-platform coverage and recent product/news flow, including AgentPulse Command Center and “agentic AI governance” updates. I don’t see a clear news catalyst in the provided results for AMPL, so its move may be stock-specific or tied to a separate headline not included here.

themes.name: Life Insurance & Annuity Providers
themes.description: PFG, PRU, and MET are being pulled higher mainly by sector-wide tailwinds: stable-to-elevated rates, strong equity markets, and ongoing optimism around life/retirement product profitability, which support spreads and asset-based fees across life insurers. Company-specific near-term catalysts are also in focus, particularly upcoming Q2 earnings for PFG and PRU, where investors expect confirmation of solid earnings momentum and capital return, alongside recent positive/raised price targets and prior earnings beats and dividend hikes (notably at MET and PFG). Broadly constructive risk sentiment in U.S. equities is adding beta support to high-quality financials, amplifying these stock-specific drivers.

themes.name: U.S. Domestic Steel Producers
themes.description: The main catalyst pushing STLD and NUE higher this week is the continued rebound in U.S. steel prices, with benchmark hot-rolled coil moving back toward roughly $1,200/ton on tight supply, mill price hikes, extended lead times, and tariff-reduced imports. In addition, STLD is getting a direct boost from its stronger-than-expected Q2 earnings print with record shipments and elevated realized prices, while NUE is being bid up into its upcoming Q2 earnings on guidance that reflects the same steel price strength. Broader optimism around domestic demand, infrastructure and reshoring, plus recent analyst target increases on the group, are reinforcing the move.

themes.name: Industrial Construction Execution & On-Site Supply Chain
themes.description: TPC is being driven higher by a string of large contract wins and balance sheet improvement, including the $651.8M Guam defense power infrastructure award and subsequent debt refinancing/redemption that are boosting backlog, earnings visibility, and perceived credit quality. SUNB’s move is largely sector-driven, benefiting from rotation into small-cap financials on post-holiday positioning and higher-rate resilience rather than a single stock-specific headline. DNOW and RYZ are gaining on corporate actions: DNOW from its completed combination with MRC Global that enhances scale and synergies, and RYZ from its completed merger with Olympic Steel plus a fresh 52-week high and expanded incentive plan that signal confidence and support momentum.

themes.name: Truckload & LTL Freight Carriers
themes.description: The move in HUBG, ARCB, SNDR, and TFII this week is mainly a sector trade: investors are rotating into truckload/intermodal names on expectations of a late‑cycle freight upturn, improving spot and contract pricing, and better operating leverage as volumes firm. Within that, HUBG also has stock‑specific momentum as it stabilizes after the accounting restatement/delinquency overhang, with short covering and “buy” technical signals helping fuel a rebound. Broader risk‑on sentiment and rate‑cut expectations are adding a tailwind to economically sensitive transport stocks as a group.

themes.name: Smart Home Security & Comfort Systems
themes.description: ALRM’s move appears tied to renewed attention after being added to several Russell value and small-cap indices in late June, which can trigger index-fund buying. For REZI, the main catalyst this week is Resideo’s planned ADI spin-off and the related senior-notes financing/escrow update, which the market is treating as a transaction-driven catalyst.

themes.name: Wealth Management & Retail Brokerage Platforms
themes.description: The primary catalyst this week is stronger-than-expected earnings and asset-growth prints across the wealth/online brokerage complex, led by Raymond James and Charles Schwab, which are lifting the group on read‑through to AUM, fee income, and trading activity. RJF reported record Q3 net revenues and an earnings beat, while SCHW posted record Q2 revenue and EPS above expectations, reinforcing the bullish narrative for retail investing, advisory, and platform businesses that benefits SEIC, SF, HOOD, AMP and peers. Sector sentiment is further aided by Schwab’s ongoing expansion in digital assets/crypto and continued analyst confidence, which supports higher multiples across brokerage and asset‑management names.

themes.name: U.S. Apparel & Lifestyle Brand Recovery
themes.description: VSXY is being driven higher by ongoing enthusiasm around Victoria’s Secret’s turnaround story: strong Q1 earnings, raised FY26 guidance, and persistent short-covering/ momentum following the recent proxy victory and operational improvements, with no new single headline this week but continued bullish coverage and product/newsflow (e.g., PINK launches) keeping buyers engaged. OXM’s strength appears more technical than fundamental this week, as the stock rebounds from prior weakness and benefits from a positive short-term setup and improving sentiment in discretionary/apparel names, rather than a specific fresh company-level news catalyst.

themes.name: Molecular Diagnostics & DNA-Based Genetic Testing
themes.description: The main catalyst appears to be Qiagen’s inclusion in the Russell 1000 Dynamic Index, which has drawn index-following buying and broader investor attention this week. QIAGEN also had supportive headlines from analyst actions and product/portfolio expansion news, which may be reinforcing the move. For BLLN, I don’t see a clear company-specific catalyst in the results provided; the stock’s move looks more tied to general medical-lab sector sentiment than a fresh headline.

themes.name: Online Insurance Comparison & Digital Marketplace Platforms
themes.description: The move in EVER MAX this week is being driven by the Meta partnership announcement with Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions, under which Meta will support roughly 837–900 MW of new solar and wind capacity in India and purchase all green attributes from these projects. That deal has pushed Clean Max shares to an all-time high and triggered a multi-session rally of roughly 25%, drawing momentum and thematic interest into the broader “Ever/Clean Max” complex.

themes.name: Defense Precision Components & Mission-Critical Subsystems
themes.description: Expanding U.S. and allied defense budgets are flowing downstream to second-tier precision suppliers — superalloy engine castings (DPC), frequency/timing control devices for defense electronics (FEIM), and defense mission-solutions supply chain (VVX) — a layer entirely distinct from the large primes and structural composites already in live themes.

themes.name: Consumer Fintech & Digital Credit Platforms
themes.description: Sezzle (SEZL) is being driven higher by a combination of strong growth fundamentals and capital return: recent reports highlight rapid revenue and EPS growth, attractive valuation metrics, and a new or expanded stock repurchase authorization that signals management’s confidence in the business. For Dave (DAVE), the main recent catalyst has been a shareholder vote tied to corporate actions, with the stock continuing to trade within its high-volatility uptrend supported by strong multi‑year revenue and margin expansion rather than a specific fresh news event this week.

themes.name: Cloud Supply Chain & Warehouse Management Software
themes.description: MANH is being driven higher by a strong Q2 earnings beat and a raised 2025 outlook, which triggered a sharp rerating in the name. SPSC is moving on strategic news: the company announced an agreement to sell its 3P Revenue Recovery business and hired Morgan Stanley to explore a broader sale amid activist pressure, boosting takeover/speculation premium.

themes.name: Life Science Tools & Analytical Instruments
themes.description: TMO is being lifted mainly by its strong Q2 earnings beat and raised full-year guidance, which also triggered a wave of analyst price-target upgrades. WAT’s move is more likely tied to product/diagnostic news flow, but there is no clear unusual-volume catalyst in the results you provided.

themes.name: Cloud Data Storage & Analytics Infrastructure
themes.description: BLZE is being driven higher primarily by the recently announced five-year, multi‑exabyte AI cloud storage agreement with CoreWeave valued at $335 million, which investors and analysts are treating as a game‑changing validation of Backblaze’s role in AI infrastructure. The deal has sparked substantial analyst upgrades and higher price targets, reframing the company as an emerging AI cloud/GenAI storage contender and supporting a re‑rating of the stock. Broader enthusiasm around accelerating AI storage demand and Backblaze’s B2 cloud growth is reinforcing the move.

themes.name: Cross-Border & International Payments Processing
themes.description: The move in EEFT and GPN this week is being driven mainly by a sector-wide bid into payments/fintech ahead of their upcoming Q2 earnings, with expectations for solid volume and margin prints as travel and consumer spending remain resilient. Global Payments has a specific near-term catalyst in its August 5 Q2 release and recent supportive analyst commentary and buy ratings, which is lifting the group. Euronet tends to trade as a high-beta peer and is catching a sympathy move as investors rotate into under-owned, reasonably valued payment processors.

themes.name: Medical Device Mean-Reversion & Rotation Recovery
themes.description: INSP is being driven by new positive clinical data from the SLEEP 2026 meeting and publication of the PREDICTOR/ADHERE studies showing strong efficacy and adherence for its hypoglossal nerve stimulation therapy, alongside an 8-K board change that has brought trader attention. TNDM is moving ahead of its upcoming earnings as investors position around the impact of its pay-as-you-go model shift in diabetes pumps. XRAY and CNMD are benefiting from recent management/CFO changes and product/clinical milestones that reinforce their strategic positioning in dental and minimally invasive surgery, respectively, drawing incremental institutional interest.

themes.name: Senior & Long-Term Care Healthcare REITs
themes.description: The main catalyst is growing investor focus on the senior housing / healthcare REIT theme, supported by data showing U.S. senior housing occupancy approaching 90% with minimal new supply and several names (including OHI and VTR peers) breaking to 12‑month and even all‑time highs. This week’s move is largely a continuation of that structural-demand trade, with demographic tailwinds and perceived defensiveness driving inflows into long-term care and senior housing landlords. Index inclusion for VTR in Russell defensive/value indices and positive sentiment/target hikes around OHI are reinforcing the bid across the group.

themes.name: Specialty Insurance Underwriting & Brokerage
themes.description: PLMR is higher this week mainly on post-earnings momentum: Palomar’s Q1 2026 results beat estimates, with EPS and revenue both topping expectations and revenue up sharply year over year. For RYAN, the move is more likely tied to stock-specific news around Ryan Specialty, not Palomar; if you meant RYAN, recent coverage points to institutional accumulation and a generally solid Q1 backdrop rather than a single headline catalyst.

themes.name: Department Store Retail Recovery
themes.description: KSS is being lifted mainly by company-specific turnaround news, especially Kohl’s appointment of a new chief operating officer and the market’s focus on its operational overhaul and balance-sheet/liquidity improvements. Recent coverage also points to the stock reacting to stronger quarterly results and a new brand partnership, while DDS appears to be moving with the same retail-turnaround sentiment rather than a separate sector-wide catalyst.

themes.name: Network Security & Zero-Trust Edge
themes.description: The move is being driven by a broad bid into cybersecurity and data‑protection names on the back of accelerating AI‑related cyber risk and rising enterprise security spend, which is lifting the dedicated cyber ETFs and baskets these stocks sit in. Fortinet, CrowdStrike, Okta and peers are also seeing follow‑through from strong recent earnings/AI narratives plus incremental partnership/integration headlines (e.g., CVLT’s integrations with Microsoft Security, CrowdStrike and Okta, and FTNT’s Intel foundry/security collaboration), reinforcing the theme. Flows into sector baskets like the CRWD·FTNT·OKTA·TENB·RBRK group highlighted by traders are amplifying the move as investors rotate into high‑beta security plays.

themes.name: European Bank Stocks
themes.description: The primary catalyst is strong European bank earnings and guidance, led by Banco Santander’s record H1 results and Q2 beats on net interest income and profit, plus a large ongoing share buyback that has lifted sentiment across the sector. In addition, a broader risk-on move into European and Latin American financials as oil prices ease and the dollar softens is supporting Spanish and UK banks, benefiting SAN, BBVA, NWG, LYG, BCS, and ING together. NatWest’s recently completed Evelyn Partners acquisition and upcoming H1 print are also helping underpin UK bank momentum.

themes.name: Private Mortgage Insurance
themes.description: The move is mostly a sector/rates trade in mortgage insurers, with no single company-specific headline clearly explaining all four names. The closest identifiable catalysts are Radian (RDN) hitting a 52-week high on strong recent earnings/continued positive earnings-surprise momentum and Essent (ESNT) benefiting from Moody’s rating upgrades/stable outlook, while NMIH appears to be drifting higher ahead of its July 30 earnings release and MTG’s usual drivers are earnings, portfolio stats, reinsurance, dividends and buybacks.

themes.name: Property & Casualty Insurance Underwriters
themes.description: For THG, the main recent company-specific catalyst is its inclusion in U.S. News & World Report’s 2026–2027 “Best Companies to Work For” list, which has coincided with the stock pushing to new 52-week highs and can support sentiment and valuation rerating in a quality-focused insurance tape. For AFG, the driver is ongoing positive follow-through from recent dividend, earnings, and conference-related news flow ahead of upcoming financial events, with investors positioning for capital return and steady fundamentals in the specialty insurance space. For WRB, ACGL, AXS, and ORI, the move is largely sector-driven: property & casualty and specialty insurers are benefiting from a constructive macro backdrop for underwriting margins and investment income, with no single dominant, stock-specific headline this week beyond that broader insurance rally.

themes.name: Global Crude & Product Tanker Fleet Operators
themes.description: The main driver is a sector-wide bid into crude and product tankers on renewed geopolitical and oil market risk, specifically headlines around potential disruption in/around the Strait of Hormuz and rising oil prices that tighten tanker supply and push spot rates higher. Individual positives like TRMD’s strong LR2 spot exposure and special dividend, DHT’s VLCC strength and newbuild orders, and broadly favorable media/analyst sentiment toward tanker names are reinforcing the move but are secondary to the macro/geopolitical shipping thesis.

themes.name: Global Steel & Metal Producers Recovery
themes.description: The main near-term catalyst is positive analyst and insider-related news: BNP Paribas upgraded Commercial Metals to Outperform and raised its price target to $75 on July 8, and Smart Insider highlighted CMC as “Pick of the Week” on July 22 following a CEO share purchase. These have reinforced the broader Buy consensus and attracted incremental institutional and retail interest, supporting the stock’s move higher this week.

themes.name: Industrial & Logistics REITs
themes.description: The move looks fundamentally driven by leasing and portfolio-growth headlines, especially TRNO’s recent lease announcements in Doral and other markets, plus a prior property acquisition update. I don’t see a distinct fresh company-specific catalyst for STAG, so the week’s strength likely reflects the broader industrial REIT bid and sector flow rather than one major new headline.

themes.name: Open-Air & Strip Mall Retail REITs
themes.description: This week’s strength in KIM, UE, REG, PECO, KRG, and BRX is being driven primarily by a sector-wide bid into grocery-anchored and open-air shopping center REITs as investors rotate toward defensive, income-oriented real estate ahead of upcoming earnings and in the wake of Kroger’s Giant Eagle acquisition headlines. Kroger’s deal is reinforcing the durability and growth narrative for necessity-based retail, which benefits landlords with similar tenant mixes and footprint exposure. There is no single stock-specific catalyst for these names this week; the move is largely a thematic trade around necessity retail and REIT yield.

themes.name: Insurance Brokerage & Distribution Services
themes.description: The main catalyst is a positive sector call: Zacks highlighted insurance brokers including Aon, Brown & Brown and Arthur J. Gallagher as beneficiaries of strong pricing, consolidation, and organic growth in the insurance brokerage industry, which is lifting sentiment across the group. In addition, AJG specifically is being supported by a continued stream of accretive specialty and wholesale brokerage acquisitions and AI/technology initiatives that reinforce its long‑term growth narrative. Analyst price-target increases and constructive earnings/revenue trends for AON and its peers are reinforcing the move higher this week.

themes.name: U.S. Passenger Airlines
themes.description: The main catalyst lifting SKYW, UAL, DAL, and ALK this week is a combination of strong summer travel demand and a pullback in crude oil prices, which improves margin visibility for the group. Sector pieces highlight “airline stocks soar as summer travel demand holds strong” and “airline stocks jump as oil eases” alongside record holiday booking trends and robust operational performance at carriers like Alaska and Hawaiian, supporting a bid across U.S. airline equities. Additionally, recent analyst target hikes and commentary flag upside catalysts for Delta and SkyWest, reinforcing positive sentiment in the space.

themes.name: Canadian Big Banks
themes.description: The main catalyst pushing RY, TD, BNS, BMO and CM higher this week is positive read-through from strong Q2 U.S. bank earnings, especially in capital markets, lending and credit quality, which Scotiabank and RBC analysts highlight as supportive for the large Canadian banks’ near‑term earnings outlook. In particular, strength in capital markets and U.S. commercial lending is seen as especially beneficial for BMO, TD and RY, improving sentiment toward the group as a whole. This is occurring against a backdrop of already solid capital positions and sector momentum, so the U.S. results are reinforcing an existing constructive view rather than reversing a negative trend.

themes.name: U.S. Regional & Mid-Cap Commercial Banks
themes.description: The likely catalyst is a regional-bank rebound after easing Treasury yields and a firmer rate-cut narrative, with traders also rotating into financials ahead of this week’s Fed-related data and minutes. EWBC has an added stock-specific boost from Barclays raising its price target to $150 from $142 while keeping Overweight. I don’t see a single company-specific catalyst tying all six names together, so this looks more like sector rotation than one shared headline.

themes.name: Cyber Exposure Management & Vulnerability Assessment
themes.description: RPD, TENB and QLYS are being driven higher by a combination of renewed rotation into cybersecurity/software as an AI-adjacent “safe” growth theme and name-specific positives. For Tenable, fresh news that it is expanding Tenable One to include application security data, plus recent target hikes and upgrades highlighting its positioning around AI-driven vulnerabilities, is adding incremental upside. Qualys is benefiting from bullish analyst moves (notably Scotiabank’s upgrade to Outperform and a prior JPMorgan upgrade) and the halo from stronger vulnerability-management and platform narratives that are lifting the whole group, including Rapid7.

themes.name: Industrial Fluid Control, Filtration & Water Infrastructure Equipment
themes.description: IEX (Indian Energy Exchange) is being driven higher by strong Q1 FY27 results showing a ~12% YoY PAT increase and ~16% YoY growth in traded electricity volumes, supported by record summer power demand and higher exchange prices. For IDEX (IEX) in the US, the main near-term catalyst is its upcoming quarterly cash dividend, with the stock trading ex-dividend this month. For IR (Ingersoll Rand), FELE (Franklin Electric), and DCI (Donaldson), the move appears more rotational/sector-based with no single stock-specific news catalyst dominating this week.

themes.name: Copper Mining & Production
themes.description: The main catalyst is a broad rebound in copper prices and renewed optimism on global industrial demand, which is lifting copper miners as high-beta proxies for the metal. For SCCO specifically, the move is being amplified by expectations of stronger upcoming earnings and margin expansion at higher realized copper prices, alongside supportive analyst commentary and index-related flows. TGB and FCX are being carried by the same macro copper theme: tight supply, electrification/AI-related demand narratives, and positioning ahead of copper-sensitive economic data and earnings.

themes.name: Bitcoin Mining & Crypto Infrastructure Operators
themes.description: CIFR is moving higher mostly on a sector sympathy rally, not company-specific news, after Hut 8 landed a second $9.8 billion AI data-center lease and IREN raised its AI/cloud revenue outlook. That reinforced the market’s view that bitcoin miners pivoting into AI infrastructure can monetize their power and data-center assets. Cipher also got a lift from bargain-hunting and positioning ahead of its Q2 earnings.

themes.name: Commercial Real Estate Brokerage & Advisory Services
themes.description: The main catalyst pushing CBRE, NMRK, and JLL higher is renewed optimism around the commercial real estate operations cycle, driven by stronger leasing and capital markets activity, plus growing outsourcing demand that supports more recurring, fee-based revenue. Recent Q1 2026 results and guidance from CBRE and JLL highlighted double‑digit revenue growth, EPS beats, and raised or reinforced 2026 outlooks, while analysts have been emphasizing EPS growth in the high‑teens for both CBRE and Newmark and recommending the group as a way to play the sector’s rebound. The market is effectively repricing these names as beneficiaries of CRE recovery, data-center/AI-related infrastructure demand, and corporate outsourcing trends, rather than cyclical office-only proxies.

themes.name: Powersports & Recreational Vehicle Manufacturers
themes.description: Harley-Davidson (HOG) is being driven higher mainly by a bullish analyst shift and earnings setup: Loop Capital upgraded the stock to Buy with a higher $32 target, and investors are positioning ahead of its Q2 print and a new financing partnership for HDFS. Polaris (PII) is moving on Bank of America’s positive earnings preview, with estimates held near the high end of full-year guidance and expectations for solid upcoming results for the powersports group.

themes.name: Semiconductor Wafer Foundry & Advanced IC Manufacturing
themes.description: AMAT, ICHR, and TSEM are all being lifted by the same macro catalyst: renewed optimism around AI-driven semiconductor and capex spending, highlighted by TSMC’s announced chip price increases and its $100 billion Arizona expansion, which point to structurally higher demand for wafer fab equipment and related subsystems. For AMAT specifically, the move has been reinforced by bullish sell-side target hikes, strong recent earnings and guidance, and commentary from management and peers (Micron, Qualcomm, Meta) that underscore long runway in AI infrastructure and advanced packaging tools. TSEM has an additional idiosyncratic boost from its recent AI photonics deal and IP settlement, which has sharpened the market’s focus on its role in silicon photonics and specialty foundry capacity.

themes.name: Korean Financial Sector Recovery
themes.description: Shinhan Financial Group (SHG) is moving higher this week primarily on the back of its FY2025 profit growth and technical breakout above the 200-day moving average, which has attracted momentum and value investors. Recent disclosures around its 2026 value-up plan, higher payout intentions, and strategic moves such as weighing a Lotte Insurance acquisition are reinforcing the rerating trend in Korean financials. Sector-wide strength in South Korean banks and improving net interest income dynamics are adding a supportive macro tailwind to the move.

themes.name: Independent Power Producers & Nuclear Generation
themes.description: VST (diversified power generation with a large nuclear fleet), TLN (wholesale electricity generation), and CEG (pure-play nuclear generation via Constellation) are all leveraged to surging U.S. power demand driven by data center electrification and AI infrastructure build-out. The catalyst is structural: utilities cannot build fast enough, putting IPPs and nuclear operators in a strong pricing position in deregulated wholesale markets. This is a distinct sub-theme from traditional utilities — these companies sell into merchant markets, not regulated rate cases.

themes.name: Industrial Automation & Electrical Control Systems
themes.description: AME’s move looks tied to renewed investor focus on industrial automation and margins/free cash flow, not a single fresh headline catalyst. HLIO is being helped by recent positive company news, especially its first-quarter results that beat outlook and showed 17% sales growth, plus newer product/market expansion updates. ROK appears to be moving on company-specific wins like the Aalo Atomics control-systems selection and broader optimism around factory upgrades and industrial automation.

themes.name: Custom AI Silicon & Chip Architecture Licensing
themes.description: ARM, ALAB, CRDO, and MRVL are all being pulled higher by the same macro theme: renewed risk-on flows into AI and high-speed connectivity semis as investors rotate back into AI infrastructure after a recent pullback, with strong data-center demand and optical/interconnect growth the core narrative. For MRVL specifically, the move is reinforced by bullish analyst calls and target hikes tied to its AI data center and optical interconnect exposure, plus ongoing enthusiasm around its Nvidia/AI custom silicon positioning. CRDO and ALAB are benefiting from the same AI connectivity thesis and positive analyst sentiment, with CRDO supported by very strong growth guidance and ALAB by recent target hikes highlighting CXL upside.

themes.name: Targeted Protein Degradation Oncology
themes.description: The main catalyst is renewed enthusiasm around targeted protein degradation and “molecular glue” degraders following Kymera’s accelerated timeline and strong momentum, which is lifting the broader degradation space and spilling over into Monte Rosa (GLUE). In GLUE specifically, investors are reacting to recent AACR data on its Cyclin E1‑directed molecular glue degrader for CCNE1‑amplified solid tumors and looking ahead to the expected IND submission for MRT‑55811 later in 2026. Together, those clinical and regulatory milestones are driving incremental speculative interest and bid in the stock this week.

themes.name: Automotive Components & Tire Suppliers
themes.description: Goodyear (GT) is being supported this week by its upcoming index change, moving from the S&P MidCap 400 to the S&P SmallCap 600 effective before trading on July 6, 2026, which typically drives incremental demand from index and small-cap managers. Adient (ADNT) is trading higher on the back of its recent Q2 FY26 earnings beat and raised 2026 guidance, with stronger-than-expected EPS, slight revenue beat, and ongoing share repurchases reinforcing the bullish narrative despite margin and regional demand concerns.

themes.name: Cloud Communications & Contact Center Platforms
themes.description: FIVN is trading higher on follow-through from its strong Q1 print and guidance, including accelerating AI-driven revenue, a swing to GAAP profitability, and the announcement of a new $200M share repurchase program that has reinforced the bullish analyst narrative around its Voice AI Agents and broader CX AI positioning. BAND’s move is more technical and sentiment-driven, with the stock in an established uptrend supported by bullish market/AI SaaS sentiment rather than a single discrete company-specific news release this week.

themes.name: Digital Advertising Technology Platforms
themes.description: Magnite and QuinStreet are moving higher on sympathetic momentum to the broader ad-tech and performance marketing complex, helped by renewed interest in AI-driven ad solutions and connected TV/retail media data partnerships such as Magnite’s work with Walmart and dentsu/DIRECTV. There is also a structural catalyst from the DOJ antitrust case against Google’s ad business, which is driving flows into independent ad platforms. In the absence of company-specific headlines this week, the move is largely a sector re-rating and correlation trade rather than a discrete news release for MGNI or QNST.

themes.name: Liquid Biopsy & Multi-Cancer Early Detection
themes.description: GH Research (ticker GH, and GHR on some feeds) is trading higher this week on M&A read-through from Bloomberg’s report that Eli Lilly is in advanced talks to acquire AtaiBeckley, whose lead psychedelic asset targets the same treatment-resistant depression indication as GH’s GH001. That news, combined with RBC highlighting GH Research as the top beneficiary of this deal dynamic and a supportive regulatory backdrop for psychedelic therapies, is driving incremental buying interest and a sharp move higher.

themes.name: Emerging Market Digital Commerce & Fintech Platforms
themes.description: MELI is being bid up mainly on investors revisiting the long-term growth story ahead of its upcoming Q2 earnings, with renewed focus on accelerating revenue, strong user engagement, and management’s confidence in its heavy ecosystem investments across e-commerce and fintech. Several recent articles and analyst pieces frame the stock as a potential once-in-a-decade compounder despite margin pressure, which is drawing in buyers after the roughly 13% rebound from June lows. The near-term earnings date and the market’s willingness to look through margin compression toward AI, logistics, credit and advertising-driven growth are the key catalysts this week.

themes.name: B2B Marketing Automation & Customer Engagement SaaS
themes.description: KVYO is being driven higher by continued enthusiasm around its recent AI product rollouts, accelerating revenue growth, record operating margins, raised full‑year guidance, and an expanded share buyback, which together reinforce the earnings and profitability story. BRZE is moving in sympathy as a closely correlated peer in marketing automation/CRM software, benefiting from read‑through from KVYO’s strength rather than a discrete new headline of its own. HUBS is riding the broader rebound in high‑quality SaaS/CRM names after strong Q1 results and a reputation for consistent estimate beats, with investors positioning ahead of upcoming investor events despite a prior downgrade.

themes.name: Digital Payments Processing & Merchant Acquiring Networks
themes.description: FOUR is trading higher on continued follow‑through from last week’s upside earnings surprise and raised guidance, which has investors leaning into the name as a small‑cap payments winner ahead of broader fintech M&A chatter. PYPL is being driven almost entirely by the reported $53 billion, $60.50/share takeover offer from Stripe and Advent International, which has re-rated the stock toward the bid and fueled expectations for either a higher offer or competing interest. Both moves are being reinforced by traders positioning ahead of upcoming earnings and board responses to the PYPL bid.

themes.name: Cloud Observability & AIOps Monitoring Platforms
themes.description: DT, PD, and DDOG are all benefiting from a renewed bid into observability/monitoring and incident-response names tied to AI infrastructure spend and cloud security, with Datadog in particular seeing momentum from strong Q1 results, rising revenue/EPS estimates, and aggressive AI product launches like Bits AI and GPU/LLM observability. The group is also catching support from recent analyst price target hikes and “Leader” recognition in observability, which reinforce the AI-driven growth narrative and institutional interest in the space. In the absence of stock-specific headlines this week for DT and PD, the move is largely a sympathy trade to DDOG’s AI/observability strength and positioning ahead of the next earnings prints.

themes.name: Precious Metals Miners & Royalty Streamers
themes.description: The primary catalyst is a sharp move higher in spot gold prices, which has lifted the entire gold-mining complex. Rising bullion, driven by geopolitical tensions around the U.S.–Iran situation and its implications for inflation and Fed policy, is pushing NEM, KGC, AU, GFI, HMY and AGI higher in tandem. There does not appear to be a single, stock-specific news item this week; the move is largely macro and commodity-price driven.

themes.name: Precious Metals Royalty & Streaming Companies
themes.description: The primary driver for Franco-Nevada (FNV), Royal Gold (RGLD), and Wheaton Precious Metals (WPM) this week is macro: firmer gold prices on softer Fed rate expectations and a weaker dollar, which is lifting gold-linked royalty/streaming names leveraged to the metal. Company-specific news flow for FNV has been relatively quiet and mixed (Burkina Faso stream dispute, Cobre Panamá stockpile processing approvals, record prior-quarter results), so the move is largely a sector-wide precious metals and royalty trade rather than a single headline catalyst. Earnings estimate upgrades and optimistic analyst targets for FNV add incremental support but are secondary to the gold-price and rates backdrop.

themes.name: Financial Services Vertical SaaS
themes.description: JKHY is being helped by bullish analyst revisions and commentary on upside potential, alongside positive sentiment around its expanded Google Cloud AI security partnership for banks. GWRE is trading higher on strong fiscal Q3 results and ongoing news flow highlighting AI-driven insurance innovation and broader adoption of its platform. SSNC is benefiting from news about its push into tokenized funds and digital cash settlement using stablecoins and tokenized bank deposits, reinforcing a structural growth and innovation narrative.

themes.name: Financial Compliance & Regulatory Reporting SaaS
themes.description: WK’s strength in DFIN this week is being driven primarily by renewed interest in its AI-enabled disclosure and compliance tools, including the recently launched AI-powered iXBRL tagging capability within its Active Intelligence suite. Investors are also viewing DFIN as a beneficiary of the SEC’s proposed shift toward more flexible reporting (new Form 10-S), which highlights structural demand for its ActiveDisclosure platform. The combination of these regulatory and AI themes is catalyzing a rerating of the stock.

themes.name: Analog & Microcontroller Semiconductors — Automotive & Industrial Cycle Recovery
themes.description: The primary catalyst is a broad-based upturn in analog and embedded semiconductor demand, especially in industrial, automotive, and data center markets, which is driving estimate revisions and a sector-wide re-rating across ADI, MCHP, NXPI, ON, and TXN. Texas Instruments’ role as an analog bellwether, coupled with multiple analyst price target and estimate hikes ahead of its Q2 earnings, is reinforcing the view that the cyclical trough is over and that the recovery in these end-markets is sustainable. This analog/industrial recovery is being layered on top of accelerating AI data center infrastructure demand, providing a powerful combination of cyclical and structural growth drivers for the group.

themes.name: Defense Prime Contractors & Aerospace Systems
themes.description: The primary catalyst is a very strong Q2 earnings season for the defense primes, with Lockheed Martin and RTX both posting beat-and-raise quarters, record backlogs, and raised 2026 guidance tied to sustained global rearmament and Pentagon restocking of missiles and munitions. LMT and RTX’s moves are spilling over into the group, helping LHX and HII as investors rotate back into defense on the combination of robust order books, missile and space contract wins, and renewed focus on air and missile defense capabilities. A supportive macro backdrop of ongoing geopolitical tensions and U.S. defense budget visibility is reinforcing the bid across these names.

themes.name: Coastal & Suburban Residential Rental REITs
themes.description: The move appears tied to a fresh analyst re-rating of the single-family rental group, led by Barclays lifting AMH’s price target, which is supporting sentiment across residential REITs. INVH and the apartment names EQR and ESS are likely trading higher in sympathy on the same sector rotation rather than on company-specific news.

themes.name: Multifamily Apartment REITs
themes.description: The main catalyst this week is a supportive macro backdrop for rate‑sensitive REITs as inflation expectations and long rates have eased, improving the outlook for apartment REIT cash flows and valuations. On the name-specific side, UDR is benefiting from recent bullish sell-side actions (Wells Fargo price target increase and Deutsche Bank upgrade to Buy with a higher target), which reinforce the broader bid into residential REITs. The rest of the group (CPT, MAA, IRT, UDR) is moving largely on sector rotation rather than stock-specific headlines.

themes.name: For-Profit Education & Career Training Providers
themes.description: Workforce retraining demand from displaced workers and the ongoing push for vocational and career-focused education credentials are creating tailwinds for for-profit education operators. The correlation cluster (CVSA, LINC, PRDO, STRA) alongside existing theme members suggests broader sector-level accumulation. Community college alternatives and online degree providers share the regulatory and enrollment cycle driver.

themes.name: Cruise Line & Ocean Travel Recovery
themes.description: Global cruise operators are benefiting from continued pent-up demand for experiential travel, record booking volumes, and improving yield-per-passenger as pricing power returns. LIND (luxury marine expedition cruises), RCL (premium mass-market cruise operator), and NCLH (Norwegian Cruise Line) span the experiential-to-premium cruise spectrum and are all seeing sustained RS improvement as consumer spending on travel remains resilient.

themes.name: Hospital & Behavioral Health Facility Procedure Volume Recovery
themes.description: U.S. hospital operators and their key device suppliers are recovering as procedure volumes normalize post-pandemic deferral backlog and labor costs stabilize. HCA and UHS (behavioral health) are facility operators directly leveraged to admission and procedure counts, while BSX (interventional cardiology devices) and THC (hospital systems) are tightly coupled to in-hospital procedure volume. Rate-sensitive capex and staffing cost relief provide a second tailwind.

themes.name: Regulated Gas & Electric Distribution Utilities
themes.description: Small and mid-cap regulated gas and electric distribution utilities (serving state-regulated service territories) are moving in a tight statistical cluster, likely reflecting a rotation into rate-sensitive, dividend-paying utilities as interest rate expectations shift. AVA (Avista), BKH (Black Hills), NJR (New Jersey Resources), NWE (Northwestern Energy), POR (Portland General), and SR (Spire) are all pure-play regulated distribution utilities with limited merchant exposure, making them highly sensitive to the same rate and regulatory catalysts.

themes.name: B2B Digital Financial Infrastructure & Payment Rails Modernization
themes.description: PAY (PayPal), QTWO (Q2 Holdings), and ACIW (ACI Worldwide) are all moving higher primarily on sector-wide strength in digital payments and fintech ahead of a heavy earnings week, with investors positioning for continued growth in electronic payments and digital banking demand. For QTWO specifically, the move is being supported by growing interest in its digital banking and fraud/AI solutions as banks accelerate digital transformation, which is seen as a driver of subscription revenue and platform adoption. ACIW’s bid is helped by recent positive developments in instant payments (Wero/EPI integrations, Rabobank partnership) and institutional accumulation, reinforcing the long-term real-time payments and open banking growth narrative.

themes.name: U.S. Petroleum Refining & Downstream Processing
themes.description: Refining stocks are being driven higher by very strong crack spreads and refining margins, helped by tight global product supply and persistent geopolitical disruptions to refining capacity. Recent analyst actions have reinforced the theme: Raymond James highlighted mid-cap refiners DK, DINO and PARR as direct beneficiaries of record WTI 3‑2‑1 crack spreads, while Mizuho upgraded PSX and raised targets on PARR on improving refining operations and above-consensus Q2 earnings expectations. Index inclusion and ongoing analyst optimism around earnings and capital returns are adding incremental support for larger names like MPC and PSX.

themes.name: Inflammatory Disease & Immunology Biologics
themes.description: SYRE ORKA’s strength this week is primarily a continuation of the momentum from its recent positive Phase 2a psoriasis data for lead asset ORKA-001, which triggered major price target hikes and “strong buy” ratings in late April and established a high-conviction growth narrative. Investor focus remains on the favorable efficacy profile in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis and the expanded upside embedded in updated analyst targets, rather than any new discrete catalyst in the past few days. In short, the current move is an extension of the prior clinical-trial-driven rerating rather than a fresh news event.

themes.name: Hotel REIT Recovery & Re-Rating
themes.description: RLJ and XHR are moving higher on sector-specific and company-specific lodging REIT catalysts rather than a single headline event. RLJ is benefiting from continued strength and relative outperformance in hotel REITs over the past month, with the stock up roughly mid‑single digits in the last four weeks and over 60% year-on-year, as investors rotate into higher-beta real estate and travel plays. XHR’s bid is being supported by anticipation around its upcoming Q2 earnings release and dividend news flow, following solid prior quarters and the scheduled Q2 2026 earnings call timing, which is drawing incremental interest into the name.

themes.name: Uniform Rental & Managed Workwear Services
themes.description: CTAS is being driven higher by a strong post-earnings reaction: the company reported robust Q4 and full-year results with higher sales, revenue, and net income, plus raised guidance for fiscal 2027, which the market is now pricing in more fully. In addition, Cintas has been in focus due to its UniFirst acquisition bid and a recent 8-K on results of operations, both reinforcing the growth and consolidation narrative around the name. I do not see a discrete, stock-specific news catalyst of similar magnitude for VST this week; its move appears more like a continuation of the recent uptrend tied to broader market and utility/power demand dynamics rather than a fresh headline.

themes.name: Containerboard & Corrugated Packaging Producers
themes.description: IP and PKG are trading higher on the back of improving containerboard pricing and investor optimism around cost-cutting and footprint optimization initiatives at International Paper, alongside recent price hikes and cost reductions at Packaging Corp of America that support stronger near-term earnings. Sector sentiment has been reinforced by reports that containerboard prices used for shipping boxes and packaging are rising, which boosted both IP and PKG sharply late last week and is still being repriced by the market this week. There is no single new headline today; the move is largely a continuation of the rerating on better pricing, margin recovery, and restructuring narratives ahead of upcoming earnings.

themes.name: Casual Dining Restaurant Turnaround
themes.description: Brinker International (EAT) is trading higher this week mainly on continued momentum from early July media-driven enthusiasm, after Jim Cramer highlighted the name positively and called out upside in the story. That bullish commentary helped shift sentiment, and investors have been leaning into the casual dining recovery and EAT’s operating leverage as comps and traffic stabilize.

themes.name: SMB & Workforce Business Services Platforms
themes.description: NSP is being bid up mainly on follow‑through from its SHRM26 conference exposure, where Insperity spotlighted its HR360, HRCore and HRScale platforms, driving fresh interest in its technology offering and valuation upside narrative. LZ is moving higher on the back of its better‑than‑expected Q1 results and raised full‑year revenue outlook, supported by recent insider buying that reinforces a confidence signal.

themes.name: Cruise Line & Ocean Travel Recovery
themes.description: Global cruise operators are benefiting from continued pent-up demand for experiential travel, record booking volumes, and improving yield-per-passenger as pricing power returns. LIND (luxury marine expedition cruises), RCL (premium mass-market cruise operator), and NCLH (Norwegian Cruise Line) span the experiential-to-premium cruise spectrum and are all seeing sustained RS improvement as consumer spending on travel remains resilient.

themes.name: IT Distribution & Technology Services Providers
themes.description: EFOR is being driven higher primarily by Truist Securities’ upgrade of Everforth to Buy from Hold and the accompanying price target hike to $36 from $33. The firm also raised its Q2 revenue and EPS estimates, citing stronger expected growth in commercial consulting services, which is feeding bullish sentiment into this week’s trade. INGM’s move is more anticipatory, with positioning ahead of its upcoming Q2 earnings release and recent recognition/partnership wins rather than a single fresh headline catalyst.

themes.name: Enterprise HR & Workforce Management SaaS
themes.description: WDAY is being driven higher by a rebound bid into large-cap software on the back of strong recent earnings, AI-related optimism, and multiple bullish pieces of research calling it undervalued and highlighting margin/AI momentum. PCTY is moving with the broader HCM/software complex, helped by positive commentary around product expansion, broker channel strength, and its efforts to deepen its HCM moat (including embedded retirement plans). ALIT’s strength is tied to company-specific news flow around cost-saving validation for its Healthcare Navigation offering, governance/leadership changes, and positioning ahead of its reverse split, all contributing to a re-rating in a thinly traded small-cap name.

themes.name: Corporate Spend, Expense Management & Financial Operations Software
themes.description: WEX’s move higher is being driven mainly by its strong Q2 2026 earnings beat and raised full-year guidance, with management citing the benefit of higher fuel prices in Mobility. Morgan Stanley also lifted its price target on WEX, pointing to near-term upside from recent fuel strength.

themes.name: Enterprise Server, Storage & Data Infrastructure Hardware
themes.description: The main catalyst this week is Super Micro Computer’s blowout preliminary Q4 update, showing AI server gross margins roughly doubling prior guidance and a record ~$60B order backlog, which has re-rated the entire AI infrastructure complex and driven read-through buying in HPE, DELL, and broader server/storage peers. That sector-wide AI hardware optimism is being reinforced by Dell’s own strong AI server outlook and recent bullish analyst target hikes, keeping DELL particularly bid and pulling HPE along. STX and NTAP are moving largely on sympathy as investors rotate into data-center and storage names leveraged to the same AI infrastructure spend theme.

themes.name: Domestic Steel Producers
themes.description: The main catalyst pushing STLD and NUE higher this week is the continued rebound in U.S. steel prices, with benchmark hot-rolled coil moving back toward roughly $1,200/ton on tight supply, mill price hikes, extended lead times, and tariff-reduced imports. In addition, STLD is getting a direct boost from its stronger-than-expected Q2 earnings print with record shipments and elevated realized prices, while NUE is being bid up into its upcoming Q2 earnings on guidance that reflects the same steel price strength. Broader optimism around domestic demand, infrastructure and reshoring, plus recent analyst target increases on the group, are reinforcing the move.

themes.name: Online Insurance Comparison & Digital Marketplace Platforms
themes.description: The move in EVER MAX this week is being driven by the Meta partnership announcement with Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions, under which Meta will support roughly 837–900 MW of new solar and wind capacity in India and purchase all green attributes from these projects. That deal has pushed Clean Max shares to an all-time high and triggered a multi-session rally of roughly 25%, drawing momentum and thematic interest into the broader “Ever/Clean Max” complex.

themes.name: Cloud Supply Chain & Warehouse Management Software
themes.description: MANH is being driven higher by a strong Q2 earnings beat and a raised 2025 outlook, which triggered a sharp rerating in the name. SPSC is moving on strategic news: the company announced an agreement to sell its 3P Revenue Recovery business and hired Morgan Stanley to explore a broader sale amid activist pressure, boosting takeover/speculation premium.

themes.name: Professional Advisory & Business Services
themes.description: The main catalyst appears to be continued momentum from CRA International’s Q1 2026 results, which showed record revenue and came with recent positive commentary around the business. For CBIZ (CBZ), I do not see a matching company-specific catalyst in the provided results, so the move higher this week may be more sector- or market-driven than news-driven.

themes.name: Cross-Border & International Payments Processing
themes.description: The move in EEFT and GPN this week is being driven mainly by a sector-wide bid into payments/fintech ahead of their upcoming Q2 earnings, with expectations for solid volume and margin prints as travel and consumer spending remain resilient. Global Payments has a specific near-term catalyst in its August 5 Q2 release and recent supportive analyst commentary and buy ratings, which is lifting the group. Euronet tends to trade as a high-beta peer and is catching a sympathy move as investors rotate into under-owned, reasonably valued payment processors.

themes.name: Digital Payments Processing & Merchant Acquiring Networks
themes.description: PYPL is moving higher this week primarily on a stronger-than-expected Q2 earnings print and raised full-year profit outlook, which reinforced confidence in the ongoing turnaround and margin improvement story. In the background, the stock is still benefiting from the reset in sentiment and perceived valuation floor created by the recent $60.50-per-share takeover offer from Stripe and Advent, along with related analyst upgrades. Together, better fundamentals plus lingering M&A optionality are driving the bid in the name.

themes.name: Smart Home Security & Comfort Systems
themes.description: ALRM’s move appears tied to renewed attention after being added to several Russell value and small-cap indices in late June, which can trigger index-fund buying. For REZI, the main catalyst this week is Resideo’s planned ADI spin-off and the related senior-notes financing/escrow update, which the market is treating as a transaction-driven catalyst.

themes.name: Office REIT Recovery & Re-Rating
themes.description: The main catalyst pushing SLG, BXP, HIW and CDP higher this week is renewed bullishness on U.S. office REITs driven by stronger leasing commentary and expectations that fundamentals are bottoming. SL Green has highlighted New York City office leasing as “the strongest I’ve seen in my career,” reinforcing the narrative of improving demand and de‑risking cash flows across the group. Positioning ahead of Q2 earnings for the office REIT complex is also contributing as investors rotate into higher‑beta real estate names.

themes.name: Life Science Tools & Analytical Instruments
themes.description: TMO is being lifted mainly by its strong Q2 earnings beat and raised full-year guidance, which also triggered a wave of analyst price-target upgrades. WAT’s move is more likely tied to product/diagnostic news flow, but there is no clear unusual-volume catalyst in the results you provided.

themes.name: Medical Device Mean-Reversion & Rotation Recovery
themes.description: INSP is being driven by new positive clinical data from the SLEEP 2026 meeting and publication of the PREDICTOR/ADHERE studies showing strong efficacy and adherence for its hypoglossal nerve stimulation therapy, alongside an 8-K board change that has brought trader attention. TNDM is moving ahead of its upcoming earnings as investors position around the impact of its pay-as-you-go model shift in diabetes pumps. XRAY and CNMD are benefiting from recent management/CFO changes and product/clinical milestones that reinforce their strategic positioning in dental and minimally invasive surgery, respectively, drawing incremental institutional interest.

themes.name: AI-Powered Enterprise Analytics & Intelligent Workflow SaaS
themes.description: INTA is higher on fresh customer-deal news around Intapp DealCloud/Celeste wins, which the market is treating as validation of its AI-driven relationship-intelligence platform. AVPT is moving on positive AI-platform coverage and recent product/news flow, including AgentPulse Command Center and “agentic AI governance” updates. I don’t see a clear news catalyst in the provided results for AMPL, so its move may be stock-specific or tied to a separate headline not included here.

QIAGEN also had supportive headlines from analyst actions and product/portfolio expansion news, which may be reinforcing the move. For BLLN, I don’t see a clear company-specific catalyst in the results provided; the stock’s move looks more tied to general medical-lab sector sentiment than a fresh headline.

themes.name: Clinical-Stage Oncology Biotech

Enliven Therapeutics (ELVN) is moving higher on the back of recent positive Phase 1 ENABLE trial data in chronic myeloid leukemia, subsequent FDA-aligned development path, and multiple analyst price target hikes (including Goldman Sachs and H.C. Wainwright) following a large, successfully executed equity offering that strengthened the balance sheet.

themes.description: The main catalyst is a positive sector call: Zacks highlighted insurance brokers including Aon, Brown & Brown and Arthur J. Gallagher as beneficiaries of strong pricing, consolidation, and organic growth in the insurance brokerage industry, which is lifting sentiment across the group. In addition, AJG specifically is being supported by a continued stream of accretive specialty and wholesale brokerage acquisitions and AI/technology initiatives that reinforce its long‑term growth narrative. Analyst price-target increases and constructive earnings/revenue trends for AON and its peers are reinforcing the move higher this week.

themes.name: B2B Marketing Automation & Customer Engagement SaaS
themes.description: KVYO and HUBS are being driven mostly by product/AI and growth-related headlines, not a single major takeover-style event. For KVYO, the clearest catalyst is its AI push, including the launch of its AI Marketing Agent Composer and Customer Agent updates, which followed coverage framing the stock as up on AI-agent and CRM automation momentum. For HUBS, the recent lift is tied to positive product/integration news and sentiment around AI-driven expansion, including the Impartner native CRM sync and HubSpot’s revenue-hub launch.

themes.name: Department Store Retail Recovery
themes.description: KSS is being lifted mainly by company-specific turnaround news, especially Kohl’s appointment of a new chief operating officer and the market’s focus on its operational overhaul and balance-sheet/liquidity improvements. Recent coverage also points to the stock reacting to stronger quarterly results and a new brand partnership, while DDS appears to be moving with the same retail-turnaround sentiment rather than a separate sector-wide catalyst.

themes.name: Industrial Construction Execution & On-Site Supply Chain
themes.description: TPC is being driven higher by a string of large contract wins and balance sheet improvement, including the $651.8M Guam defense power infrastructure award and subsequent debt refinancing/redemption that are boosting backlog, earnings visibility, and perceived credit quality. SUNB’s move is largely sector-driven, benefiting from rotation into small-cap financials on post-holiday positioning and higher-rate resilience rather than a single stock-specific headline. DNOW and RYZ are gaining on corporate actions: DNOW from its completed combination with MRC Global that enhances scale and synergies, and RYZ from its completed merger with Olympic Steel plus a fresh 52-week high and expanded incentive plan that signal confidence and support momentum.
