PTGX strength is tied to its recent FDA approval and strong launch of Icotyde plus the NDA submission for rusfertide in polycythemia vera, reinforcing a multi‑asset value story. XERS and MBX appear to be moving largely on sector sentiment and speculative positioning rather than a single, clear company‑specific headline this week.

themes.name: U.S. Apparel & Lifestyle Brand Recovery
themes.description: VSXY is being driven higher by ongoing enthusiasm around Victoria’s Secret’s turnaround story: strong Q1 earnings, raised FY26 guidance, and persistent short-covering/ momentum following the recent proxy victory and operational improvements, with no new single headline this week but continued bullish coverage and product/newsflow (e.g., PINK launches) keeping buyers engaged. OXM’s strength appears more technical than fundamental this week, as the stock rebounds from prior weakness and benefits from a positive short-term setup and improving sentiment in discretionary/apparel names, rather than a specific fresh company-level news catalyst.

themes.name: Financial Compliance & Regulatory Reporting SaaS
themes.description: Workiva (WK) is trading higher this week primarily on continued momentum around its AI-powered GRC and reporting platform, which has been a recurring focus in recent company news and commentary. In a tape driven by AI-related earnings optimism and resilient U.S. equity sentiment, investors are rotating into software names with clear AI narratives and recurring revenue profiles, and WK is benefiting from that broader theme. There is no single discrete company-specific headline this week; the move is more about positioning into AI-levered governance, risk, and compliance software ahead of earnings in a supportive macro and tech tape.

themes.name: U.S. Passenger Airlines
themes.description: The main catalyst is a sharp drop in oil prices, which is boosting fuel-sensitive airline stocks across the board; Reuters-linked coverage says crude fell enough to lift UAL, DAL, SKYW and ALK, with additional support from optimism around U.S.-Iran peace talks lowering geopolitical risk. There’s also some company-specific support layered on top: United has earnings and route-expansion momentum, while Alaska has been helped by bullish outlook/analyst coverage and recent operational updates.

themes.name: Truckload & LTL Freight Carriers
themes.description: The move in HUBG, ARCB, SNDR, and TFII this week is mainly a sector trade: investors are rotating into truckload/intermodal names on expectations of a late‑cycle freight upturn, improving spot and contract pricing, and better operating leverage as volumes firm. Within that, HUBG also has stock‑specific momentum as it stabilizes after the accounting restatement/delinquency overhang, with short covering and “buy” technical signals helping fuel a rebound. Broader risk‑on sentiment and rate‑cut expectations are adding a tailwind to economically sensitive transport stocks as a group.

themes.name: Industrial Fluid Control, Filtration & Water Infrastructure Equipment
themes.description: IEX (Indian Energy Exchange) is being driven higher by strong Q1 FY27 results showing a ~12% YoY PAT increase and ~16% YoY growth in traded electricity volumes, supported by record summer power demand and higher exchange prices. For IDEX (IEX) in the US, the main near-term catalyst is its upcoming quarterly cash dividend, with the stock trading ex-dividend this month. For IR (Ingersoll Rand), FELE (Franklin Electric), and DCI (Donaldson), the move appears more rotational/sector-based with no single stock-specific news catalyst dominating this week.

themes.name: Global Crude & Product Tanker Fleet Operators
themes.description: The main driver is a sector-wide bid into crude and product tankers on renewed geopolitical and oil market risk, specifically headlines around potential disruption in/around the Strait of Hormuz and rising oil prices that tighten tanker supply and push spot rates higher. Individual positives like TRMD’s strong LR2 spot exposure and special dividend, DHT’s VLCC strength and newbuild orders, and broadly favorable media/analyst sentiment toward tanker names are reinforcing the move but are secondary to the macro/geopolitical shipping thesis.

themes.name: Network Security & Zero-Trust Edge
themes.description: The move is being driven by a broad bid into cybersecurity and data‑protection names on the back of accelerating AI‑related cyber risk and rising enterprise security spend, which is lifting the dedicated cyber ETFs and baskets these stocks sit in. Fortinet, CrowdStrike, Okta and peers are also seeing follow‑through from strong recent earnings/AI narratives plus incremental partnership/integration headlines (e.g., CVLT’s integrations with Microsoft Security, CrowdStrike and Okta, and FTNT’s Intel foundry/security collaboration), reinforcing the theme. Flows into sector baskets like the CRWD·FTNT·OKTA·TENB·RBRK group highlighted by traders are amplifying the move as investors rotate into high‑beta security plays.

themes.name: Senior & Long-Term Care Healthcare REITs
themes.description: The main catalyst is growing investor focus on the senior housing / healthcare REIT theme, supported by data showing U.S. senior housing occupancy approaching 90% with minimal new supply and several names (including OHI and VTR peers) breaking to 12‑month and even all‑time highs. This week’s move is largely a continuation of that structural-demand trade, with demographic tailwinds and perceived defensiveness driving inflows into long-term care and senior housing landlords. Index inclusion for VTR in Russell defensive/value indices and positive sentiment/target hikes around OHI are reinforcing the bid across the group.

themes.name: Open-Air & Strip Mall Retail REITs
themes.description: This week’s strength in KIM, UE, REG, PECO, KRG, and BRX is being driven primarily by a sector-wide bid into grocery-anchored and open-air shopping center REITs as investors rotate toward defensive, income-oriented real estate ahead of upcoming earnings and in the wake of Kroger’s Giant Eagle acquisition headlines. Kroger’s deal is reinforcing the durability and growth narrative for necessity-based retail, which benefits landlords with similar tenant mixes and footprint exposure. There is no single stock-specific catalyst for these names this week; the move is largely a thematic trade around necessity retail and REIT yield.

themes.name: Property & Casualty Insurance Underwriters
themes.description: For THG, the main recent company-specific catalyst is its inclusion in U.S. News & World Report’s 2026–2027 “Best Companies to Work For” list, which has coincided with the stock pushing to new 52-week highs and can support sentiment and valuation rerating in a quality-focused insurance tape. For AFG, the driver is ongoing positive follow-through from recent dividend, earnings, and conference-related news flow ahead of upcoming financial events, with investors positioning for capital return and steady fundamentals in the specialty insurance space. For WRB, ACGL, AXS, and ORI, the move is largely sector-driven: property & casualty and specialty insurers are benefiting from a constructive macro backdrop for underwriting margins and investment income, with no single dominant, stock-specific headline this week beyond that broader insurance rally.

themes.name: U.S. Regional & Mid-Cap Commercial Banks
themes.description: The likely catalyst is a regional-bank rebound after easing Treasury yields and a firmer rate-cut narrative, with traders also rotating into financials ahead of this week’s Fed-related data and minutes. EWBC has an added stock-specific boost from Barclays raising its price target to $150 from $142 while keeping Overweight. I don’t see a single company-specific catalyst tying all six names together, so this looks more like sector rotation than one shared headline.

themes.name: Industrial & Logistics REITs
themes.description: The move looks fundamentally driven by leasing and portfolio-growth headlines, especially TRNO’s recent lease announcements in Doral and other markets, plus a prior property acquisition update. I don’t see a distinct fresh company-specific catalyst for STAG, so the week’s strength likely reflects the broader industrial REIT bid and sector flow rather than one major new headline.

themes.name: European Bank Stocks
themes.description: The primary catalyst is strong European bank earnings and guidance, led by Banco Santander’s record H1 results and Q2 beats on net interest income and profit, plus a large ongoing share buyback that has lifted sentiment across the sector. In addition, a broader risk-on move into European and Latin American financials as oil prices ease and the dollar softens is supporting Spanish and UK banks, benefiting SAN, BBVA, NWG, LYG, BCS, and ING together. NatWest’s recently completed Evelyn Partners acquisition and upcoming H1 print are also helping underpin UK bank momentum.

themes.name: Cyber Exposure Management & Vulnerability Assessment
themes.description: RPD, TENB and QLYS are being driven higher by a combination of renewed rotation into cybersecurity/software as an AI-adjacent “safe” growth theme and name-specific positives. For Tenable, fresh news that it is expanding Tenable One to include application security data, plus recent target hikes and upgrades highlighting its positioning around AI-driven vulnerabilities, is adding incremental upside. Qualys is benefiting from bullish analyst moves (notably Scotiabank’s upgrade to Outperform and a prior JPMorgan upgrade) and the halo from stronger vulnerability-management and platform narratives that are lifting the whole group, including Rapid7.

themes.name: Cloud Data Storage & Analytics Infrastructure
themes.description: BLZE is being driven higher primarily by the recently announced five-year, multi‑exabyte AI cloud storage agreement with CoreWeave valued at $335 million, which investors and analysts are treating as a game‑changing validation of Backblaze’s role in AI infrastructure. The deal has sparked substantial analyst upgrades and higher price targets, reframing the company as an emerging AI cloud/GenAI storage contender and supporting a re‑rating of the stock. Broader enthusiasm around accelerating AI storage demand and Backblaze’s B2 cloud growth is reinforcing the move.

themes.name: Specialty Insurance Underwriting & Brokerage
themes.description: PLMR is higher this week mainly on post-earnings momentum: Palomar’s Q1 2026 results beat estimates, with EPS and revenue both topping expectations and revenue up sharply year over year. For RYAN, the move is more likely tied to stock-specific news around Ryan Specialty, not Palomar; if you meant RYAN, recent coverage points to institutional accumulation and a generally solid Q1 backdrop rather than a single headline catalyst.

themes.name: Global Steel & Metal Producers Recovery
themes.description: The main near-term catalyst is positive analyst and insider-related news: BNP Paribas upgraded Commercial Metals to Outperform and raised its price target to $75 on July 8, and Smart Insider highlighted CMC as “Pick of the Week” on July 22 following a CEO share purchase. These have reinforced the broader Buy consensus and attracted incremental institutional and retail interest, supporting the stock’s move higher this week.

themes.name: Copper Mining & Production
themes.description: The main catalyst is a broad rebound in copper prices and renewed optimism on global industrial demand, which is lifting copper miners as high-beta proxies for the metal. For SCCO specifically, the move is being amplified by expectations of stronger upcoming earnings and margin expansion at higher realized copper prices, alongside supportive analyst commentary and index-related flows. TGB and FCX are being carried by the same macro copper theme: tight supply, electrification/AI-related demand narratives, and positioning ahead of copper-sensitive economic data and earnings.

themes.name: Commercial Real Estate Brokerage & Advisory Services
themes.description: The main catalyst pushing CBRE, NMRK, and JLL higher is renewed optimism around the commercial real estate operations cycle, driven by stronger leasing and capital markets activity, plus growing outsourcing demand that supports more recurring, fee-based revenue. Recent Q1 2026 results and guidance from CBRE and JLL highlighted double‑digit revenue growth, EPS beats, and raised or reinforced 2026 outlooks, while analysts have been emphasizing EPS growth in the high‑teens for both CBRE and Newmark and recommending the group as a way to play the sector’s rebound. The market is effectively repricing these names as beneficiaries of CRE recovery, data-center/AI-related infrastructure demand, and corporate outsourcing trends, rather than cyclical office-only proxies.

themes.name: Independent Power Producers & Nuclear Generation
themes.description: VST (diversified power generation with a large nuclear fleet), TLN (wholesale electricity generation), and CEG (pure-play nuclear generation via Constellation) are all leveraged to surging U.S. power demand driven by data center electrification and AI infrastructure build-out. The catalyst is structural: utilities cannot build fast enough, putting IPPs and nuclear operators in a strong pricing position in deregulated wholesale markets. This is a distinct sub-theme from traditional utilities — these companies sell into merchant markets, not regulated rate cases.

themes.name: Hospital & Behavioral Health Facility Procedure Volume Recovery
themes.description: U.S. hospital operators and their key device suppliers are recovering as procedure volumes normalize post-pandemic deferral backlog and labor costs stabilize. HCA and UHS (behavioral health) are facility operators directly leveraged to admission and procedure counts, while BSX (interventional cardiology devices) and THC (hospital systems) are tightly coupled to in-hospital procedure volume. Rate-sensitive capex and staffing cost relief provide a second tailwind.

themes.name: Targeted Protein Degradation Oncology
themes.description: The main catalyst is renewed enthusiasm around targeted protein degradation and “molecular glue” degraders following Kymera’s accelerated timeline and strong momentum, which is lifting the broader degradation space and spilling over into Monte Rosa (GLUE). In GLUE specifically, investors are reacting to recent AACR data on its Cyclin E1‑directed molecular glue degrader for CCNE1‑amplified solid tumors and looking ahead to the expected IND submission for MRT‑55811 later in 2026. Together, those clinical and regulatory milestones are driving incremental speculative interest and bid in the stock this week.

themes.name: Automotive Components & Tire Suppliers
themes.description: Goodyear (GT) is being supported this week by its upcoming index change, moving from the S&P MidCap 400 to the S&P SmallCap 600 effective before trading on July 6, 2026, which typically drives incremental demand from index and small-cap managers. Adient (ADNT) is trading higher on the back of its recent Q2 FY26 earnings beat and raised 2026 guidance, with stronger-than-expected EPS, slight revenue beat, and ongoing share repurchases reinforcing the bullish narrative despite margin and regional demand concerns.

themes.name: Custom AI Silicon & Chip Architecture Licensing
themes.description: ARM, ALAB, CRDO, and MRVL are all being pulled higher by the same macro theme: renewed risk-on flows into AI and high-speed connectivity semis as investors rotate back into AI infrastructure after a recent pullback, with strong data-center demand and optical/interconnect growth the core narrative. For MRVL specifically, the move is reinforced by bullish analyst calls and target hikes tied to its AI data center and optical interconnect exposure, plus ongoing enthusiasm around its Nvidia/AI custom silicon positioning. CRDO and ALAB are benefiting from the same AI connectivity thesis and positive analyst sentiment, with CRDO supported by very strong growth guidance and ALAB by recent target hikes highlighting CXL upside.

themes.name: Traditional Staffing & Talent Placement Services
themes.description: MAN RHI is higher this week mainly on the leadership rejig after the company announced the resignations of its Managing Director and CEO, which traders appear to be treating as the main catalyst. There is also support from the recent JV approval with Khemka Refractories, but the stock’s sharp move has been tied more directly to the management change.

themes.name: Powersports & Recreational Vehicle Manufacturers
themes.description: Harley-Davidson (HOG) is being driven higher mainly by a bullish analyst shift and earnings setup: Loop Capital upgraded the stock to Buy with a higher $32 target, and investors are positioning ahead of its Q2 print and a new financing partnership for HDFS. Polaris (PII) is moving on Bank of America’s positive earnings preview, with estimates held near the high end of full-year guidance and expectations for solid upcoming results for the powersports group.

themes.name: Semiconductor Wafer Foundry & Advanced IC Manufacturing
themes.description: AMAT, ICHR, and TSEM are all being lifted by the same macro catalyst: renewed optimism around AI-driven semiconductor and capex spending, highlighted by TSMC’s announced chip price increases and its $100 billion Arizona expansion, which point to structurally higher demand for wafer fab equipment and related subsystems. For AMAT specifically, the move has been reinforced by bullish sell-side target hikes, strong recent earnings and guidance, and commentary from management and peers (Micron, Qualcomm, Meta) that underscore long runway in AI infrastructure and advanced packaging tools. TSEM has an additional idiosyncratic boost from its recent AI photonics deal and IP settlement, which has sharpened the market’s focus on its role in silicon photonics and specialty foundry capacity.

themes.name: Analog & Microcontroller Semiconductors — Automotive & Industrial Cycle Recovery
themes.description: The primary catalyst is a broad-based upturn in analog and embedded semiconductor demand, especially in industrial, automotive, and data center markets, which is driving estimate revisions and a sector-wide re-rating across ADI, MCHP, NXPI, ON, and TXN. Texas Instruments’ role as an analog bellwether, coupled with multiple analyst price target and estimate hikes ahead of its Q2 earnings, is reinforcing the view that the cyclical trough is over and that the recovery in these end-markets is sustainable. This analog/industrial recovery is being layered on top of accelerating AI data center infrastructure demand, providing a powerful combination of cyclical and structural growth drivers for the group.

themes.name: Defense Prime Contractors & Aerospace Systems
themes.description: The primary catalyst is a very strong Q2 earnings season for the defense primes, with Lockheed Martin and RTX both posting beat-and-raise quarters, record backlogs, and raised 2026 guidance tied to sustained global rearmament and Pentagon restocking of missiles and munitions. LMT and RTX’s moves are spilling over into the group, helping LHX and HII as investors rotate back into defense on the combination of robust order books, missile and space contract wins, and renewed focus on air and missile defense capabilities. A supportive macro backdrop of ongoing geopolitical tensions and U.S. defense budget visibility is reinforcing the bid across these names.

themes.name: Multifamily Apartment REITs
themes.description: The main catalyst this week is a supportive macro backdrop for rate‑sensitive REITs as inflation expectations and long rates have eased, improving the outlook for apartment REIT cash flows and valuations. On the name-specific side, UDR is benefiting from recent bullish sell-side actions (Wells Fargo price target increase and Deutsche Bank upgrade to Buy with a higher target), which reinforce the broader bid into residential REITs. The rest of the group (CPT, MAA, IRT, UDR) is moving largely on sector rotation rather than stock-specific headlines.

themes.name: For-Profit Education & Career Training Providers
themes.description: Workforce retraining demand from displaced workers and the ongoing push for vocational and career-focused education credentials are creating tailwinds for for-profit education operators. The correlation cluster (CVSA, LINC, PRDO, STRA) alongside existing theme members suggests broader sector-level accumulation. Community college alternatives and online degree providers share the regulatory and enrollment cycle driver.

themes.name: Cloud Observability & AIOps Monitoring Platforms
themes.description: DT, PD, and DDOG are all benefiting from a renewed bid into observability/monitoring and incident-response names tied to AI infrastructure spend and cloud security, with Datadog in particular seeing momentum from strong Q1 results, rising revenue/EPS estimates, and aggressive AI product launches like Bits AI and GPU/LLM observability. The group is also catching support from recent analyst price target hikes and “Leader” recognition in observability, which reinforce the AI-driven growth narrative and institutional interest in the space. In the absence of stock-specific headlines this week for DT and PD, the move is largely a sympathy trade to DDOG’s AI/observability strength and positioning ahead of the next earnings prints.

themes.name: U.S. Apparel & Fashion Recovery
themes.description: RVLV is being bid up on optimism around its upcoming earnings, with sell-side previews highlighting improving digital engagement, AI-driven personalization, and margin expansion as key drivers for better growth and profitability. CROX is rallying on strong post-earnings sentiment, multiple price target hikes (Needham, Williams Trading, Stifel, BoA) and confidence in North America DTC strength, Hey Dude’s second-half recovery, and potential buybacks. UA is moving with the broader footwear/apparel complex on sector rotation into consumer discretionary and positive sentiment around demand and capital allocation, even without a single dominant company-specific headline this week.

themes.name: Life Insurance & Annuity Providers
themes.description: PFG, PRU, and MET are being pulled higher mainly by sector-wide tailwinds: stable-to-elevated rates, strong equity markets, and ongoing optimism around life/retirement product profitability, which support spreads and asset-based fees across life insurers. Company-specific near-term catalysts are also in focus, particularly upcoming Q2 earnings for PFG and PRU, where investors expect confirmation of solid earnings momentum and capital return, alongside recent positive/raised price targets and prior earnings beats and dividend hikes (notably at MET and PFG). Broadly constructive risk sentiment in U.S. equities is adding beta support to high-quality financials, amplifying these stock-specific drivers.

themes.name: Defense Precision Components & Mission-Critical Subsystems
themes.description: Hexcel (HXL) is being bid up on aerospace optimism following its long-term composite materials partnership with Deutsche Aircraft for the D328eco regional turboprop, which has refocused investors on secular demand from next-gen commercial and defense platforms. Frequency Electronics (FEIM) is moving higher on the back of its July 23 announcement of approximately $18 million in new satellite contract awards, plus attention around its recent Q4 earnings call and contract win headlines.

themes.name: Consumer Fintech & Digital Credit Platforms
themes.description: Sezzle (SEZL) is being driven higher by a combination of strong growth fundamentals and capital return: recent reports highlight rapid revenue and EPS growth, attractive valuation metrics, and a new or expanded stock repurchase authorization that signals management’s confidence in the business. For Dave (DAVE), the main recent catalyst has been a shareholder vote tied to corporate actions, with the stock continuing to trade within its high-volatility uptrend supported by strong multi‑year revenue and margin expansion rather than a specific fresh news event this week.

themes.name: Private Mortgage Insurance
themes.description: The move is mostly a sector/rates trade in mortgage insurers, with no single company-specific headline clearly explaining all four names. The closest identifiable catalysts are Radian (RDN) hitting a 52-week high on strong recent earnings/continued positive earnings-surprise momentum and Essent (ESNT) benefiting from Moody’s rating upgrades/stable outlook, while NMIH appears to be drifting higher ahead of its July 30 earnings release and MTG’s usual drivers are earnings, portfolio stats, reinsurance, dividends and buybacks.

themes.name: Bitcoin Mining & Crypto Infrastructure Operators
themes.description: CIFR is moving higher mostly on a sector sympathy rally, not company-specific news, after Hut 8 landed a second $9.8 billion AI data-center lease and IREN raised its AI/cloud revenue outlook. That reinforced the market’s view that bitcoin miners pivoting into AI infrastructure can monetize their power and data-center assets. Cipher also got a lift from bargain-hunting and positioning ahead of its Q2 earnings.

themes.name: Franchise Auto Dealership Groups
themes.description: ABG, SAH, and PAG are all moving higher on the back of the Penske Automotive Group (PAG) take‑private proposal at $210/share in cash from Penske Corporation and Mitsui, which is repricing the entire auto dealer group on M&A/value-unlock read‑through. In PAG specifically, the non‑binding buyout offer and related arbitrage/setup dynamics are the direct catalyst, while peers like ABG and SAH are catching a sympathy bid as investors reassess private-market and strategic value across the franchise dealer space.

themes.name: Specialty Pharma — Rare Disease & Cardiopulmonary Therapeutics
themes.description: KNSA is moving higher on a combination of strong year-to-date performance, recent estimate revisions that show rising 2026–2027 EPS expectations, and momentum-focused coverage highlighting its positive price trend. LQDA is being driven by bullish fundamental and technical setups, recent inclusion in the S&P SmallCap 600 index, and ongoing positive sentiment around its YUTREPIA franchise and growth vs. patent-risk narrative. Overall, this week’s strength in both names is primarily a continuation of momentum fueled by upward earnings revisions and index/visibility catalysts rather than a single discrete news event.

themes.name: Asset Management & Fund Administration Platform Ecosystem
themes.description: BX is trading higher on renewed enthusiasm around alternative asset managers’ fee-related earnings leverage and capital deployment after a strong earnings season read-through from peers, plus support from the broader rebound in risk assets. SSNC is being driven by its record Q2 print with a clean beat on revenue and EPS, raised full‑year guidance, and its largest‑ever quarterly buyback, which together triggered the sharp repricing higher.

themes.name: Wealth Management & Retail Brokerage Platforms
themes.description: The primary catalyst this week is stronger-than-expected earnings and asset-growth prints across the wealth/online brokerage complex, led by Raymond James and Charles Schwab, which are lifting the group on read‑through to AUM, fee income, and trading activity. RJF reported record Q3 net revenues and an earnings beat, while SCHW posted record Q2 revenue and EPS above expectations, reinforcing the bullish narrative for retail investing, advisory, and platform businesses that benefits SEIC, SF, HOOD, AMP and peers. Sector sentiment is further aided by Schwab’s ongoing expansion in digital assets/crypto and continued analyst confidence, which supports higher multiples across brokerage and asset‑management names.

themes.name: Canadian Big Banks
themes.description: The main catalyst pushing RY, TD, BNS, BMO and CM higher this week is positive read-through from strong Q2 U.S. bank earnings, especially in capital markets, lending and credit quality, which Scotiabank and RBC analysts highlight as supportive for the large Canadian banks’ near‑term earnings outlook. In particular, strength in capital markets and U.S. commercial lending is seen as especially beneficial for BMO, TD and RY, improving sentiment toward the group as a whole. This is occurring against a backdrop of already solid capital positions and sector momentum, so the U.S. results are reinforcing an existing constructive view rather than reversing a negative trend.

themes.name: Korean Financial Sector Recovery
themes.description: Shinhan Financial Group (SHG) is moving higher this week primarily on the back of its FY2025 profit growth and technical breakout above the 200-day moving average, which has attracted momentum and value investors. Recent disclosures around its 2026 value-up plan, higher payout intentions, and strategic moves such as weighing a Lotte Insurance acquisition are reinforcing the rerating trend in Korean financials. Sector-wide strength in South Korean banks and improving net interest income dynamics are adding a supportive macro tailwind to the move.

themes.name: Coastal & Suburban Residential Rental REITs
themes.description: The move appears tied to a fresh analyst re-rating of the single-family rental group, led by Barclays lifting AMH’s price target, which is supporting sentiment across residential REITs. INVH and the apartment names EQR and ESS are likely trading higher in sympathy on the same sector rotation rather than on company-specific news.
