themes.name: Consumer Staples Packaged Food & Snack Brand Recovery
themes.description: After years of underperformance, packaged food and snack companies are staging a powerful rotation with LW, UTZ, and CAG all turning from multi-month lows (RS as low as 23-27) to RS 74-97 over a sustained 4-week streak. The catalyst appears to be easing input cost pressures, volume stabilization after years of price-driven trade-down, and renewed consumer spending on branded staples. This is a classic defensive rotation with offensive price action.

themes.name: Industrial Automation & Electrical Control Systems
themes.description: AME’s move looks tied to renewed investor focus on industrial automation and margins/free cash flow, not a single fresh headline catalyst. HLIO is being helped by recent positive company news, especially its first-quarter results that beat outlook and showed 17% sales growth, plus newer product/market expansion updates. ROK appears to be moving on company-specific wins like the Aalo Atomics control-systems selection and broader optimism around factory upgrades and industrial automation.

themes.name: Precious Metals Miners & Royalty Streamers
themes.description: The primary catalyst is a sharp move higher in spot gold prices, which has lifted the entire gold-mining complex. Rising bullion, driven by geopolitical tensions around the U.S.–Iran situation and its implications for inflation and Fed policy, is pushing NEM, KGC, AU, GFI, HMY and AGI higher in tandem. There does not appear to be a single, stock-specific news item this week; the move is largely macro and commodity-price driven.

themes.name: Precious Metals Royalty & Streaming Companies
themes.description: The primary driver for Franco-Nevada (FNV), Royal Gold (RGLD), and Wheaton Precious Metals (WPM) this week is macro: firmer gold prices on softer Fed rate expectations and a weaker dollar, which is lifting gold-linked royalty/streaming names leveraged to the metal. Company-specific news flow for FNV has been relatively quiet and mixed (Burkina Faso stream dispute, Cobre Panamá stockpile processing approvals, record prior-quarter results), so the move is largely a sector-wide precious metals and royalty trade rather than a single headline catalyst. Earnings estimate upgrades and optimistic analyst targets for FNV add incremental support but are secondary to the gold-price and rates backdrop.

themes.name: Traditional Staffing & Talent Placement Services
themes.description: Robert Half (RHI) is moving higher this week primarily on the back of a significant analyst price target hike and reiterated Buy rating, which triggered a sharp rerating in the shares. Multiple outlets note the stock has climbed more than 20–25% week-over-week after this upgrade and related bullish commentary highlighting it as a “Bull of the Day” and a cyclical recovery play.

themes.name: Casual Dining & Full-Service Restaurant Chain Recovery
themes.description: The move in CAKE is being driven by a strong Q2 earnings beat: adjusted EPS came in at $1.44 versus $1.18 expected, revenue hit $1.03B, and same-store sales rose 5.8%. Management also raised full-year revenue guidance to $4.0B, which is reinforcing the rally.

themes.name: Franchise Auto Dealership Groups
themes.description: SAH, ABG, and PAG are trading higher this week on a combination of sector-wide strength in auto retail and company-specific corporate activity/expectations. For PAG specifically, the key catalyst is the unsolicited, preliminary, non-binding offer from Penske Corporation and Mitsui to acquire the remaining shares at $210 per share in cash, along with follow-through from bullish technical momentum and capital-allocation actions like dividend increases. SAH and ABG are benefiting from read-across and M&A/spec takeout sentiment in the dealer group space as investors reassess valuations and consolidation potential.

themes.name: SMB & Workforce Business Services Platforms
themes.description: NSP is moving higher on a technical breakout after Insperity (NSP US) crossed above its 200-day moving average around $36.5 this week, which is drawing in momentum and trend-following flows. In addition, recent commentary that Insperity could be materially undervalued following the SHRM26 HR conference spotlight on its HR360/HRCore/HRScale platforms has supported a re-rating narrative among investors. There does not appear to be a single discrete fundamental news release this week, but rather a combination of these technical and valuation-driven catalysts.

themes.name: B2B Digital Financial Infrastructure & Payment Rails Modernization
themes.description: PAY is reacting to renewed crypto-payment sentiment and positive flow around Alchemy Pay’s expanding fiat/crypto on-ramp integrations, which has traders rotating back into niche payment rails. QTWO is being bid up ahead of its Q2 earnings report after the bell, with DA Davidson recently reiterating a Buy rating and higher full-year 2026 guidance and AI product (Q2 Assistant) underpinning sentiment. ACIW is moving higher on a series of strategic payment wins, notably its role in Europe’s Wero instant-payments initiative and broader EPI integration, which have strengthened the bull case around its global real-time payments footprint.

themes.name: Enterprise HR & Workforce Management SaaS
themes.description: PCTY is higher on Citigroup naming it a top pick in HR software ahead of earnings, while WDAY is rallying on pre-earnings positioning plus renewed AI/enterprise-software optimism. ALIT’s move appears more sector/tactical than company-specific based on the available tape, with no clear fresh catalyst visible in the results.

themes.name: Professional Advisory & Business Services
themes.description: CBIZ is trading higher this week primarily on its Q2 earnings beat, with adjusted diluted EPS of $0.91 versus the $0.72 consensus, which triggered a gap up in the stock. A secondary catalyst is the announced all-cash acquisition by Grant Thornton Advisors at $55 per share, which is anchoring near-term valuation and supporting the move higher. There is no fresh company-specific catalyst for CRA International yet, as its Q2 results are not scheduled to be reported until August 6.

themes.name: Cloud Supply Chain & Warehouse Management Software
themes.description: MANH is trading higher this week primarily on a strong Q2 earnings beat and a “beat-and-raise” guide, with revenue, EPS, and full-year 2026 guidance all coming in above Street expectations. Management highlighted a third consecutive record bookings quarter and accelerating cloud-driven growth, reinforcing confidence in future demand and margins. The move is being amplified by positive analyst reactions, including price target increases that are adding to the momentum bid in the stock.

themes.name: U.S. Petroleum Refining & Downstream Processing
themes.description: The group is moving higher on a sector-wide bid driven by elevated refining margins and crack spreads supported by tight global refining capacity, resilient fuel demand, and ongoing geopolitical disruptions in the Middle East and broader oil supply routes. Additional momentum is coming from bullish sentiment into Q2 earnings (especially for VLO and DINO), where the market expects strong margin realization and export demand to show up in the numbers. PARR also has a specific tailwind from recent analyst target increases tied to tight regional fuel markets and improved West Coast/Pacific Northwest margins, which reinforces the broader refining bull case.

themes.name: Corporate Spend, Expense Management & Financial Operations Software
themes.description: The move higher in WEX this week is being driven primarily by its setting a new 12‑month high on the back of strong recent fundamentals and momentum, which has attracted fresh “time to buy” commentary from equity research outlets. That follows a robust backdrop of record 2025 revenue and net income, Q1 2026 beats on EPS and revenue, and an active capital return story (large 2025 buybacks and a new US$1bn repurchase authorization announced in June), all of which are reinforcing the bull narrative. NAVN/BILL aren’t showing a discrete, stock‑specific headline this week; they are largely participating in the broader strength in payments/fintech and business services rather than trading off a single, new catalyst.

themes.name: Hotel REIT Recovery & Re-Rating
themes.description: RLJ and XHR are being bid up this week primarily on the back of a broad lodging/hotel REIT move tied to World Cup-driven strength in New York/New Jersey hotel fundamentals, with occupancy above 90% and ADR up roughly 38% year over year on match days. Strong RevPAR gains in host markets (game-day RevPAR up about 41% on average, with some markets up more than 100% year over year) are reinforcing the bullish narrative around urban, transient-focused hotel REITs, pulling the group to fresh 52-week highs.

themes.name: Digital Payments Processing & Merchant Acquiring Networks
themes.description: PYPL is trading higher this week primarily on its Q2 beat-and-raise: PayPal reported stronger-than-expected earnings and lifted full-year non-GAAP guidance, which drove a roughly 4% move up after the print. Earnings strength is being layered onto the existing takeover narrative from Stripe/Advent, with the CEO signaling openness to value-creating deals, keeping M&A speculation alive as an ongoing catalyst. For the FOUR ETF, the same fintech repricing theme around PayPal’s bid and solid results is contributing to a supportive backdrop for payments names.

themes.name: Office REIT Recovery & Re-Rating
themes.description: The move in the office REITs is being driven mainly by a constructive shift in sentiment toward high‑quality office landlords, supported by fresh leasing wins and valuation calls. For BXP specifically, Scotiabank’s recent upgrade to Outperform on the back of strong leasing momentum, plus multiple large lease announcements, has reinforced the “return‑to‑office” and occupancy-recovery narrative and highlighted the stock as undervalued. SLG, HIW and CDP are riding the same theme of improving fundamentals and renewed investor interest in trophy and Sunbelt office assets rather than any single company‑specific headline this week.

themes.name: Dermatology & Atopic Immunology Biologics
themes.description: FBRX is ripping on the definitive all‑cash takeover by argenx at $77 per share, a roughly 41% premium that crystallizes upside and effectively caps the stock near deal terms while it trades into the spread. The move is underpinned by recent positive Phase 1b data for FB102 in vitiligo and celiac disease, which argenx highlighted as the core rationale for the $2.2 billion acquisition. APGE’s strength is being driven by sustained follow‑through on earlier positive 52‑week Phase 2 data for APG777 in atopic dermatitis plus a successful $403 million equity raise, with added momentum from AbbVie’s subsequent cash buyout offer headlines keeping M&A premium expectations elevated.

themes.name: Uniform Rental & Managed Workwear Services
themes.description: CTAS is being driven higher by a clean earnings beat and upbeat forward guidance, followed by an upgrade from Bank of America to Buy with a higher price target, which is reinforcing the post-earnings momentum. For VSTS, the move is tied to ongoing rerating in the name after its recent spin/standalone listing, with improving fundamentals and investors rotating into outsourced facilities/uniform services as a more defensive, recurring-revenue play.

themes.name: AI-Powered Enterprise Analytics & Intelligent Workflow SaaS
themes.description: INTA is moving higher on follow‑through from its recent earnings beat and guidance raise, plus ongoing enthusiasm around its AI-enabled vertical SaaS positioning for professional services firms. AVPT is being driven by a strong AI narrative: recent earnings, new AI/agentic product initiatives, and research highlighting rapid enterprise AI adoption and governance needs are fueling demand for its data management and compliance platform. AMPL’s strength this week is tied to its latest earnings and upbeat outlook on demand for its digital optimization/experimentation platform, benefiting from the broader AI and data-driven marketing/software rerating.

themes.name: IT Distribution & Technology Services Providers
themes.description: INGM is moving higher mainly on an earnings-driven re‑rating: consensus estimates and “Most Accurate” estimates have been revised up, Zacks upgraded the name to Strong Buy, and the stock is benefiting from positive AI and cloud news (including an Oracle Cloud distribution program) that supports a higher fair value and targets. EFOR’s strength this week is tied to its recent 8‑K filing detailing a new material agreement and financial obligation plus upbeat company news flow, including government contract-related recognition and management share purchases, which together signal improved fundamentals and leadership confidence.

themes.name: Cross-Border & International Payments Processing
themes.description: EEFT and GPN are higher largely on a broad payment-processor rebound rather than a single company-specific headline, with both names showing modest gains this week. The clearest stock-specific catalyst in the results is GPN’s resumed coverage at Morgan Stanley with an Equal Weight rating and $65 target, while EEFT’s move appears more sentiment-driven.

themes.name: Containerboard & Corrugated Packaging Producers
themes.description: The main catalyst is a containerboard price hike: Packaging Corporation of America announced plans to raise prices by $140 per ton in September, and investors expect International Paper and Smurfit WestRock to follow. PKG also got a lift from strong Q2 results and a raised quarterly dividend, while SW has been riding the same sector-wide pricing momentum.

themes.name: Inflammatory Disease & Immunology Biologics
themes.description: SYRE/ORKA doesn’t appear to have a fresh, stock-specific news catalyst this week; the move looks like a continuation of the strong uptrend that began after the positive Phase 2 psoriasis data and major analyst target hikes in late April, plus ongoing “Strong Buy” ratings and very high institutional ownership. Recent scanners explicitly flag no unusual-volume or headline catalyst and suggest trading is in line with its established range, with the next clear event on the calendar being the August earnings report. In other words, price action is being driven more by momentum and positioning than by new fundamental news this week.

themes.name: Online Insurance Comparison & Digital Marketplace Platforms
themes.description: MAX EVER’s strength this week is being driven primarily by company-specific news: MediaAlpha (MAX) is rallying into its scheduled Q2 2026 earnings release, which is increasing speculation about improved profitability and a continued recovery in insurance customer acquisition spending. Separately, Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions (often tagged as MAX EVER/Max Ever in some feeds) recently hit an all-time high after announcing a major renewable energy partnership with Meta to build 837 MW of solar and wind capacity, with Meta buying all green attributes from these projects, which remains a key sentiment tailwind. Broadly supportive AI- and tech-led equity momentum is providing a constructive backdrop but is secondary to these direct catalysts.

themes.name: U.S. Apparel & Fashion Recovery
themes.description: The move in UA, RVLV, and CROX this week is primarily driven by a rotation back into consumer/retail discretionary on easing inflation and improving consumer-spending sentiment, which is lifting the broader athletic and specialty retail complex. Within that, CROX has an added catalyst from positive earnings momentum and a fresh Bank of America price target hike that is prompting a valuation re-rate, while RVLV is benefiting from recent favorable research/upgrade coverage highlighting margin expansion and AI-driven customer growth. Under Armour is catching sympathy flows as investors re-risk into branded athletic/lifestyle names ahead of the next earnings cycle.

themes.name: Life Insurance & Annuity Providers
themes.description: Met, Principal and Prudential are all trading higher on a combination of sector and stock-specific catalysts: investors are leaning into life insurers as “higher-for-longer” rates continue to support spreads and investment income, and the group is being highlighted positively in recent research coverage. On the name level, PFG is breaking out to a new 52-week high after another round of price-target hikes (most recently Bank of America to $104) on the back of strong Q1 earnings and margin expansion, while PRU and MET are benefiting from upcoming earnings visibility and incremental target raises from Mizuho and others alongside the favorable rate backdrop. Overall, the move is being driven more by reinforcement of the “rate tailwind + solid earnings/valuation” narrative than by any single company-specific headline this week.

themes.name: Cloud Observability & AIOps Monitoring Platforms
themes.description: DDOG is being driven higher this week by a cluster of bullish analyst actions, including multiple price target hikes (Morgan Stanley to 300, Citi to 300, Benchmark to 330, JMP to 311) tied to strong AI/cloud observability growth and momentum ahead of its August 6 earnings print. PD is benefiting from similar positioning in high-growth software tied to AI and observability, with investors rotating into the group on expectations that upcoming earnings and AI-related demand will support continued multiple expansion.

themes.name: Life Science Tools & Analytical Instruments
themes.description: Thermo Fisher (TMO) is moving higher mainly on its strong Q2 2026 earnings beat and raised full-year guidance, which reassured investors that life-science tools demand is improving. The stock is also getting an extra lift from analyst upgrades and bullish price-target hikes after the report.

themes.name: B2B Marketing Automation & Customer Engagement SaaS
themes.description: HubSpot (HUBS) is trading higher on renewed AI enthusiasm around its CRM and marketing automation platform, with investors rotating back into AI-enabled software following positive megacap AI sentiment. Klaviyo (KVYO) is being bid up on accelerating revenue growth, record operating margins, raised full-year guidance, and an expanded share buyback program, which collectively signal improving profitability and stronger management confidence. Broader AI sector strength and CRM automation headlines are reinforcing the move in both names.

themes.name: Financial Compliance & Regulatory Reporting SaaS
themes.description: DFIN is catching a bid on the back of a recent institutional buy disclosure from Fifth Third Bancorp, which increased its stake and highlighted DFIN’s better‑than‑expected earnings, strong recurring revenue profile, and Buy‑rated analyst backdrop. WK is moving higher on its own strong earnings print and bullish 2026 outlook that came out this week, which is driving follow‑through buying in cloud/compliance names. Together, the combination of positive fundamental news and supportive analyst sentiment is the key catalyst for both names.

themes.name: Wealth Management & Retail Brokerage Platforms
themes.description: The group is moving higher on a combination of strong recent/ongoing earnings prints and upward estimate/price-target revisions that reinforce the durability of wealth-management and brokerage fee/interest income in a stable-rate, risk-on equity tape. RJF is specifically reacting to record fiscal Q3 results and a wave of higher price targets, while LPLA, AMP and SEIC are bid ahead of or around earnings on expectations of advisory and asset-based fee growth and continued AUM gains. SCHW is additionally supported by rising trading activity (STAX at a four-year high) and optimism around new revenue levers like digital assets, which lifts the whole retail brokerage/RIAs complex.

themes.name: Insurance Brokerage & Distribution Services
themes.description: AJG, AON, and BRO are being driven higher primarily by a sector-wide bid into insurance brokers ahead of earnings, as investors rotate toward stable, fee-based financials in a volatile macro and rate backdrop. In addition, Brown & Brown’s strong Q1 print and AJG’s ongoing M&A-driven growth and price target hike from UBS have reinforced the bullish fundamental narrative across the group. AON’s upcoming earnings and positive industry commentary highlighting favorable pricing, underwriting, and consolidation in insurance brokerage are adding to the momentum.

themes.name: Medical Device Mean-Reversion & Rotation Recovery
themes.description: XRAY is being driven by optimism around its restructuring and capital deployment plan, including $120M in annualized cost savings and a shift toward debt reduction and share repurchases, which has supported a rebound after prior earnings-related volatility. CNMD is seeing interest ahead of its Q2 earnings report along with support from recent capital structure moves, notably the planned buyback of $645.2M of 2.25% convertible notes due 2027 and a new CFO appointment. INSP and TNDM are benefiting from the broader bid into medtech/medical device names, with TNDM additionally supported by recent regulatory and product milestones such as expanded EU indications and new sensor compatibility, which improve its long-term growth narrative.

themes.name: AI-Augmented Business Process Outsourcing & IT Services
themes.description: EXLS G’s move higher this week is being driven primarily by follow-through from its stronger-than-expected recent quarterly earnings, which showed double-digit revenue and EPS growth and came with a raised full-year outlook. Management increased guidance for both revenue and adjusted EPS, reinforcing the growth story and sustaining momentum in the stock after the initial post-earnings surge. There is no new single-day headline catalyst this week; it’s an extension of the positive earnings/guide and AI-focused strategic narrative already in place.

themes.name: Consumer Staples Packaged Food & Snack Brand Recovery
themes.description: LW is trading higher this week mainly on anticipation around its July 24th Q4/FY26 earnings release and Starboard Value’s activist involvement pushing for an Investor Day and a 25% EBITDA margin target by FY2029. There is also a defensive bid as investors focus on operational efficiency moves like the planned closure of the Broekhuizenvorst, Netherlands plant and cost-savings/capex discipline highlighted in recent results and guidance. CAG’s move higher is being driven by value and yield interest after the stock crossed a double‑digit dividend yield, alongside insider buying and a new CEO that is prompting a contrarian turnaround narrative despite recent negative sentiment and estimate cuts.

themes.name: Molecular Diagnostics & DNA-Based Genetic Testing
themes.description: QGEN is likely moving on a mix of recent corporate/news flow and positioning, especially Qiagen’s June 27 addition to the Russell 1000 Dynamic Index and the recent Goldman Sachs disclosure of a 3.65% voting interest. There’s also some support from recent analyst coverage/news such as Kepler’s Hold rating and the IngenuitySystems acquisition headline, but the Russell-index inclusion appears to be the clearest catalyst.

themes.name: Asset Management & Fund Administration Platform Ecosystem
themes.description: BX is moving higher on renewed interest in alternatives and strong fee-related earnings momentum, as investors rotate into large-cap private equity platforms that benefit from higher realizations and fundraising visibility. SS&C (SSNC) is being driven by its record Q2 print, double beat on revenue and EPS, raised full‑year 2026 guidance, and a record share buyback, which collectively triggered double‑digit upside and follow‑through buying. Incremental support is coming from positive sell-side reactions and growing investor focus on SS&C’s AI-driven automation and data platforms as margin and growth catalysts.

themes.name: Peptide & Hormone Therapies for Metabolic & Endocrine Disorders
themes.description: CORT is being driven by the FDA resubmission of its New Drug Application for relacorilant in Cushing’s syndrome, renewing expectations for an approval and incremental revenue. PTGX is rallying on positive sentiment and sell-side commentary following Johnson & Johnson’s recent FDA approval of its psoriasis drug that uses Protagonist’s peptide, which is seen as unlocking significant value for PTGX. For XERS and MBX, there is no specific stock‑specific news; the move appears more momentum/technical and sympathy-based within the biotech space rather than tied to a discrete catalyst.

themes.name: Smart Home Security & Comfort Systems
themes.description: Resideo (REZI) and Alarm.com (ALRM) have been moving higher primarily on company‑specific and structural catalysts rather than a single discrete headline this week. For REZI, the key drivers are the ongoing ADI spin-off process and related unsecured notes offering, plus accumulation by institutions such as Arrowstreet Capital and a still‑constructive Street view with upside to consensus targets. For ALRM, the move is largely sympathy and sector read‑through, as investors reposition into home security and smart‑home names that benefit from Resideo’s restructuring and improving sentiment in connected‑home/security peers.

themes.name: U.S. Domestic Steel Producers
themes.description: The move in STLD and NUE this week is being driven primarily by a continued rally in U.S. steel prices, with hot‑rolled coil rebounding toward roughly $1,200/ton on mill price hikes, longer lead times and tighter supply from outages and reduced imports under tariffs. That macro steel pricing backdrop is being reinforced by bullish analyst actions and earnings momentum at NUE (recent beats and upgrades on stronger steel pricing outlook) and ongoing strong flat‑rolled order activity at STLD. Together, those factors are feeding a sector‑wide bid into U.S. steel producers, lifting both names.

themes.name: Enterprise Server, Storage & Data Infrastructure Hardware
themes.description: The common driver is a renewed leg of the AI infrastructure/server trade, with upside read‑through from Super Micro’s record AI server orders and Dell’s own blowout AI server results and analyst target hikes, which are lifting the whole enterprise hardware complex. For DELL specifically, investors are chasing its AI server growth story after historic AI-optimized server revenue, strong guidance and fresh price target raises. For HPE and NTAP, the move is largely sympathy/sector rotation into AI data center, storage, and server names as investors extrapolate the same tight capacity and accelerating AI infrastructure demand theme.

themes.name: Investment Research & Financial Analytics Data Platforms
themes.description: The main driver this week is Morningstar’s continued AI-related product push and visibility, including recent commentary and tools around AI stock analysis and digital asset funds, which has reinforced the narrative that it can monetize data/analytics demand tied to the AI cycle. That thematic interest, combined with its positioning as a beneficiary of increased market volatility and fund-flows ahead of the Fed meeting and megacap earnings, is likely attracting incremental institutional buying rather than a single, discrete company-specific headline.

themes.name: Cruise Line & Ocean Travel Recovery
themes.description: NCLH and RCL are higher mainly on a broad cruise-sector rally after reports of a pause in U.S.-Iran hostilities pushed oil prices down, which eases fuel-cost pressure on cruise lines. NCLH is also getting an added lift from pre-earnings positioning ahead of its July 30 Q2 report, with investors looking for a potential beat and better cruise-demand commentary.

themes.name: Private Mortgage Insurance
themes.description: The common upside driver is a broad re-rating of U.S. mortgage insurers on expectations that still-strong credit performance, benign loss trends, and active capital return (buybacks/dividends) will support earnings and book-value growth even with muted origination volumes. In addition, M&A and diversification themes (e.g., Radian’s Inigo acquisition broadening earnings beyond U.S. MI) plus a pickup in positive news sentiment and valuation-focused research are pulling the group higher as investors rotate into discounted housing-credit names. Finally, positioning ahead of upcoming earnings (notably for NMIH) is adding a short-term bid as investors expect capital deployment and reserve/credit updates to reinforce the bullish narrative.

themes.name: Specialty Insurance Underwriting & Brokerage
themes.description: PLMR is moving higher on the back of raised 2026 adjusted net income guidance and a subsequent wave of positive commentary highlighting upside to earnings and price targets. RYAN is being supported by the recently expanded $600 million share repurchase authorization and disclosure of significant institutional buying (e.g., Fenimore Asset Management increasing its stake by over 80%), which together signal strong management and investor confidence.

themes.name: Clinical-Stage Oncology Biotech
themes.description: TGTX is trading higher on renewed optimism around its MS drug BRIUMVI, driven by fresh enthusiasm over the emerging subcutaneous formulation and broader expansion potential in autoimmune/neurologic indications, which has boosted sentiment on the franchise’s long‑term growth. In parallel, increasing biotech M&A chatter has put TG Therapeutics on lists of potential buyout candidates, adding a speculative premium to the stock. ELVN’s strength is being supported by recent positive Phase 1 ENABLE data for ELVN‑001 in CML, upward analyst target revisions, and follow‑through from its large, recently upsized equity offering that validated institutional interest in the story.

themes.name: Department Store Retail Recovery
themes.description: DDS is being driven by its recent massive Q1 earnings beat, bolstered by a one-time $104M litigation settlement that added over $5 per share to EPS and has analysts highlighting upside in the stock. For KSS, the move is largely tied to its ongoing turnaround narrative: a solid Q1 print in late May and, more recently, the appointment and expanded mandate of new COO Elliott Rodgers, which has prompted bullish commentary about operational improvements and undervaluation. Overall, both are benefiting from a bid into department stores/retail on improving fundamentals and restructuring stories rather than a single new headline this week.

themes.name: Tax Preparation & Consumer Financial Software Platforms
themes.description: INTU is moving higher this week primarily on follow-through from strong fiscal Q3 results and raised full-year revenue and earnings guidance, plus renewed focus on its longer-term growth story after a recent selloff. The launch of a new QuickBooks-integrated business credit card and expanded AI/strategic partnerships (including Anthropic and FedNow) are reinforcing the small-business ecosystem and improving sentiment. HRB’s move appears more modest, with the main recent catalyst being Stephens initiating coverage at Equal Weight with a $47 price target, which has put some incremental attention on the name.

themes.name: Cloud Data Storage & Analytics Infrastructure
themes.description: BLZE is being driven higher by the recently announced five-year, multi-exabyte AI cloud storage deal with CoreWeave valued at about $335 million, which materially changes the growth and revenue outlook for the company. Follow-on coverage has framed the CoreWeave agreement as a “game-changing” AI storage megadeal, triggering analyst upgrades and higher price targets, which is fueling momentum in the stock this week. SNOW’s move is being supported by a cluster of bullish sell-side actions (UBS, BTIG, Barclays, TD Cowen raising or reiterating buy/equal-weight ratings and higher targets) and ongoing positive narrative around its AI/data cloud positioning and large-scale AWS contract, sustaining investor appetite.

themes.name: Property & Casualty Insurance Underwriters
themes.description: The move looks most likely driven by a broad re-rating of the U.S. property & casualty insurance group rather than a company-specific event, with investors rotating into the sector’s large, high-quality underwriters. I do not see a single common announcement across WRB, TRV, ALL, ACGL, CB, and AFG in the provided material; WRB’s only company-specific item is an executive change, which would not explain the group-wide strength.

themes.name: Global Crude & Product Tanker Fleet Operators
themes.description: The main driver is a broad move higher in crude tanker rates and sentiment as spot earnings and time-charter equivalents have inflected up again, boosting cash flow expectations across the group. In addition, investors are rotating back into high-dividend shipping names after recent oil price volatility and macro data revived interest in energy and transport cyclicals. There is no single stock‑specific headline this week; it’s a sector-wide rate and yield trade lifting TNK, INSW, DHT, FRO, and NAT together.

themes.name: Network Security & Zero-Trust Edge
themes.description: The move is being driven mainly by broad strength in cybersecurity stocks after Bank of America raised price targets across the group and reiterated a constructive long-term outlook for cyber names like CRWD, NET, and peers. There is also company-specific follow-through from recent AI/security product and partnership headlines, especially for Cloudflare and CrowdStrike. For CVLT, the lift is more idiosyncratic and mixed, with positive business-news flow offsetting some litigation overhang.

themes.name: Senior & Long-Term Care Healthcare REITs
themes.description: LTC, OHI, and VTR are all benefiting from a broad bid into defensive, higher-yield healthcare REITs ahead of key central bank decisions this week, as investors rotate toward rate-sensitive income names with relatively stable fundamentals. Specifically, VTR is being driven higher by strong Q2 results in its senior housing (SHOP) segment and a cluster of price target hikes and positive analyst coverage, including upward FFO revisions and new initiation at Barclays and others. OHI is getting support from its recent revenue beat, renewed growth narrative, and dividend-focused positioning, while LTC is moving more on sector sympathy and anticipation into its upcoming August earnings and recent financing/obligation disclosures rather than a single, stock-specific headline.

themes.name: U.S. Regional & Mid-Cap Commercial Banks
themes.description: The move is mostly a regional-bank rerating after strong earnings and upbeat analyst revisions, with WSFS specifically getting a boost from a Q1 beat, higher guidance sentiment, and multiple target raises. For WAL, SSB, EWBC, USB, and UMBF, the likely shared catalyst is the same sector rotation into banks on improved net interest income, stable credit trends, and post-earnings momentum.

themes.name: Industrial Fluid Control, Filtration & Water Infrastructure Equipment
themes.description: DCI (Donaldson), FELE (Franklin Electric), IR (Ingersoll Rand), and IEX (Indian Energy Exchange) are all being helped by a pro‑cyclical backdrop of stronger industrial and energy demand, with investors rotating back into economically sensitive, high-quality industrials and infrastructure plays ahead of the next macro data and earnings wave. For IEX specifically, the catalyst is sustained volume and pricing strength on India’s power exchanges as summer heat drives electricity demand higher, plus continued foreign institutional accumulation and upcoming Q1 FY27 results that could validate the growth trend. Across the group, the trade is essentially a continuation bet on resilient capex, secular demand for efficiency/filtration/pressure solutions, and tight power markets supporting exchange economics.

themes.name: Truckload & LTL Freight Carriers
themes.description: HUBG is being driven higher by anticipation around resolving its accounting restatement/Nasdaq delinquency overhang and a potential relief move ahead of its next earnings and restated filings. ARCB is benefiting from positive sector sentiment after Goldman raised estimates on LTL and truckload carriers and from a 5.9% ABF Freight rate increase that supports pricing power. SNDR’s strength is tied to improving transport cycle expectations and constructive sell-side coverage (e.g., Stephens resuming with an Equal Weight and $40 target), alongside incremental positives around its refrigerated and cold-chain positioning.

themes.name: Open-Air & Strip Mall Retail REITs
themes.description: The move is mainly tied to stronger-than-expected Q2 REIT earnings and guidance from the retail shopping-center names, especially PECO’s record occupancy, raised 2026 FFO guidance, and higher acquisition outlook, which lifted sentiment across the group. FRT, KRG, KIM, SKT, and BRX are catching the same sector re-rating, with PECO and peers seeing analyst target increases and buy-side interest after the report.

themes.name: Cyber Exposure Management & Vulnerability Assessment
themes.description: For all three (Rapid7, Tenable, Qualys) the move is being driven less by stock‑specific news and more by a broad bid into cybersecurity software as investors position ahead of big‑tech/AI earnings and continued enterprise security spend themes. Qualys has an added tailwind from recent analyst upgrades and raised EPS guidance, which is pulling up the vulnerability‑management peer group. There are no major new M&A headlines or company‑specific catalysts for RPD or TENB this week beyond the sector re‑rating and short-covering in higher‑beta security names.

themes.name: Canadian Big Banks
themes.description: The main catalyst this week has been a combination of easing bond yields supporting financials, plus strong U.S. bank Q2 earnings that are being read through positively for the large Canadian banks, particularly BMO and TD given their U.S. exposure and for the group via capital markets strength. In addition, investors are paying up for perceived safety and dividend yield in Canadian bank stocks, driving sector-wide multiple expansion and flows into names like TD, RY, BNS, CM and BMO. A smaller, name-specific boost for BMO comes from the voiding of a US$564 million U.S. Ponzi-case verdict, which reduces legal overhang and supports sentiment.

themes.name: European Bank Stocks
themes.description: The main catalyst is a broader bid into European and UK banks on expectations that ECB/BoE rate cuts will be shallower and slower than previously priced, supporting net interest margins, combined with rising confidence that the region will avoid a hard landing. That macro shift is being reinforced by solid recent price action and technical breakouts in the major-bank cohort, with BBVA/SAN notably making new 1-year highs, drawing in momentum and sector-rotation flows. Stock-specific news is secondary this week; the move is largely sector- and macro-driven rather than on fresh company headlines for NWG, ING, LYG or BCS.

themes.name: Bitcoin Mining & Crypto Infrastructure Operators
themes.description: CIFR is moving higher mostly on a sector sympathy rally, not company-specific news, after Hut 8 landed a second $9.8 billion AI data-center lease and IREN raised its AI/cloud revenue outlook. That reinforced the market’s view that bitcoin miners pivoting into AI infrastructure can monetize their power and data-center assets. Cipher also got a lift from bargain-hunting and positioning ahead of its Q2 earnings.

themes.name: Coastal & Suburban Residential Rental REITs
themes.description: The main catalyst is the AVB–EQR all‑stock merger of equals, which has refocused attention on apartment REITs and highlighted the value of large-scale coastal multifamily platforms. That deal, plus better‑than‑expected Q2 FFO and raised same‑store revenue/NOI guidance at AVB and EQR, is lifting sentiment across the apartment and single‑family rental space (benefiting ESS, AMH, INVH) as investors price in improving fundamentals and potential further consolidation. A backdrop of moderating new supply and solid rent/occupancy trends in multifamily is reinforcing the move.

themes.name: Defense Precision Components & Mission-Critical Subsystems
themes.description: Hexcel (HXL) is being bid up on aerospace optimism following its long-term composite materials partnership with Deutsche Aircraft for the D328eco regional turboprop, which has refocused investors on secular demand from next-gen commercial and defense platforms. Frequency Electronics (FEIM) is moving higher on the back of its July 23 announcement of approximately $18 million in new satellite contract awards, plus attention around its recent Q4 earnings call and contract win headlines.

themes.name: U.S. Apparel & Lifestyle Brand Recovery
themes.description: VSXY is being driven higher by ongoing enthusiasm around Victoria’s Secret’s turnaround story: strong Q1 earnings, raised FY26 guidance, and persistent short-covering/ momentum following the recent proxy victory and operational improvements, with no new single headline this week but continued bullish coverage and product/newsflow (e.g., PINK launches) keeping buyers engaged. OXM’s strength appears more technical than fundamental this week, as the stock rebounds from prior weakness and benefits from a positive short-term setup and improving sentiment in discretionary/apparel names, rather than a specific fresh company-level news catalyst.

themes.name: Consumer Fintech & Digital Credit Platforms
themes.description: Sezzle (SEZL) is being driven higher by a combination of strong growth fundamentals and capital return: recent reports highlight rapid revenue and EPS growth, attractive valuation metrics, and a new or expanded stock repurchase authorization that signals management’s confidence in the business. For Dave (DAVE), the main recent catalyst has been a shareholder vote tied to corporate actions, with the stock continuing to trade within its high-volatility uptrend supported by strong multi‑year revenue and margin expansion rather than a specific fresh news event this week.

themes.name: Industrial Construction Execution & On-Site Supply Chain
themes.description: TPC is being driven higher by a string of large contract wins and balance sheet improvement, including the $651.8M Guam defense power infrastructure award and subsequent debt refinancing/redemption that are boosting backlog, earnings visibility, and perceived credit quality. SUNB’s move is largely sector-driven, benefiting from rotation into small-cap financials on post-holiday positioning and higher-rate resilience rather than a single stock-specific headline. DNOW and RYZ are gaining on corporate actions: DNOW from its completed combination with MRC Global that enhances scale and synergies, and RYZ from its completed merger with Olympic Steel plus a fresh 52-week high and expanded incentive plan that signal confidence and support momentum.

themes.name: U.S. Passenger Airlines
themes.description: The main catalyst is a sharp drop in oil prices, which is boosting fuel-sensitive airline stocks across the board; Reuters-linked coverage says crude fell enough to lift UAL, DAL, SKYW and ALK, with additional support from optimism around U.S.-Iran peace talks lowering geopolitical risk. There’s also some company-specific support layered on top: United has earnings and route-expansion momentum, while Alaska has been helped by bullish outlook/analyst coverage and recent operational updates.

themes.name: Commercial Real Estate Brokerage & Advisory Services
themes.description: The main catalyst pushing CBRE, NMRK, and JLL higher is renewed optimism around the commercial real estate operations cycle, driven by stronger leasing and capital markets activity, plus growing outsourcing demand that supports more recurring, fee-based revenue. Recent Q1 2026 results and guidance from CBRE and JLL highlighted double‑digit revenue growth, EPS beats, and raised or reinforced 2026 outlooks, while analysts have been emphasizing EPS growth in the high‑teens for both CBRE and Newmark and recommending the group as a way to play the sector’s rebound. The market is effectively repricing these names as beneficiaries of CRE recovery, data-center/AI-related infrastructure demand, and corporate outsourcing trends, rather than cyclical office-only proxies.

themes.name: Industrial & Logistics REITs
themes.description: The move looks fundamentally driven by leasing and portfolio-growth headlines, especially TRNO’s recent lease announcements in Doral and other markets, plus a prior property acquisition update. I don’t see a distinct fresh company-specific catalyst for STAG, so the week’s strength likely reflects the broader industrial REIT bid and sector flow rather than one major new headline.

themes.name: Global Steel & Metal Producers Recovery
themes.description: The main near-term catalyst is positive analyst and insider-related news: BNP Paribas upgraded Commercial Metals to Outperform and raised its price target to $75 on July 8, and Smart Insider highlighted CMC as “Pick of the Week” on July 22 following a CEO share purchase. These have reinforced the broader Buy consensus and attracted incremental institutional and retail interest, supporting the stock’s move higher this week.

themes.name: Copper Mining & Production
themes.description: The main catalyst is a broad rebound in copper prices and renewed optimism on global industrial demand, which is lifting copper miners as high-beta proxies for the metal. For SCCO specifically, the move is being amplified by expectations of stronger upcoming earnings and margin expansion at higher realized copper prices, alongside supportive analyst commentary and index-related flows. TGB and FCX are being carried by the same macro copper theme: tight supply, electrification/AI-related demand narratives, and positioning ahead of copper-sensitive economic data and earnings.

themes.name: Powersports & Recreational Vehicle Manufacturers
themes.description: Harley-Davidson (HOG) is being driven higher mainly by a bullish analyst shift and earnings setup: Loop Capital upgraded the stock to Buy with a higher $32 target, and investors are positioning ahead of its Q2 print and a new financing partnership for HDFS. Polaris (PII) is moving on Bank of America’s positive earnings preview, with estimates held near the high end of full-year guidance and expectations for solid upcoming results for the powersports group.

themes.name: Korean Financial Sector Recovery
themes.description: Shinhan Financial Group (SHG) is moving higher this week primarily on the back of its FY2025 profit growth and technical breakout above the 200-day moving average, which has attracted momentum and value investors. Recent disclosures around its 2026 value-up plan, higher payout intentions, and strategic moves such as weighing a Lotte Insurance acquisition are reinforcing the rerating trend in Korean financials. Sector-wide strength in South Korean banks and improving net interest income dynamics are adding a supportive macro tailwind to the move.

themes.name: Independent Power Producers & Nuclear Generation
themes.description: VST (diversified power generation with a large nuclear fleet), TLN (wholesale electricity generation), and CEG (pure-play nuclear generation via Constellation) are all leveraged to surging U.S. power demand driven by data center electrification and AI infrastructure build-out. The catalyst is structural: utilities cannot build fast enough, putting IPPs and nuclear operators in a strong pricing position in deregulated wholesale markets. This is a distinct sub-theme from traditional utilities — these companies sell into merchant markets, not regulated rate cases.

themes.name: Custom AI Silicon & Chip Architecture Licensing
themes.description: ARM, ALAB, CRDO, and MRVL are all being pulled higher by the same macro theme: renewed risk-on flows into AI and high-speed connectivity semis as investors rotate back into AI infrastructure after a recent pullback, with strong data-center demand and optical/interconnect growth the core narrative. For MRVL specifically, the move is reinforced by bullish analyst calls and target hikes tied to its AI data center and optical interconnect exposure, plus ongoing enthusiasm around its Nvidia/AI custom silicon positioning. CRDO and ALAB are benefiting from the same AI connectivity thesis and positive analyst sentiment, with CRDO supported by very strong growth guidance and ALAB by recent target hikes highlighting CXL upside.

themes.name: Hospital & Behavioral Health Facility Procedure Volume Recovery
themes.description: U.S. hospital operators and their key device suppliers are recovering as procedure volumes normalize post-pandemic deferral backlog and labor costs stabilize. HCA and UHS (behavioral health) are facility operators directly leveraged to admission and procedure counts, while BSX (interventional cardiology devices) and THC (hospital systems) are tightly coupled to in-hospital procedure volume. Rate-sensitive capex and staffing cost relief provide a second tailwind.

themes.name: Targeted Protein Degradation Oncology
themes.description: The main catalyst is renewed enthusiasm around targeted protein degradation and “molecular glue” degraders following Kymera’s accelerated timeline and strong momentum, which is lifting the broader degradation space and spilling over into Monte Rosa (GLUE). In GLUE specifically, investors are reacting to recent AACR data on its Cyclin E1‑directed molecular glue degrader for CCNE1‑amplified solid tumors and looking ahead to the expected IND submission for MRT‑55811 later in 2026. Together, those clinical and regulatory milestones are driving incremental speculative interest and bid in the stock this week.

themes.name: Automotive Components & Tire Suppliers
themes.description: Goodyear (GT) is being supported this week by its upcoming index change, moving from the S&P MidCap 400 to the S&P SmallCap 600 effective before trading on July 6, 2026, which typically drives incremental demand from index and small-cap managers. Adient (ADNT) is trading higher on the back of its recent Q2 FY26 earnings beat and raised 2026 guidance, with stronger-than-expected EPS, slight revenue beat, and ongoing share repurchases reinforcing the bullish narrative despite margin and regional demand concerns.

themes.name: Precious Metals Miners & Royalty Streamers
themes.description: The primary catalyst is a sharp move higher in spot gold prices, which has lifted the entire gold-mining complex. Rising bullion, driven by geopolitical tensions around the U.S.–Iran situation and its implications for inflation and Fed policy, is pushing NEM, KGC, AU, GFI, HMY and AGI higher in tandem. There does not appear to be a single, stock-specific news item this week; the move is largely macro and commodity-price driven.

themes.name: Precious Metals Royalty & Streaming Companies
themes.description: The primary driver for Franco-Nevada (FNV), Royal Gold (RGLD), and Wheaton Precious Metals (WPM) this week is macro: firmer gold prices on softer Fed rate expectations and a weaker dollar, which is lifting gold-linked royalty/streaming names leveraged to the metal. Company-specific news flow for FNV has been relatively quiet and mixed (Burkina Faso stream dispute, Cobre Panamá stockpile processing approvals, record prior-quarter results), so the move is largely a sector-wide precious metals and royalty trade rather than a single headline catalyst. Earnings estimate upgrades and optimistic analyst targets for FNV add incremental support but are secondary to the gold-price and rates backdrop.

themes.name: Analog & Microcontroller Semiconductors — Automotive & Industrial Cycle Recovery
themes.description: The primary catalyst is a broad-based upturn in analog and embedded semiconductor demand, especially in industrial, automotive, and data center markets, which is driving estimate revisions and a sector-wide re-rating across ADI, MCHP, NXPI, ON, and TXN. Texas Instruments’ role as an analog bellwether, coupled with multiple analyst price target and estimate hikes ahead of its Q2 earnings, is reinforcing the view that the cyclical trough is over and that the recovery in these end-markets is sustainable. This analog/industrial recovery is being layered on top of accelerating AI data center infrastructure demand, providing a powerful combination of cyclical and structural growth drivers for the group.

themes.name: Defense Prime Contractors & Aerospace Systems
themes.description: The primary catalyst is a very strong Q2 earnings season for the defense primes, with Lockheed Martin and RTX both posting beat-and-raise quarters, record backlogs, and raised 2026 guidance tied to sustained global rearmament and Pentagon restocking of missiles and munitions. LMT and RTX’s moves are spilling over into the group, helping LHX and HII as investors rotate back into defense on the combination of robust order books, missile and space contract wins, and renewed focus on air and missile defense capabilities. A supportive macro backdrop of ongoing geopolitical tensions and U.S. defense budget visibility is reinforcing the bid across these names.

themes.name: Multifamily Apartment REITs
themes.description: The main catalyst this week is a supportive macro backdrop for rate‑sensitive REITs as inflation expectations and long rates have eased, improving the outlook for apartment REIT cash flows and valuations. On the name-specific side, UDR is benefiting from recent bullish sell-side actions (Wells Fargo price target increase and Deutsche Bank upgrade to Buy with a higher target), which reinforce the broader bid into residential REITs. The rest of the group (CPT, MAA, IRT, UDR) is moving largely on sector rotation rather than stock-specific headlines.

themes.name: For-Profit Education & Career Training Providers
themes.description: Workforce retraining demand from displaced workers and the ongoing push for vocational and career-focused education credentials are creating tailwinds for for-profit education operators. The correlation cluster (CVSA, LINC, PRDO, STRA) alongside existing theme members suggests broader sector-level accumulation. Community college alternatives and online degree providers share the regulatory and enrollment cycle driver.

themes.description: Auto-retired 2026-07-29: dropped during merge/absorption (no successor found) (prior stage Nascent, 2 tickers).

themes.name: Regulated Gas & Electric Distribution Utilities
themes.description: Small and mid-cap regulated gas and electric distribution utilities (serving state-regulated service territories) are moving in a tight statistical cluster, likely reflecting a rotation into rate-sensitive, dividend-paying utilities as interest rate expectations shift. AVA (Avista), BKH (Black Hills), NJR (New Jersey Resources), NWE (Northwestern Energy), POR (Portland General), and SR (Spire) are all pure-play regulated distribution utilities with limited merchant exposure, making them highly sensitive to the same rate and regulatory catalysts.

themes.name: Traditional Staffing & Talent Placement Services
themes.description: Robert Half (RHI) is moving higher this week primarily on the back of a significant analyst price target hike and reiterated Buy rating, which triggered a sharp rerating in the shares. Multiple outlets note the stock has climbed more than 20–25% week-over-week after this upgrade and related bullish commentary highlighting it as a “Bull of the Day” and a cyclical recovery play.

themes.name: Specialty Pharma — Rare Disease & Cardiopulmonary Therapeutics
themes.description: KNSA is trading higher on the back of a Q2 Arcalyst-driven earnings beat, raised revenue guidance, and a series of aggressive price target hikes from major banks like Wedbush, Wells Fargo, and Goldman Sachs. LQDA’s strength is being driven by bullish analyst revisions and price target increases tied to favorable legal developments around the Yutrepia patent case, plus its recent inclusion in the S&P SmallCap 600 and strong launch momentum for Yutrepia.

themes.name: U.S. Petroleum Refining & Downstream Processing
themes.description: The group is moving higher on a sector-wide bid driven by elevated refining margins and crack spreads supported by tight global refining capacity, resilient fuel demand, and ongoing geopolitical disruptions in the Middle East and broader oil supply routes. Additional momentum is coming from bullish sentiment into Q2 earnings (especially for VLO and DINO), where the market expects strong margin realization and export demand to show up in the numbers. PARR also has a specific tailwind from recent analyst target increases tied to tight regional fuel markets and improved West Coast/Pacific Northwest margins, which reinforces the broader refining bull case.

themes.name: Cloud Contact Center & CCaaS Communication Platforms
themes.description: FIVN and RNG are moving higher this week primarily on sector and index-related catalysts rather than stock-specific news. RNG is benefiting from a SaaS rerating and value rotation after being added to multiple Russell value indexes and renewed focus on its AI platform, which has driven a broader re-rating of undervalued SaaS names. FIVN is rising in sympathy as a contact-center SaaS peer within the same theme, with the move tied to improving sentiment and technical momentum in mid-cap cloud/enterprise software rather than a discrete company-specific announcement.

themes.name: B2B Digital Financial Infrastructure & Payment Rails Modernization
themes.description: PAY is reacting to renewed crypto-payment sentiment and positive flow around Alchemy Pay’s expanding fiat/crypto on-ramp integrations, which has traders rotating back into niche payment rails. QTWO is being bid up ahead of its Q2 earnings report after the bell, with DA Davidson recently reiterating a Buy rating and higher full-year 2026 guidance and AI product (Q2 Assistant) underpinning sentiment. ACIW is moving higher on a series of strategic payment wins, notably its role in Europe’s Wero instant-payments initiative and broader EPI integration, which have strengthened the bull case around its global real-time payments footprint.

themes.name: SMB & Workforce Business Services Platforms
themes.description: NSP is moving higher on a technical breakout after Insperity (NSP US) crossed above its 200-day moving average around $36.5 this week, which is drawing in momentum and trend-following flows. In addition, recent commentary that Insperity could be materially undervalued following the SHRM26 HR conference spotlight on its HR360/HRCore/HRScale platforms has supported a re-rating narrative among investors. There does not appear to be a single discrete fundamental news release this week, but rather a combination of these technical and valuation-driven catalysts.

themes.name: Professional Advisory & Business Services
themes.description: CBIZ is trading higher this week primarily on its Q2 earnings beat, with adjusted diluted EPS of $0.91 versus the $0.72 consensus, which triggered a gap up in the stock. A secondary catalyst is the announced all-cash acquisition by Grant Thornton Advisors at $55 per share, which is anchoring near-term valuation and supporting the move higher. There is no fresh company-specific catalyst for CRA International yet, as its Q2 results are not scheduled to be reported until August 6.

themes.name: Cinema Exhibition & Premium Large-Format Recovery
themes.description: Cinemark (CNK) and IMAX are being driven higher this week primarily by blockbuster demand for IMAX 70mm screenings of Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” which is generating historic box office and premium ticket pricing, spotlighting premium theatrical formats across the sector. In CNK’s case that momentum is pairing with record summer box office and anticipation around its Q2 print and investor deck, while IMAX is benefitting directly from exceptionally strong IMAX revenue and pricing on “The Odyssey” and related analyst optimism.

themes.name: Inflammatory Disease & Immunology Biologics
themes.description: SYRE/ORKA doesn’t appear to have a fresh, stock-specific news catalyst this week; the move looks like a continuation of the strong uptrend that began after the positive Phase 2 psoriasis data and major analyst target hikes in late April, plus ongoing “Strong Buy” ratings and very high institutional ownership. Recent scanners explicitly flag no unusual-volume or headline catalyst and suggest trading is in line with its established range, with the next clear event on the calendar being the August earnings report. In other words, price action is being driven more by momentum and positioning than by new fundamental news this week.

themes.name: Medical Device Mean-Reversion & Rotation Recovery
themes.description: XRAY is being driven by optimism around its restructuring and capital deployment plan, including $120M in annualized cost savings and a shift toward debt reduction and share repurchases, which has supported a rebound after prior earnings-related volatility. CNMD is seeing interest ahead of its Q2 earnings report along with support from recent capital structure moves, notably the planned buyback of $645.2M of 2.25% convertible notes due 2027 and a new CFO appointment. INSP and TNDM are benefiting from the broader bid into medtech/medical device names, with TNDM additionally supported by recent regulatory and product milestones such as expanded EU indications and new sensor compatibility, which improve its long-term growth narrative.

themes.name: Franchise Auto Dealership Groups
themes.description: SAH, ABG, and PAG are trading higher this week on a combination of sector-wide strength in auto retail and company-specific corporate activity/expectations. For PAG specifically, the key catalyst is the unsolicited, preliminary, non-binding offer from Penske Corporation and Mitsui to acquire the remaining shares at $210 per share in cash, along with follow-through from bullish technical momentum and capital-allocation actions like dividend increases. SAH and ABG are benefiting from read-across and M&A/spec takeout sentiment in the dealer group space as investors reassess valuations and consolidation potential.

themes.name: China Consumer Internet & Digital Marketplace Platforms
themes.description: ATHM (Autohome) has been moving higher this week mainly on the back of a strong recent price trend and improving sentiment after solid fundamentals over the past month, with several analysts maintaining Hold ratings and medium-term upside targets. There is no single discrete news headline this week; the move looks more like a continuation of a roughly 10–11% one‑month uptrend supported by high institutional ownership and views that the stock is modestly undervalued despite Citi’s recent price target cut. In short, it’s a technical/flow-driven extension of prior positive momentum rather than a fresh, specific catalyst.

themes.name: Corporate Spend, Expense Management & Financial Operations Software
themes.description: The move higher in WEX this week is being driven primarily by its setting a new 12‑month high on the back of strong recent fundamentals and momentum, which has attracted fresh “time to buy” commentary from equity research outlets. That follows a robust backdrop of record 2025 revenue and net income, Q1 2026 beats on EPS and revenue, and an active capital return story (large 2025 buybacks and a new US$1bn repurchase authorization announced in June), all of which are reinforcing the bull narrative. NAVN/BILL aren’t showing a discrete, stock‑specific headline this week; they are largely participating in the broader strength in payments/fintech and business services rather than trading off a single, new catalyst.

themes.name: Dermatology & Atopic Immunology Biologics
themes.description: FBRX is ripping on the definitive all‑cash takeover by argenx at $77 per share, a roughly 41% premium that crystallizes upside and effectively caps the stock near deal terms while it trades into the spread. The move is underpinned by recent positive Phase 1b data for FB102 in vitiligo and celiac disease, which argenx highlighted as the core rationale for the $2.2 billion acquisition. APGE’s strength is being driven by sustained follow‑through on earlier positive 52‑week Phase 2 data for APG777 in atopic dermatitis plus a successful $403 million equity raise, with added momentum from AbbVie’s subsequent cash buyout offer headlines keeping M&A premium expectations elevated.

themes.name: Office REIT Recovery & Re-Rating
themes.description: The move in the office REITs is being driven mainly by a constructive shift in sentiment toward high‑quality office landlords, supported by fresh leasing wins and valuation calls. For BXP specifically, Scotiabank’s recent upgrade to Outperform on the back of strong leasing momentum, plus multiple large lease announcements, has reinforced the “return‑to‑office” and occupancy-recovery narrative and highlighted the stock as undervalued. SLG, HIW and CDP are riding the same theme of improving fundamentals and renewed investor interest in trophy and Sunbelt office assets rather than any single company‑specific headline this week.

themes.name: Cloud Supply Chain & Warehouse Management Software
themes.description: MANH is trading higher this week primarily on a strong Q2 earnings beat and a “beat-and-raise” guide, with revenue, EPS, and full-year 2026 guidance all coming in above Street expectations. Management highlighted a third consecutive record bookings quarter and accelerating cloud-driven growth, reinforcing confidence in future demand and margins. The move is being amplified by positive analyst reactions, including price target increases that are adding to the momentum bid in the stock.

themes.name: Enterprise HR & Workforce Management SaaS
themes.description: PCTY is higher on Citigroup naming it a top pick in HR software ahead of earnings, while WDAY is rallying on pre-earnings positioning plus renewed AI/enterprise-software optimism. ALIT’s move appears more sector/tactical than company-specific based on the available tape, with no clear fresh catalyst visible in the results.

themes.name: IT Distribution & Technology Services Providers
themes.description: INGM is moving higher mainly on an earnings-driven re‑rating: consensus estimates and “Most Accurate” estimates have been revised up, Zacks upgraded the name to Strong Buy, and the stock is benefiting from positive AI and cloud news (including an Oracle Cloud distribution program) that supports a higher fair value and targets. EFOR’s strength this week is tied to its recent 8‑K filing detailing a new material agreement and financial obligation plus upbeat company news flow, including government contract-related recognition and management share purchases, which together signal improved fundamentals and leadership confidence.

themes.name: Peptide & Hormone Therapies for Metabolic & Endocrine Disorders
themes.description: CORT is being driven by the FDA resubmission of its New Drug Application for relacorilant in Cushing’s syndrome, renewing expectations for an approval and incremental revenue. PTGX is rallying on positive sentiment and sell-side commentary following Johnson & Johnson’s recent FDA approval of its psoriasis drug that uses Protagonist’s peptide, which is seen as unlocking significant value for PTGX. For XERS and MBX, there is no specific stock‑specific news; the move appears more momentum/technical and sympathy-based within the biotech space rather than tied to a discrete catalyst.

themes.name: Containerboard & Corrugated Packaging Producers
themes.description: The main catalyst is a containerboard price hike: Packaging Corporation of America announced plans to raise prices by $140 per ton in September, and investors expect International Paper and Smurfit WestRock to follow. PKG also got a lift from strong Q2 results and a raised quarterly dividend, while SW has been riding the same sector-wide pricing momentum.

themes.name: Digital Payments Processing & Merchant Acquiring Networks
themes.description: PYPL is trading higher this week primarily on its Q2 beat-and-raise: PayPal reported stronger-than-expected earnings and lifted full-year non-GAAP guidance, which drove a roughly 4% move up after the print. Earnings strength is being layered onto the existing takeover narrative from Stripe/Advent, with the CEO signaling openness to value-creating deals, keeping M&A speculation alive as an ongoing catalyst. For the FOUR ETF, the same fintech repricing theme around PayPal’s bid and solid results is contributing to a supportive backdrop for payments names.

themes.name: Life Insurance & Annuity Providers
themes.description: Met, Principal and Prudential are all trading higher on a combination of sector and stock-specific catalysts: investors are leaning into life insurers as “higher-for-longer” rates continue to support spreads and investment income, and the group is being highlighted positively in recent research coverage. On the name level, PFG is breaking out to a new 52-week high after another round of price-target hikes (most recently Bank of America to $104) on the back of strong Q1 earnings and margin expansion, while PRU and MET are benefiting from upcoming earnings visibility and incremental target raises from Mizuho and others alongside the favorable rate backdrop. Overall, the move is being driven more by reinforcement of the “rate tailwind + solid earnings/valuation” narrative than by any single company-specific headline this week.

themes.name: AI-Powered Enterprise Analytics & Intelligent Workflow SaaS
themes.description: INTA is moving higher on follow‑through from its recent earnings beat and guidance raise, plus ongoing enthusiasm around its AI-enabled vertical SaaS positioning for professional services firms. AVPT is being driven by a strong AI narrative: recent earnings, new AI/agentic product initiatives, and research highlighting rapid enterprise AI adoption and governance needs are fueling demand for its data management and compliance platform. AMPL’s strength this week is tied to its latest earnings and upbeat outlook on demand for its digital optimization/experimentation platform, benefiting from the broader AI and data-driven marketing/software rerating.

themes.name: Uniform Rental & Managed Workwear Services
themes.description: CTAS is being driven higher by a clean earnings beat and upbeat forward guidance, followed by an upgrade from Bank of America to Buy with a higher price target, which is reinforcing the post-earnings momentum. For VSTS, the move is tied to ongoing rerating in the name after its recent spin/standalone listing, with improving fundamentals and investors rotating into outsourced facilities/uniform services as a more defensive, recurring-revenue play.

themes.name: Wealth Management & Retail Brokerage Platforms
themes.description: The group is moving higher on a combination of strong recent/ongoing earnings prints and upward estimate/price-target revisions that reinforce the durability of wealth-management and brokerage fee/interest income in a stable-rate, risk-on equity tape. RJF is specifically reacting to record fiscal Q3 results and a wave of higher price targets, while LPLA, AMP and SEIC are bid ahead of or around earnings on expectations of advisory and asset-based fee growth and continued AUM gains. SCHW is additionally supported by rising trading activity (STAX at a four-year high) and optimism around new revenue levers like digital assets, which lifts the whole retail brokerage/RIAs complex.

themes.name: European Bank Stocks
themes.description: The main catalyst lifting BBVA, Santander, ING, NatWest, Lloyds and other European banks this week is the “higher-for-longer” rates narrative, which improves net interest margins and sector earnings expectations, combined with resilient recent bank results. Spanish and UK bank commentary has highlighted strong trading income, solid loan growth, limited credit deterioration, and supportive analyst actions (e.g., upbeat BBVA midterm targets, Fitch affirming BBVA’s rating, Jefferies reiterating buy), which is driving a broad rerating of European financials rather than stock-specific news. Geopolitical-driven oil and inflation worries are a modest headwind, but are being outweighed by improved profitability outlooks and ongoing capital return (buybacks and dividends) across the group.

themes.name: Global Crude & Product Tanker Fleet Operators
themes.description: The main driver is a broad move higher in crude tanker rates and sentiment as spot earnings and time-charter equivalents have inflected up again, boosting cash flow expectations across the group. In addition, investors are rotating back into high-dividend shipping names after recent oil price volatility and macro data revived interest in energy and transport cyclicals. There is no single stock‑specific headline this week; it’s a sector-wide rate and yield trade lifting TNK, INSW, DHT, FRO, and NAT together.

themes.name: Online Insurance Comparison & Digital Marketplace Platforms
themes.description: MAX EVER’s strength this week is being driven primarily by company-specific news: MediaAlpha (MAX) is rallying into its scheduled Q2 2026 earnings release, which is increasing speculation about improved profitability and a continued recovery in insurance customer acquisition spending. Separately, Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions (often tagged as MAX EVER/Max Ever in some feeds) recently hit an all-time high after announcing a major renewable energy partnership with Meta to build 837 MW of solar and wind capacity, with Meta buying all green attributes from these projects, which remains a key sentiment tailwind. Broadly supportive AI- and tech-led equity momentum is providing a constructive backdrop but is secondary to these direct catalysts.

themes.name: U.S. Domestic Steel Producers
themes.description: The move in STLD and NUE this week is being driven primarily by a continued rally in U.S. steel prices, with hot‑rolled coil rebounding toward roughly $1,200/ton on mill price hikes, longer lead times and tighter supply from outages and reduced imports under tariffs. That macro steel pricing backdrop is being reinforced by bullish analyst actions and earnings momentum at NUE (recent beats and upgrades on stronger steel pricing outlook) and ongoing strong flat‑rolled order activity at STLD. Together, those factors are feeding a sector‑wide bid into U.S. steel producers, lifting both names.

themes.name: Commercial Real Estate Brokerage & Advisory Services
themes.description: CBRE and JLL are trading higher this week primarily on the back of blowout Q2 2026 earnings beats and raised full-year guidance, signaling accelerating growth in their core advisory and outsourcing businesses. A key narrative shift is their leveraged exposure to AI-driven data center and critical infrastructure demand, with CBRE showing particularly strong double‑digit growth in data center and infrastructure services and JLL highlighting similar themes. The move is reinforced by a broader re‑rating of commercial real estate services as a cyclical recovery story, with improving leasing, capital markets activity, and positive industry outlooks from analysts for outsourced real estate and AI‑related infrastructure.

themes.name: Consumer Staples Packaged Food & Snack Brand Recovery
themes.description: LW is trading higher this week mainly on anticipation around its July 24th Q4/FY26 earnings release and Starboard Value’s activist involvement pushing for an Investor Day and a 25% EBITDA margin target by FY2029. There is also a defensive bid as investors focus on operational efficiency moves like the planned closure of the Broekhuizenvorst, Netherlands plant and cost-savings/capex discipline highlighted in recent results and guidance. CAG’s move higher is being driven by value and yield interest after the stock crossed a double‑digit dividend yield, alongside insider buying and a new CEO that is prompting a contrarian turnaround narrative despite recent negative sentiment and estimate cuts.

themes.name: Life Science Tools & Analytical Instruments
themes.description: Thermo Fisher (TMO) is moving higher mainly on its strong Q2 2026 earnings beat and raised full-year guidance, which reassured investors that life-science tools demand is improving. The stock is also getting an extra lift from analyst upgrades and bullish price-target hikes after the report.

themes.name: Hotel REIT Recovery & Re-Rating
themes.description: RLJ and XHR are being bid up this week primarily on the back of a broad lodging/hotel REIT move tied to World Cup-driven strength in New York/New Jersey hotel fundamentals, with occupancy above 90% and ADR up roughly 38% year over year on match days. Strong RevPAR gains in host markets (game-day RevPAR up about 41% on average, with some markets up more than 100% year over year) are reinforcing the bullish narrative around urban, transient-focused hotel REITs, pulling the group to fresh 52-week highs.

themes.name: Cloud Observability & AIOps Monitoring Platforms
themes.description: DDOG is being driven higher this week by a cluster of bullish analyst actions, including multiple price target hikes (Morgan Stanley to 300, Citi to 300, Benchmark to 330, JMP to 311) tied to strong AI/cloud observability growth and momentum ahead of its August 6 earnings print. PD is benefiting from similar positioning in high-growth software tied to AI and observability, with investors rotating into the group on expectations that upcoming earnings and AI-related demand will support continued multiple expansion.

themes.name: Department Store Retail Recovery
themes.description: DDS is being driven by its recent massive Q1 earnings beat, bolstered by a one-time $104M litigation settlement that added over $5 per share to EPS and has analysts highlighting upside in the stock. For KSS, the move is largely tied to its ongoing turnaround narrative: a solid Q1 print in late May and, more recently, the appointment and expanded mandate of new COO Elliott Rodgers, which has prompted bullish commentary about operational improvements and undervaluation. Overall, both are benefiting from a bid into department stores/retail on improving fundamentals and restructuring stories rather than a single new headline this week.

themes.name: U.S. Apparel & Fashion Recovery
themes.description: The move in UA, RVLV, and CROX this week is primarily driven by a rotation back into consumer/retail discretionary on easing inflation and improving consumer-spending sentiment, which is lifting the broader athletic and specialty retail complex. Within that, CROX has an added catalyst from positive earnings momentum and a fresh Bank of America price target hike that is prompting a valuation re-rate, while RVLV is benefiting from recent favorable research/upgrade coverage highlighting margin expansion and AI-driven customer growth. Under Armour is catching sympathy flows as investors re-risk into branded athletic/lifestyle names ahead of the next earnings cycle.

themes.name: Asset Management & Fund Administration Platform Ecosystem
