themes.description: BX is moving higher on renewed interest in alternatives and strong fee-related earnings momentum, as investors rotate into large-cap private equity platforms that benefit from higher realizations and fundraising visibility. SS&C (SSNC) is being driven by its record Q2 print, double beat on revenue and EPS, raised full‑year 2026 guidance, and a record share buyback, which collectively triggered double‑digit upside and follow‑through buying. Incremental support is coming from positive sell-side reactions and growing investor focus on SS&C’s AI-driven automation and data platforms as margin and growth catalysts.

themes.name: Cloud Data Storage & Analytics Infrastructure
themes.description: BLZE is being driven higher by the recently announced five-year, multi-exabyte AI cloud storage deal with CoreWeave valued at about $335 million, which materially changes the growth and revenue outlook for the company. Follow-on coverage has framed the CoreWeave agreement as a “game-changing” AI storage megadeal, triggering analyst upgrades and higher price targets, which is fueling momentum in the stock this week. SNOW’s move is being supported by a cluster of bullish sell-side actions (UBS, BTIG, Barclays, TD Cowen raising or reiterating buy/equal-weight ratings and higher targets) and ongoing positive narrative around its AI/data cloud positioning and large-scale AWS contract, sustaining investor appetite.

themes.name: Enterprise Server, Storage & Data Infrastructure Hardware
themes.description: The common driver is a renewed leg of the AI infrastructure/server trade, with upside read‑through from Super Micro’s record AI server orders and Dell’s own blowout AI server results and analyst target hikes, which are lifting the whole enterprise hardware complex. For DELL specifically, investors are chasing its AI server growth story after historic AI-optimized server revenue, strong guidance and fresh price target raises. For HPE and NTAP, the move is largely sympathy/sector rotation into AI data center, storage, and server names as investors extrapolate the same tight capacity and accelerating AI infrastructure demand theme.

themes.name: AI-Augmented Business Process Outsourcing & IT Services
themes.description: EXLS G’s move higher this week is being driven primarily by follow-through from its stronger-than-expected recent quarterly earnings, which showed double-digit revenue and EPS growth and came with a raised full-year outlook. Management increased guidance for both revenue and adjusted EPS, reinforcing the growth story and sustaining momentum in the stock after the initial post-earnings surge. There is no new single-day headline catalyst this week; it’s an extension of the positive earnings/guide and AI-focused strategic narrative already in place.

themes.name: Clinical-Stage Oncology Biotech
themes.description: TGTX is trading higher on renewed optimism around its MS drug BRIUMVI, driven by fresh enthusiasm over the emerging subcutaneous formulation and broader expansion potential in autoimmune/neurologic indications, which has boosted sentiment on the franchise’s long‑term growth. In parallel, increasing biotech M&A chatter has put TG Therapeutics on lists of potential buyout candidates, adding a speculative premium to the stock. ELVN’s strength is being supported by recent positive Phase 1 ENABLE data for ELVN‑001 in CML, upward analyst target revisions, and follow‑through from its large, recently upsized equity offering that validated institutional interest in the story.

themes.name: Smart Home Security & Comfort Systems
themes.description: Resideo (REZI) and Alarm.com (ALRM) have been moving higher primarily on company‑specific and structural catalysts rather than a single discrete headline this week. For REZI, the key drivers are the ongoing ADI spin-off process and related unsecured notes offering, plus accumulation by institutions such as Arrowstreet Capital and a still‑constructive Street view with upside to consensus targets. For ALRM, the move is largely sympathy and sector read‑through, as investors reposition into home security and smart‑home names that benefit from Resideo’s restructuring and improving sentiment in connected‑home/security peers.

themes.name: Private Mortgage Insurance
themes.description: The common upside driver is a broad re-rating of U.S. mortgage insurers on expectations that still-strong credit performance, benign loss trends, and active capital return (buybacks/dividends) will support earnings and book-value growth even with muted origination volumes. In addition, M&A and diversification themes (e.g., Radian’s Inigo acquisition broadening earnings beyond U.S. MI) plus a pickup in positive news sentiment and valuation-focused research are pulling the group higher as investors rotate into discounted housing-credit names. Finally, positioning ahead of upcoming earnings (notably for NMIH) is adding a short-term bid as investors expect capital deployment and reserve/credit updates to reinforce the bullish narrative.

themes.name: Network Security & Zero-Trust Edge
themes.description: The move is being driven mainly by broad strength in cybersecurity stocks after Bank of America raised price targets across the group and reiterated a constructive long-term outlook for cyber names like CRWD, NET, and peers. There is also company-specific follow-through from recent AI/security product and partnership headlines, especially for Cloudflare and CrowdStrike. For CVLT, the lift is more idiosyncratic and mixed, with positive business-news flow offsetting some litigation overhang.

themes.name: Insurance Brokerage & Distribution Services
themes.description: AJG, AON, and BRO are being driven higher primarily by a sector-wide bid into insurance brokers ahead of earnings, as investors rotate toward stable, fee-based financials in a volatile macro and rate backdrop. In addition, Brown & Brown’s strong Q1 print and AJG’s ongoing M&A-driven growth and price target hike from UBS have reinforced the bullish fundamental narrative across the group. AON’s upcoming earnings and positive industry commentary highlighting favorable pricing, underwriting, and consolidation in insurance brokerage are adding to the momentum.

themes.name: Industrial Fluid Control, Filtration & Water Infrastructure Equipment
themes.description: DCI (Donaldson), FELE (Franklin Electric), IR (Ingersoll Rand), and IEX (Indian Energy Exchange) are all being helped by a pro‑cyclical backdrop of stronger industrial and energy demand, with investors rotating back into economically sensitive, high-quality industrials and infrastructure plays ahead of the next macro data and earnings wave. For IEX specifically, the catalyst is sustained volume and pricing strength on India’s power exchanges as summer heat drives electricity demand higher, plus continued foreign institutional accumulation and upcoming Q1 FY27 results that could validate the growth trend. Across the group, the trade is essentially a continuation bet on resilient capex, secular demand for efficiency/filtration/pressure solutions, and tight power markets supporting exchange economics.

themes.name: Property & Casualty Insurance Underwriters
themes.description: The move looks most likely driven by a broad re-rating of the U.S. property & casualty insurance group rather than a company-specific event, with investors rotating into the sector’s large, high-quality underwriters. I do not see a single common announcement across WRB, TRV, ALL, ACGL, CB, and AFG in the provided material; WRB’s only company-specific item is an executive change, which would not explain the group-wide strength.

themes.name: U.S. Passenger Airlines
themes.description: The main catalyst is a stronger airline read-through after recent earnings: United and Delta both beat Q2 expectations, and United raised guidance, which is supporting the group. SKYW also got a direct boost from its Q2 update, including a bigger buyback authorization and an expanded American Airlines flying deal. Lower oil prices after recent U.S.-Iran tensions easing are adding a second tailwind for UAL and DAL.

themes.name: Powersports & Recreational Vehicle Manufacturers
themes.description: Harley-Davidson (HOG) is being driven higher mainly by a bullish analyst shift and earnings setup: Loop Capital upgraded the stock to Buy with a higher $32 target, and investors are positioning ahead of its Q2 print and a new financing partnership for HDFS. Polaris (PII) is moving on Bank of America’s positive earnings preview, with estimates held near the high end of full-year guidance and expectations for solid upcoming results for the powersports group.

themes.name: Industrial Construction Execution & On-Site Supply Chain
themes.description: TPC (Tutor Perini) has been driven higher by a series of large federal and defense-related contract wins, notably a roughly $650 million Guam defense contract and a major Houston data center infrastructure project that materially boost backlog and earnings visibility. RYZ (Ryze) and DNOW (NOW Inc.) are rising on the broader strength in energy and industrial spending tied to heightened geopolitical tension and infrastructure demand, which supports oilfield services, distribution, and related equipment names. Across all three tickers, incremental analyst upgrades and improving credit/debt profiles are reinforcing the move as investors rotate into cyclical, infrastructure-levered stories.

themes.name: Canadian Big Banks
themes.description: The main catalyst this week has been a combination of easing bond yields supporting financials, plus strong U.S. bank Q2 earnings that are being read through positively for the large Canadian banks, particularly BMO and TD given their U.S. exposure and for the group via capital markets strength. In addition, investors are paying up for perceived safety and dividend yield in Canadian bank stocks, driving sector-wide multiple expansion and flows into names like TD, RY, BNS, CM and BMO. A smaller, name-specific boost for BMO comes from the voiding of a US$564 million U.S. Ponzi-case verdict, which reduces legal overhang and supports sentiment.

themes.name: U.S. Regional & Mid-Cap Commercial Banks
themes.description: The move is mostly a regional-bank rerating after strong earnings and upbeat analyst revisions, with WSFS specifically getting a boost from a Q1 beat, higher guidance sentiment, and multiple target raises. For WAL, SSB, EWBC, USB, and UMBF, the likely shared catalyst is the same sector rotation into banks on improved net interest income, stable credit trends, and post-earnings momentum.

themes.name: Cyber Exposure Management & Vulnerability Assessment
themes.description: The main catalyst is a heightened focus on cybersecurity and vulnerability management following a joint U.S./international security advisory warning of Russian state-sponsored cyber threats against critical infrastructure, which has boosted investor demand for names like Tenable and Rapid7. In addition, Tenable and Qualys both recently secured FedRAMP High authorizations for key cloud exposure/TotalCloud offerings, expanding their addressable U.S. federal market and reinforcing the sector’s government/critical infrastructure growth narrative. This is occurring against a broader backdrop of strong AI-led product momentum and platform positioning across these vendors, which is attracting incremental interest as investors rotate into cybersecurity beneficiaries of rising threat volumes.

themes.name: Open-Air & Strip Mall Retail REITs
themes.description: The move is mainly tied to stronger-than-expected Q2 REIT earnings and guidance from the retail shopping-center names, especially PECO’s record occupancy, raised 2026 FFO guidance, and higher acquisition outlook, which lifted sentiment across the group. FRT, KRG, KIM, SKT, and BRX are catching the same sector re-rating, with PECO and peers seeing analyst target increases and buy-side interest after the report.

themes.name: Cross-Border & International Payments Processing
themes.description: EEFT and GPN are higher largely on a broad payment-processor rebound rather than a single company-specific headline, with both names showing modest gains this week. The clearest stock-specific catalyst in the results is GPN’s resumed coverage at Morgan Stanley with an Equal Weight rating and $65 target, while EEFT’s move appears more sentiment-driven.

themes.name: Senior & Long-Term Care Healthcare REITs
themes.description: LTC, OHI, and VTR are all benefiting from a broad bid into defensive, higher-yield healthcare REITs ahead of key central bank decisions this week, as investors rotate toward rate-sensitive income names with relatively stable fundamentals. Specifically, VTR is being driven higher by strong Q2 results in its senior housing (SHOP) segment and a cluster of price target hikes and positive analyst coverage, including upward FFO revisions and new initiation at Barclays and others. OHI is getting support from its recent revenue beat, renewed growth narrative, and dividend-focused positioning, while LTC is moving more on sector sympathy and anticipation into its upcoming August earnings and recent financing/obligation disclosures rather than a single, stock-specific headline.

themes.name: B2B Marketing Automation & Customer Engagement SaaS
themes.description: HubSpot (HUBS) is trading higher on renewed AI enthusiasm around its CRM and marketing automation platform, with investors rotating back into AI-enabled software following positive megacap AI sentiment. Klaviyo (KVYO) is being bid up on accelerating revenue growth, record operating margins, raised full-year guidance, and an expanded share buyback program, which collectively signal improving profitability and stronger management confidence. Broader AI sector strength and CRM automation headlines are reinforcing the move in both names.

themes.name: Financial Compliance & Regulatory Reporting SaaS
themes.description: DFIN is catching a bid on the back of a recent institutional buy disclosure from Fifth Third Bancorp, which increased its stake and highlighted DFIN’s better‑than‑expected earnings, strong recurring revenue profile, and Buy‑rated analyst backdrop. WK is moving higher on its own strong earnings print and bullish 2026 outlook that came out this week, which is driving follow‑through buying in cloud/compliance names. Together, the combination of positive fundamental news and supportive analyst sentiment is the key catalyst for both names.

themes.name: Molecular Diagnostics & DNA-Based Genetic Testing
themes.description: QGEN is likely moving on a mix of recent corporate/news flow and positioning, especially Qiagen’s June 27 addition to the Russell 1000 Dynamic Index and the recent Goldman Sachs disclosure of a 3.65% voting interest. There’s also some support from recent analyst coverage/news such as Kepler’s Hold rating and the IngenuitySystems acquisition headline, but the Russell-index inclusion appears to be the clearest catalyst.

themes.name: Coastal & Suburban Residential Rental REITs
themes.description: Auto-retired 2026-07-30: dropped during merge/absorption (no successor found) (prior stage Fading, 5 tickers).

themes.name: Copper Mining & Production
themes.description: The main catalyst is a broad copper rally driven by stronger China industrial data, AI-related infrastructure demand, and renewed tariff/reshoring narratives that are pushing base metals and copper miners higher across the board. At the stock level, sentiment is being reinforced by recent positive operating/earnings commentary for copper producers (e.g., TECK’s output and government-support news) and a wave of analyst target hikes and “outperform” style pieces on smaller copper names like TGB, which is pulling up the whole group. There is no single company-specific headline this week; it’s a sector-wide copper theme that is lifting SCCO, HBM, FCX, and TGB simultaneously.

themes.name: Investment Research & Financial Analytics Data Platforms
themes.description: The main driver this week is Morningstar’s continued AI-related product push and visibility, including recent commentary and tools around AI stock analysis and digital asset funds, which has reinforced the narrative that it can monetize data/analytics demand tied to the AI cycle. That thematic interest, combined with its positioning as a beneficiary of increased market volatility and fund-flows ahead of the Fed meeting and megacap earnings, is likely attracting incremental institutional buying rather than a single, discrete company-specific headline.

themes.name: Cruise Line & Ocean Travel Recovery
themes.description: NCLH and RCL are higher mainly on a broad cruise-sector rally after reports of a pause in U.S.-Iran hostilities pushed oil prices down, which eases fuel-cost pressure on cruise lines. NCLH is also getting an added lift from pre-earnings positioning ahead of its July 30 Q2 report, with investors looking for a potential beat and better cruise-demand commentary.

themes.name: Specialty Insurance Underwriting & Brokerage
themes.description: PLMR is moving higher on the back of raised 2026 adjusted net income guidance and a subsequent wave of positive commentary highlighting upside to earnings and price targets. RYAN is being supported by the recently expanded $600 million share repurchase authorization and disclosure of significant institutional buying (e.g., Fenimore Asset Management increasing its stake by over 80%), which together signal strong management and investor confidence.

themes.name: Tax Preparation & Consumer Financial Software Platforms
themes.description: INTU is moving higher this week primarily on follow-through from strong fiscal Q3 results and raised full-year revenue and earnings guidance, plus renewed focus on its longer-term growth story after a recent selloff. The launch of a new QuickBooks-integrated business credit card and expanded AI/strategic partnerships (including Anthropic and FedNow) are reinforcing the small-business ecosystem and improving sentiment. HRB’s move appears more modest, with the main recent catalyst being Stephens initiating coverage at Equal Weight with a $47 price target, which has put some incremental attention on the name.

themes.name: Truckload & LTL Freight Carriers
themes.description: HUBG is being driven higher by anticipation around resolving its accounting restatement/Nasdaq delinquency overhang and a potential relief move ahead of its next earnings and restated filings. ARCB is benefiting from positive sector sentiment after Goldman raised estimates on LTL and truckload carriers and from a 5.9% ABF Freight rate increase that supports pricing power. SNDR’s strength is tied to improving transport cycle expectations and constructive sell-side coverage (e.g., Stephens resuming with an Equal Weight and $40 target), alongside incremental positives around its refrigerated and cold-chain positioning.

themes.name: Defense Precision Components & Mission-Critical Subsystems
themes.description: Hexcel (HXL) is being bid up on aerospace optimism following its long-term composite materials partnership with Deutsche Aircraft for the D328eco regional turboprop, which has refocused investors on secular demand from next-gen commercial and defense platforms. Frequency Electronics (FEIM) is moving higher on the back of its July 23 announcement of approximately $18 million in new satellite contract awards, plus attention around its recent Q4 earnings call and contract win headlines.

themes.name: U.S. Apparel & Lifestyle Brand Recovery
themes.description: VSXY is being driven higher by ongoing enthusiasm around Victoria’s Secret’s turnaround story: strong Q1 earnings, raised FY26 guidance, and persistent short-covering/ momentum following the recent proxy victory and operational improvements, with no new single headline this week but continued bullish coverage and product/newsflow (e.g., PINK launches) keeping buyers engaged. OXM’s strength appears more technical than fundamental this week, as the stock rebounds from prior weakness and benefits from a positive short-term setup and improving sentiment in discretionary/apparel names, rather than a specific fresh company-level news catalyst.

themes.name: Consumer Fintech & Digital Credit Platforms
themes.description: Sezzle (SEZL) is being driven higher by a combination of strong growth fundamentals and capital return: recent reports highlight rapid revenue and EPS growth, attractive valuation metrics, and a new or expanded stock repurchase authorization that signals management’s confidence in the business. For Dave (DAVE), the main recent catalyst has been a shareholder vote tied to corporate actions, with the stock continuing to trade within its high-volatility uptrend supported by strong multi‑year revenue and margin expansion rather than a specific fresh news event this week.

themes.name: Industrial & Logistics REITs
themes.description: The move looks fundamentally driven by leasing and portfolio-growth headlines, especially TRNO’s recent lease announcements in Doral and other markets, plus a prior property acquisition update. I don’t see a distinct fresh company-specific catalyst for STAG, so the week’s strength likely reflects the broader industrial REIT bid and sector flow rather than one major new headline.

themes.name: Bitcoin Mining & Crypto Infrastructure Operators
themes.description: CIFR is moving higher mostly on a sector sympathy rally, not company-specific news, after Hut 8 landed a second $9.8 billion AI data-center lease and IREN raised its AI/cloud revenue outlook. That reinforced the market’s view that bitcoin miners pivoting into AI infrastructure can monetize their power and data-center assets. Cipher also got a lift from bargain-hunting and positioning ahead of its Q2 earnings.

themes.name: Vacation Ownership & Timeshare Resort Recovery
themes.description: HGV, TNL, and VAC are trading higher mainly on sector-level optimism after Goldman Sachs highlighted the timeshare space and specifically cited TNL and VAC as compelling investments, improving sentiment across the group. Additionally, HGV has supportive company-specific catalysts including recent balance sheet refinancing, a term note securitization, an expanded receivables facility, and the appointment of industry veteran Christine Duffy to its board, which collectively strengthen the growth and governance narrative. Anticipation around upcoming Q2 earnings for HGV, alongside broader expectations for lodging and timeshare outperformance, is also contributing to the move.

themes.name: Korean Financial Sector Recovery
themes.description: Shinhan Financial Group (SHG) is moving higher this week primarily on the back of its FY2025 profit growth and technical breakout above the 200-day moving average, which has attracted momentum and value investors. Recent disclosures around its 2026 value-up plan, higher payout intentions, and strategic moves such as weighing a Lotte Insurance acquisition are reinforcing the rerating trend in Korean financials. Sector-wide strength in South Korean banks and improving net interest income dynamics are adding a supportive macro tailwind to the move.

themes.name: Independent Power Producers & Nuclear Generation
themes.description: VST (diversified power generation with a large nuclear fleet), TLN (wholesale electricity generation), and CEG (pure-play nuclear generation via Constellation) are all leveraged to surging U.S. power demand driven by data center electrification and AI infrastructure build-out. The catalyst is structural: utilities cannot build fast enough, putting IPPs and nuclear operators in a strong pricing position in deregulated wholesale markets. This is a distinct sub-theme from traditional utilities — these companies sell into merchant markets, not regulated rate cases.

themes.name: Custom AI Silicon & Chip Architecture Licensing
themes.description: ARM, ALAB, CRDO, and MRVL are all being pulled higher by the same macro theme: renewed risk-on flows into AI and high-speed connectivity semis as investors rotate back into AI infrastructure after a recent pullback, with strong data-center demand and optical/interconnect growth the core narrative. For MRVL specifically, the move is reinforced by bullish analyst calls and target hikes tied to its AI data center and optical interconnect exposure, plus ongoing enthusiasm around its Nvidia/AI custom silicon positioning. CRDO and ALAB are benefiting from the same AI connectivity thesis and positive analyst sentiment, with CRDO supported by very strong growth guidance and ALAB by recent target hikes highlighting CXL upside.

themes.name: Hospital & Behavioral Health Facility Procedure Volume Recovery
themes.description: U.S. hospital operators and their key device suppliers are recovering as procedure volumes normalize post-pandemic deferral backlog and labor costs stabilize. HCA and UHS (behavioral health) are facility operators directly leveraged to admission and procedure counts, while BSX (interventional cardiology devices) and THC (hospital systems) are tightly coupled to in-hospital procedure volume. Rate-sensitive capex and staffing cost relief provide a second tailwind.

themes.name: Precious Metals Miners & Royalty Streamers
themes.description: The primary catalyst is a sharp move higher in spot gold prices, which has lifted the entire gold-mining complex. Rising bullion, driven by geopolitical tensions around the U.S.–Iran situation and its implications for inflation and Fed policy, is pushing NEM, KGC, AU, GFI, HMY and AGI higher in tandem. There does not appear to be a single, stock-specific news item this week; the move is largely macro and commodity-price driven.

themes.name: Precious Metals Royalty & Streaming Companies
themes.description: The primary driver for Franco-Nevada (FNV), Royal Gold (RGLD), and Wheaton Precious Metals (WPM) this week is macro: firmer gold prices on softer Fed rate expectations and a weaker dollar, which is lifting gold-linked royalty/streaming names leveraged to the metal. Company-specific news flow for FNV has been relatively quiet and mixed (Burkina Faso stream dispute, Cobre Panamá stockpile processing approvals, record prior-quarter results), so the move is largely a sector-wide precious metals and royalty trade rather than a single headline catalyst. Earnings estimate upgrades and optimistic analyst targets for FNV add incremental support but are secondary to the gold-price and rates backdrop.

themes.name: Analog & Microcontroller Semiconductors — Automotive & Industrial Cycle Recovery
themes.description: The primary catalyst is a broad-based upturn in analog and embedded semiconductor demand, especially in industrial, automotive, and data center markets, which is driving estimate revisions and a sector-wide re-rating across ADI, MCHP, NXPI, ON, and TXN. Texas Instruments’ role as an analog bellwether, coupled with multiple analyst price target and estimate hikes ahead of its Q2 earnings, is reinforcing the view that the cyclical trough is over and that the recovery in these end-markets is sustainable. This analog/industrial recovery is being layered on top of accelerating AI data center infrastructure demand, providing a powerful combination of cyclical and structural growth drivers for the group.

themes.name: Defense Prime Contractors & Aerospace Systems
themes.description: The primary catalyst is a very strong Q2 earnings season for the defense primes, with Lockheed Martin and RTX both posting beat-and-raise quarters, record backlogs, and raised 2026 guidance tied to sustained global rearmament and Pentagon restocking of missiles and munitions. LMT and RTX’s moves are spilling over into the group, helping LHX and HII as investors rotate back into defense on the combination of robust order books, missile and space contract wins, and renewed focus on air and missile defense capabilities. A supportive macro backdrop of ongoing geopolitical tensions and U.S. defense budget visibility is reinforcing the bid across these names.

themes.name: For-Profit Education & Career Training Providers
themes.description: Workforce retraining demand from displaced workers and the ongoing push for vocational and career-focused education credentials are creating tailwinds for for-profit education operators. The correlation cluster (CVSA, LINC, PRDO, STRA) alongside existing theme members suggests broader sector-level accumulation. Community college alternatives and online degree providers share the regulatory and enrollment cycle driver.

themes.name: Automotive Components & Tire Suppliers
themes.description: Auto-retired 2026-07-30: dropped during merge/absorption (no successor found) (prior stage Fading, 2 tickers).

themes.name: US-China Tariff Truce — Consumer Goods & Digital Beneficiaries
themes.description: The announced US-China tariff de-escalation directly re-rates brands with heavy China-based manufacturing (HAS, MAT, SONO) and lifts Chinese consumer-facing digital platforms (BZ) as US-China sentiment improves and capital rotates back into Chinese ADRs — a cross-sector catalyst binding consumer leisure, tech hardware, and China internet into one trade.

themes.name: Casual Dining & Full-Service Restaurant Chain Recovery
themes.description: CAKE is trading higher this week primarily on a major Q2 earnings beat, with record revenue above $1 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.44 coming in well ahead of consensus. That print was accompanied by 5.8% same-store sales growth driven by traffic, raised full-year revenue guidance, and plans for up to 26 new restaurant openings, reinforcing the growth narrative. Additional fuel comes from bullish analyst revisions and price target hikes, plus incremental attention and traffic around National Cheesecake Day promotions.

themes.name: Traditional Staffing & Talent Placement Services
themes.description: MAN is trading higher this week primarily on the back of a strong Q2 earnings beat and a clear inflection in fundamentals, with sales and net income both swinging sharply higher year over year. Analysts have responded by boosting forecasts and raising price targets (e.g., Truist to $50), reinforcing the post-earnings move. The company’s Global Strategic Transformation Program, targeting $200 million in permanent cost savings by 2028, is also supporting sentiment as investors price in sustained margin improvement.

themes.name: Family Dining & Quick-Service Restaurant Chain Recovery
themes.description: JACK is being driven higher by a short-squeeze setup: the stock has very high short interest and is moving on renewed buying pressure, with no major company-specific news cited today. CBRL’s move this week is tied to its recent earnings beat and upbeat turnaround/guidance news, which likely keeps the name supported.

themes.name: Cloud Supply Chain & Warehouse Management Software
themes.description: MANH is being driven higher by its strong Q2 2026 earnings beat and raised full-year revenue and EPS guidance, which significantly exceeded analyst expectations and triggered a sharp re-rating in the name and broader SaaS peer group. SPSC is moving up on M&A/speculation flows tied to reports it is exploring a potential sale following activist investor pressure, with investors pricing in a takeout premium despite margin compression in the latest quarter.

themes.name: SMB & Workforce Business Services Platforms
themes.description: For LegalZoom (LZ), there is no clear positive news catalyst this week; the recent notable event was a Barclays downgrade to Underweight with a price target cut to $6 earlier this year, which has been an overhang rather than a bullish driver. For Insperity (NSP), the stock’s recent strength appears tied to ongoing labor-market resilience and expectations for solid HR outsourcing demand, but there is no single, discrete headline or corporate event this week that stands out as the primary catalyst.

themes.name: U.S. Petroleum Refining & Downstream Processing
themes.description: The main catalyst pushing VLO, PSX, MPC, PBF, PARR and DINO higher this week is a combination of rising oil prices on renewed Middle East tensions and tight global fuel supply, which are expanding refining margins and crack spreads. Sector flows are being reinforced by data showing declining U.S. crude inventories and strong expectations for Q2 refining earnings, with several of these names highlighted for outsized EPS growth and margin strength. Geopolitical supply risk plus constrained refining capacity are supporting sentiment that current elevated profitability for U.S. refiners can persist, drawing in incremental capital to the group.

themes.name: Peptide & Hormone Therapies for Metabolic & Endocrine Disorders
themes.description: XERS has been grinding higher on improved balance sheet optics and IP/asset value after its June announcement to retire $23M of convertible notes and the USPTO notice of allowance for a new KEVEYIS patent, plus some follow‑through from incremental institutional interest and media mentions. PTGX is being driven by the recent FDA approval and strong commercial/setup narrative for its partnered psoriasis drug Icotyde with J&J, associated milestone economics, and ongoing bullish sell‑side and retail sentiment around its broader pipeline. MBX is rallying on Mizuho’s recent call modeling roughly $10B in peak U.S. sales for GLP‑1 obesity candidate MBX‑4291 and a price‑target hike to $91 with an Outperform rating, while CORT strength is more generalist‑biotech rotation and expectations around its cortisol modulation franchise rather than a single discrete headline this week.

themes.name: Cloud Contact Center & CCaaS Communication Platforms
themes.description: FIVN has been driven higher by a mix of index inclusion and analyst/leadership catalysts: it was recently added to the S&P SmallCap 600, several new senior executives (including a new CTO and CSO) were appointed, and multiple brokers (Truist, Rosenblatt, Mizuho) raised/ reiterated Buy ratings and targets on improving operating leverage, AI momentum, and raised revenue guidance. RNG’s move is being fueled by sector rerating plus company-specific positives: it has benefited from being added to Russell value-oriented indexes and from renewed interest in undervalued SaaS names tied to AI platform expansion and upgrades, with the latest leg up coming after strong Q2 earnings that beat estimates and guidance was raised, reinforcing the turnaround narrative.

themes.name: Cinema Exhibition & Premium Large-Format Recovery
themes.description: CNK and IMAX are higher this week because of strong second-quarter results and bullish follow-through from analysts. Cinemark reported a big Q2 beat on revenue and earnings, while IMAX got a lift from price-target hikes after its own strong Q2 report.

themes.name: Professional Advisory & Business Services
themes.description: CRAI and CBZ are both moving higher this week on read-through from CBIZ’s announced $5 billion merger with Grant Thornton, which is driving a broad re-rating of mid-market professional services and consulting names as investors price in consolidation and M&A optionality across the peer group. CBZ is reacting directly to the Grant Thornton deal headlines, while CRAI is benefiting indirectly as a comparable consulting/advisory firm seen as a potential strategic or financial beneficiary of the same consolidation theme. There does not appear to be a separate, stock-specific CRAI catalyst beyond this sector M&A sentiment and positioning.

themes.name: Dermatology & Atopic Immunology Biologics
themes.description: APGE is moving higher on renewed enthusiasm around its CARD8-directed precision oncology platform after recent data and pipeline commentary highlighted potential first-in-class positioning and upcoming clinical catalysts, drawing incremental buy-side interest. For FBRX, the primary driver is argenx’s definitive agreement to acquire Forte Biosciences for $77 per share in cash, a roughly $2.2 billion deal that represents a sizable premium and has re-rated the stock toward the takeout price. Secondary support for FBRX comes from the earlier positive Phase 1b vitiligo data for FB102, which underpins why argenx was willing to pay that premium and reinforces investor confidence in deal completion.

themes.name: Inflammatory Disease & Immunology Biologics
themes.description: The main driver for ORKA’s strength this week is continued momentum from recent bullish analyst activity and clinical/strategic updates rather than a single fresh headline. In the past few days, multiple firms have reiterated or raised “Buy/Overweight” ratings with aggressive price targets (up to roughly $180–$200) tied to positive EVERLAST-A psoriasis trial data and an amended Paragon licensing deal plus an AbbVie-related transaction. That combination has kept Oruka in focus, with follow‑through buying and high relative volume pushing the stock higher into new 52‑week/highs territory.

themes.name: Corporate Spend, Expense Management & Financial Operations Software
themes.description: WEX is trading higher this week primarily on the back of a strong Q2 earnings beat, with revenue and EPS both coming in above consensus and highlighting resilient growth in its core fleet and payments businesses. Additional catalysts include the launch of its SecureFuel AI fraud prevention tool, which is being framed as a high-value, software-like offering for fleet customers, and follow-through from recent positive analyst revisions and price target hikes as the stock breaks out to new 52‑week highs.

themes.name: AI-Powered Enterprise Analytics & Intelligent Workflow SaaS
themes.description: AVPT is moving higher on growing enthusiasm around its AI governance/multicloud data protection offerings and related research updates, ahead of its Q2 earnings release and recent conference visibility. INTA’s strength is driven by a sharp post-earnings rerating: the stock jumped after its latest report and has continued to see follow-through buying as investors reassess growth and profitability. AMPL’s move is more technical than fundamental this week, with price action driven by short-term momentum/technical “buy” signals rather than a specific, high-profile news catalyst.

themes.name: Franchise Auto Dealership Groups
themes.description: ABG, SAH, and PAG are all trading higher this week on the back of a broader rebound in auto retail and renewed optimism around interest rates and consumer demand, rather than a single company-specific headline catalyst. For PAG specifically, the latest leg up has been driven by positive analyst commentary highlighting its commercial truck business as an underappreciated earnings driver and associated price target increases, which has lifted sector sentiment. For ABG and SAH, the move is primarily sympathy/sector rotation into auto dealers as investors reprice the group’s earnings resilience and cash generation under a more favorable macro backdrop.

themes.name: B2B Digital Financial Infrastructure & Payment Rails Modernization
themes.description: PAY (Paymentus) is being driven higher by a mix of technical and fundamental catalysts: recent Russell index inclusion, a strong rally off robust Q1 2026 earnings, and growing enthusiasm around its new AI-native “Billeo” platform. The stock is also seeing positioning ahead of its Q2 2026 earnings report scheduled for August 3, with investors and traders using this week to adjust exposure after a ~33% move over the past month. Board changes that reinforced private-equity backing have added to the positive narrative but are secondary to the index/earnings/AI-product story.

themes.name: Medical Device Mean-Reversion & Rotation Recovery
themes.description: XRAY is moving on a reported upbeat full-year revenue outlook, while CNMD is higher on Q2 earnings and revenue beating estimates and, more recently, takeover speculation. TNDM’s move appears tied to recent product/regulatory catalysts rather than a fresh headline this week, including expanded sensor compatibility and diabetes-device approvals.

themes.name: Enterprise HR & Workforce Management SaaS
themes.description: The main catalyst for WDAY and PCTY this week is broad pre-earnings positioning into their upcoming quarterly reports, with investors also rotating into enterprise software on renewed AI-monetization optimism. For Workday specifically, the move is being amplified by valuation recovery after recent weakness and a still-bullish setup around expected earnings growth.

themes.name: Office REIT Recovery & Re-Rating
themes.description: The main catalyst this week is a broad bid into beaten-down office REITs as investors rotate back into interest-rate sensitive real estate on expectations of Fed easing and stabilizing office fundamentals. Within that, BXP is getting a bump from its Q2 2026 earnings release and commentary around leasing/occupancy trends, while HIW is seeing flows linked to its recent index reclassification toward more “defensive” small-cap benchmarks. SLG and CDP are largely moving in sympathy with the group as investors reassess valuations and short interest in the office REIT complex.

themes.name: Wealth Management & Retail Brokerage Platforms
themes.description: The group is being pushed higher by a mix of upbeat firm-specific news and broker commentary, not one single sector-wide catalyst. LPLA stands out on strong advisor-satisfaction rankings and continued advisor/asset growth, while RJF is getting lift from multiple price-target increases; AMP is supported by its strong Q2 beat and recent 52-week high. SEIC and SCHW don’t have a clearly identified shared news catalyst in the provided items, so their move may be more of a broader asset-manager/brokerage sympathy bid.

themes.name: Hotel REIT Recovery & Re-Rating
themes.description: RLJ is likely moving higher on a continued hotel-REIT rerating and a new 12-month high breakout, with no company-specific fresh catalyst in the provided results beyond that technical momentum. The clearest fundamental catalyst in the group is Xenia’s raised 2026 EBITDAre and RevPAR outlook, which is lifting sentiment across lodging REITs and can spill over to RLJ.

themes.name: Life Insurance & Annuity Providers
themes.description: The main catalyst is the “higher-for-longer” interest rate narrative, which improves investment income and spreads for life insurers, making PRU, PFG, and MET more attractive. In addition, recent analyst price target increases and favorable fundamental/valuation commentary on MetLife and Prudential are drawing incremental institutional and retail interest. Sector-wide flows into defensive financials as rates back up and equities grind higher are reinforcing the move.

themes.name: Digital Payments Processing & Merchant Acquiring Networks
themes.description: PYPL is trading higher this week primarily on the back of a clean Q2 earnings beat and a full-year guidance raise, which confirmed progress in its margin and efficiency turnaround. Additional support comes from lingering takeover interest following the Stripe/Advent $60.50-per-share proposal that has reset the perceived valuation floor. FOUR is catching a bid as investors rotate into fintech/payment names leveraged to electronic transaction growth and AI/automation efficiency themes, with positive read-through from PYPL’s results and recent analyst upgrades across the space.

themes.name: Network Security & Zero-Trust Edge
themes.description: The main catalyst is a sector-wide cybersecurity rally driven by Fortinet’s stronger-than-expected quarterly results and raised guidance, which reinforced the view that demand for network and AI-driven security is robust across the group. In addition, the recent OpenAI cyberattack and heightened government warnings about Russian cyber threats have sharpened investor focus on cyber resilience, pulling capital into leading security names like PANW, CRWD, FTNT, OKTA, NET and VRNS. Analyst upgrades and positive commentary around AI-native security platforms and consolidation are amplifying the move.

themes.name: European Bank Stocks
themes.description: The main catalyst is strong European bank earnings and guidance, led by BBVA raising its 2026 profitability outlook after a Q2 beat, NatWest reporting a 20% profit increase and lifting its performance guidance, and Santander reiterating medium-term targets despite macro uncertainties. In parallel, a supportive regulatory backdrop (Bank of England moving to ease leverage rules, debate on simplifying EU banking regulation) is improving sentiment toward the sector’s capital and lending capacity. Together, this is driving a bid into European and UK banks like ING, LYG, BBVA, BCS, SAN, and NWG as investors position for sustained higher returns and buybacks.

themes.name: Life Science Tools & Analytical Instruments
themes.description: The main driver is a sector-wide bid into tools and life science instrumentation on improving biopharma and research-spend sentiment, which is lifting WAT, MTD, and TMO together as part of the same peer group. For TMO specifically, the move is being reinforced by its stronger-than-expected Q1 2026 results, ongoing benefits from the Clario acquisition, and a series of manufacturing and collaboration announcements that support the outsourcing and clinical-services growth narrative. There is no single, stock-specific headline this week; it’s more a rotation back into high-quality life science suppliers after a weak first half.

themes.name: Industrial HVAC, Plumbing & Fabricated Copper Products
themes.description: The main catalyst is CSW Industrials’ fiscal Q1 2027 earnings release this week, with the market focused on whether MARS Parts/Aspen synergy realization and segment growth can support further EPS and cash-flow upside. A secondary driver is the stock trading ex-dividend for the newly declared $0.30 quarterly dividend, which has drawn income-focused interest. Together, these events are reinforcing the broader positive narrative around CSW’s recent $1B acquisition spree and profitable scale-up, pushing the name higher.

themes.name: Uniform Rental & Managed Workwear Services
themes.description: CTAS is being bid up ahead of its upcoming Q4/FY26 earnings webcast, with investors positioning on the back of strong multi‑year returns and expectations for another solid print and potential guidance support. VSTS is trading higher as investors re-rate the name on its strong year-to-date performance and continued post-spin recovery in the workwear/uniform rental space, with no single discrete news headline this week but ongoing sentiment and analyst focus driving flows.

themes.name: Domestic Steel Producers
themes.description: The main catalyst pushing Nucor (NUE) and Steel Dynamics (STLD) higher this week is continued strength in U.S. steel pricing, especially hot-rolled coil, driven by tight supply, reduced imports under higher tariffs, and robust demand. That macro backdrop is being reinforced by prior Q1 earnings beats and bullish guidance (particularly from NUE) plus ongoing analyst target upgrades that highlight upside from reshoring, infrastructure, and AI-related construction spending. In STLD’s case, incremental optimism around flat-rolled demand and its new Sinton mill and aluminum capacity adds stock-specific momentum on top of the sector tailwind.

themes.name: Commercial Real Estate Brokerage & Advisory Services
themes.description: JLL and CBRE are being lifted mainly by strong Q2 2026 earnings beats with raised full-year guidance, which reinforced the case for a recovery in commercial real estate activity. For JLL, the catalyst was an especially strong advisory/leasing rebound and higher EPS guidance; for CBRE, the market is also reacting to outsized growth in data center and infrastructure services tied to AI demand.

themes.name: Cloud Observability & AIOps Monitoring Platforms
themes.description: For Datadog (DDOG), the main catalyst this week is renewed AI and cloud-observability enthusiasm driven by bullish analyst actions, including Benchmark lifting its price target to a street-high $330 and multiple upgrades/positive notes from firms like Zacks highlighting AI-led growth and strong momentum ahead of the August 6 earnings. In addition, sentiment has been reinforced by coverage of its Q1 beat-and-raise, >$1B quarterly revenue, and the acquisition of AI startup Adaptive ML, all feeding the “AI infrastructure winner” narrative. For PagerDuty (PD), the move higher is being driven primarily by sympathy flows into observability/devops names and positioning ahead of its own earnings, with investors rotating back into high-quality software names leveraged to AI and cloud operations rather than any single, stock-specific headline this week.

themes.name: Containerboard & Corrugated Packaging Producers
themes.description: PKG, IP, and SW are being lifted mainly by a sector rerate after containerboard pricing turned upward, with reports of price increases supporting better earnings expectations for box makers. For PKG specifically, the big catalyst this week was its Q2 beat plus a new containerboard price hike, which helped push the stock to record highs. IP and SW are also catching the same industry tailwind from improving containerboard pricing.

themes.name: Hospital & Behavioral Health Facility Procedure Volume Recovery
themes.description: The main catalyst pushing UHS and THC higher this week is strong fundamental news: both reported better‑than‑expected quarterly earnings with solid revenue growth and raised or reinforced full‑year outlooks, which is driving a re‑rating of the hospital/acute care group. For UHS specifically, the July 27 Q2 print showed EPS and revenues up year over year plus an updated 2026 forecast, while Tenet (THC) is benefiting from recent upside earnings revisions, a credit rating upgrade, and Q2 results that materially beat consensus. Broader sector tailwinds from favorable Medicare/CMS payment expectations and supportive analyst commentary are adding momentum to both names.

themes.name: Private Mortgage Insurance
themes.description: The main catalyst is a strong fundamental backdrop for U.S. mortgage insurers: cooling but still-stable credit trends, resilient housing prices, and solid capital positions, which together are supporting higher valuations for ESNT, NMIH, MTG, and RDN this week. In addition, Essent specifically is benefiting from bullish sentiment around its earnings trajectory and options activity pointing to expectations of further upside, which is spilling over into the group. Overall, the move is being driven more by sector-level macro/housing and credit conditions than by a single, stock-specific headline for all four names.

themes.name: Clinical-Stage Oncology Biotech
themes.description: ELVN is being driven higher this week by continued enthusiasm around its updated Phase 1 ENABLE trial data for ELVN-001 in previously treated chronic myeloid leukemia, which clarified an FDA-aligned path toward Phase 3 and boosted perceived approval odds. That clinical momentum is reinforced by the recently completed ~$460M upsized equity offering, which de-risks funding for development, and by multiple analyst price target hikes (into the mid‑60s to $70 range) following the data update. TGTX strength is tied to positive Phase 3 ENHANCE trial results for its multiple sclerosis therapy, supporting its commercial trajectory and sentiment across the hematology/oncology and neurology space.

themes.name: Global Crude & Product Tanker Fleet Operators
themes.description: The main catalyst is a broad move higher in crude and product tanker names on continued strength in spot freight rates and expectations of tighter tonnage supply into late 2026, helped by ongoing geopolitical disruptions to trade routes. For DHT and FRO specifically, investors are also leaning into VLCC exposure after commentary and research arguing these fleets are still undervalued relative to forward earnings power and rate upside. The rest of the group (TRMD, NAT, TNK, INSW) is riding the same sector bid as the market prices in sustained high dayrates, strong cash generation, and elevated dividend capacity rather than any single stock-specific headline this week.

themes.name: Industrial Construction Execution & On-Site Supply Chain
themes.description: TPC is being driven higher mainly by its upcoming inclusion in the S&P SmallCap 600, which has triggered index-buying demand and momentum following earlier strength from a large Guam defense contract and solid backlog. DNOW’s move appears tied more to sector rotation into energy/industrial distributors and leverage to higher oil-related activity rather than a single stock-specific headline this week. RYZ is reacting to its second-quarter earnings release and a new quarterly dividend declaration, which together provided the clearest direct fundamental catalyst among the three.

themes.name: Cloud Data Storage & Analytics Infrastructure
themes.description: BLZE is being driven higher by renewed enthusiasm around its large AI cloud storage partnership with CoreWeave, which investors view as a transformative growth catalyst for Backblaze’s revenue and positioning in the AI infrastructure space. That CoreWeave deal, plus subsequent analyst upgrades and price target raises highlighting a stronger long-term outlook, continue to underpin bullish sentiment this week. SNOW is benefiting from ongoing AI/data-cloud momentum, positive analyst target hikes, and news flow around its expanding AI ecosystem and international growth, which together are supporting the stock’s strength.

themes.name: Department Store Retail Recovery
themes.description: DDS is likely being lifted by Dillard’s strong Q1 report and sales beat, plus the shareholder approval of its merger/corporate restructuring, which has kept the stock in focus. KSS is moving on company-specific operating-news momentum, including the recent COO appointment and other turnaround-related headlines, but I do not see a single fresh catalyst in the provided results that clearly explains this week’s move.

themes.name: Asset Management & Fund Administration Platform Ecosystem
themes.description: SS&C Technologies (SSNC) is higher this week because of its strong Q2 2026 earnings beat, with revenue up 10.3% year over year, adjusted EPS up 18%, and management raising full-year guidance. The move is also being reinforced by a record $499 million quarterly buyback and upbeat commentary around AI-driven automation and acquisitions.

themes.name: U.S. Passenger Airlines
themes.description: The main catalyst pushing SKYW, UAL, and DAL higher this week is the sharp drop in oil/jet fuel prices following de-escalation and a preliminary U.S.–Iran deal that is easing Strait of Hormuz and broader geopolitical risk, materially improving the sector’s fuel-cost outlook. On top of that macro tailwind, SKYW is getting a stock-specific boost from its Q2 report, expanded American Airlines E175 flying agreement, and enlarged buyback, while UAL and DAL are benefiting from better‑than‑feared Q2 results, raised guidance/record revenue, and ongoing positive sentiment toward the large U.S. network carriers. Consolidation chatter (United–Delta talks that went nowhere) is adding a bit of speculative support but is secondary to the fuel-price relief and earnings beats.

themes.name: Industrial Fluid Control, Filtration & Water Infrastructure Equipment
themes.description: IEX (IDEX Corp) and FELE (Franklin Electric) are being bid up mainly on anticipation of solid Q2 earnings and guidance, with pre-earnings research highlighting resilient industrial and water-related demand trends. DCI (Donaldson) is benefiting from a rotation into industrial cyclicals and ongoing optimism around filtration demand and margin improvement ahead of its next results. IR (Ingersoll Rand) is moving higher on continued positive sentiment around industrial automation/compressed air exposure and follow-through from recent analyst target hikes and institutional accumulation.

themes.name: Property & Casualty Insurance Underwriters
themes.description: This week’s strength across HCI, CB, CINF, HIG, ORI, and AFG is being driven primarily by a broad bid into property & casualty insurers on the back of improving loss trends, solid investment income with higher-for-longer rates, and expectations for strong Q2 earnings and capital returns in the group. Stock‑specific tailwinds include HCI’s recent inclusion in Russell value/defensive indices that is bringing in benchmark and quant flows, and ongoing dividend growth plus earnings momentum stories at names like CINF that reinforce the sector’s “defensive value” narrative. No single company-specific headline is dominating; it’s largely a sector‑wide rerating theme tied to fundamentals and factor rotation.

themes.name: Insurance Brokerage & Distribution Services
themes.description: The main catalyst is sector-wide positive sentiment on insurance brokers following a bullish Zacks industry outlook highlighting improved pricing, underwriting, rising insurance demand, and consolidation benefits for AJG, AON, and BRO. In addition, investors are positioning ahead of Aon’s upcoming earnings, where the Street expects year-over-year EPS and revenue growth with a high probability of another beat, reinforcing the group’s premium-multiple narrative. Recent and ongoing M&A activity across the space (AJG’s specialty and Canadian acquisitions, BRO’s retail brokerage expansion, AON’s NFP deal) is also supporting the move higher as investors reward scalable consolidation stories.

themes.name: U.S. Apparel & Fashion Recovery
themes.description: RVLV is grinding higher into its August 4 earnings on expectations of continued double‑digit revenue growth and margin expansion after its last quarterly beat, with some support from recent analyst bullishness and “moderate buy” ratings. CROX is benefiting from a post‑earnings reset where EPS beat lowered near‑term fears, plus incremental buzz around brand collaborations like Tim Hortons that reinforce the durability of the clog franchise. UA is moving as part of a broader rebound in consumer/athletic retail on better macro data and short covering ahead of its own next guidance update, rather than a single, stock‑specific headline this week.

themes.name: U.S. Regional & Mid-Cap Commercial Banks
themes.description: Regional banks including UMBF, ZION, SSB, HWC, PNC, and TFC are moving higher this week primarily on strong regional bank earnings prints and better-than-feared credit quality, which are reinforcing the “soft landing” and stable-NIM narrative for the group. UMBF specifically reported a sizable Q2 beat on EPS and revenue driven by broad loan growth, stronger fee income, and solid capital, which is spilling over as a read-across to peers. The move is being supported by a relatively stable rate backdrop and ongoing rotation into financials as investors look for value and cyclicals into the back half of the year.

themes.name: Senior & Long-Term Care Healthcare REITs
themes.description: OHI and VTR are being driven higher primarily by strong earnings beats and reaffirmed growth in senior housing and healthcare real estate fundamentals, with OHI’s Q2 results topping consensus on accretive investment activity and VTR’s recent beat and raised full-year guidance reinforcing the sector’s recovery. Broader rate and macro backdrop this week (central bank decisions, stabilizing long-end yields, and risk-on sentiment) is also supporting defensive, income-oriented healthcare REITs as a group. LTC is participating largely as a sympathy move within the senior housing/healthcare REIT complex, supported by prior positive catalysts (SHOP expansion, dividend stability) but without a distinct new company-specific headline this week.

themes.name: Canadian Big Banks
themes.description: The main catalyst pushing CM, TD, BNS, RY, and BMO higher this week is a broad rotation into “safety” and dividend yield, with investors bidding up Canadian bank stocks to historically elevated P/E multiples as defensives outperform in a volatile market. There are also supportive stock-specific tailwinds, including fresh analyst optimism and target hikes on TD, and new product launches and fund initiatives at RBC that reinforce the sector’s stable growth and fee-income narrative. Overall, the move is sentiment-driven and macro (defensive, income-oriented positioning) rather than a single discrete news event for any one bank.

themes.name: Truckload & LTL Freight Carriers
themes.description: ArcBest (ARCB) is being driven higher by bullish analyst actions this week, including new coverage with an outperform rating and multiple price target hikes tied to a perceived end to the multi‑year trucking downturn and strong pre‑earnings revenue/tonnage trends. Hub Group (HUBG) and Schneider (SNDR) are moving with the broader freight/trucking group on the same “freight recovery” narrative and rotation into truckload/intermodal names ahead of earnings, as investors position for improving pricing power and volume. There is no company‑specific positive news for HUBG this week; its move is largely sector beta against that recovery theme despite ongoing accounting‑probe overhang.

themes.name: Cyber Exposure Management & Vulnerability Assessment
themes.description: The main catalyst is a broad cybersecurity bid after a high‑profile joint CISA/NSA/FBI advisory this week warning of intensified Russian state‑sponsored cyberattacks on critical infrastructure, which is pulling vulnerability‑management names like Tenable (TENB), Qualys (QLYS), and Rapid7 (RPD) higher as defensive plays. In addition, TENB is still benefiting from follow‑through on its recent FedRAMP High/IL5 cloud clearance and strong Q2 print/raised guidance, which reinforces the sector narrative and multiple for the group.

themes.name: Open-Air & Strip Mall Retail REITs
themes.description: The main driver is a sector-wide bid into open‑air shopping center and strip‑center REITs on the back of falling long-term yields and a defensive rotation into income-oriented real assets. For these specific names, incremental support is coming from index inclusion/flows (KIM’s addition to Russell 1000 defensive/value indexes), rising expectations into Q2 earnings (KRG, PECO and peers), and generally positive leasing/fundamentals commentary from recent REIT and ICSC/NAREIT conference appearances. There is no single stock-specific headline this week moving just one of KRG, FRT, KIM, SKT, BRX, or PECO; they are trading as a group on the macro rate/defensive and earnings-setup narrative.

themes.name: IT Distribution & Technology Services Providers
themes.description: INGM is moving higher mainly on an earnings-driven re‑rating: consensus estimates and “Most Accurate” estimates have been revised up, Zacks upgraded the name to Strong Buy, and the stock is benefiting from positive AI and cloud news (including an Oracle Cloud distribution program) that supports a higher fair value and targets. EFOR’s strength this week is tied to its recent 8‑K filing detailing a new material agreement and financial obligation plus upbeat company news flow, including government contract-related recognition and management share purchases, which together signal improved fundamentals and leadership confidence.

themes.name: Online Insurance Comparison & Digital Marketplace Platforms
themes.description: MAX EVER’s strength this week is being driven primarily by company-specific news: MediaAlpha (MAX) is rallying into its scheduled Q2 2026 earnings release, which is increasing speculation about improved profitability and a continued recovery in insurance customer acquisition spending. Separately, Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions (often tagged as MAX EVER/Max Ever in some feeds) recently hit an all-time high after announcing a major renewable energy partnership with Meta to build 837 MW of solar and wind capacity, with Meta buying all green attributes from these projects, which remains a key sentiment tailwind. Broadly supportive AI- and tech-led equity momentum is providing a constructive backdrop but is secondary to these direct catalysts.

themes.name: Consumer Staples Packaged Food & Snack Brand Recovery
themes.description: LW is trading higher this week mainly on anticipation around its July 24th Q4/FY26 earnings release and Starboard Value’s activist involvement pushing for an Investor Day and a 25% EBITDA margin target by FY2029. There is also a defensive bid as investors focus on operational efficiency moves like the planned closure of the Broekhuizenvorst, Netherlands plant and cost-savings/capex discipline highlighted in recent results and guidance. CAG’s move higher is being driven by value and yield interest after the stock crossed a double‑digit dividend yield, alongside insider buying and a new CEO that is prompting a contrarian turnaround narrative despite recent negative sentiment and estimate cuts.

themes.name: Enterprise Server, Storage & Data Infrastructure Hardware
themes.description: The common driver is a renewed leg of the AI infrastructure/server trade, with upside read‑through from Super Micro’s record AI server orders and Dell’s own blowout AI server results and analyst target hikes, which are lifting the whole enterprise hardware complex. For DELL specifically, investors are chasing its AI server growth story after historic AI-optimized server revenue, strong guidance and fresh price target raises. For HPE and NTAP, the move is largely sympathy/sector rotation into AI data center, storage, and server names as investors extrapolate the same tight capacity and accelerating AI infrastructure demand theme.

themes.name: US-China Tariff Truce — Consumer Goods & Digital Beneficiaries
themes.description: The announced US-China tariff de-escalation directly re-rates brands with heavy China-based manufacturing (HAS, MAT, SONO) and lifts Chinese consumer-facing digital platforms (BZ) as US-China sentiment improves and capital rotates back into Chinese ADRs — a cross-sector catalyst binding consumer leisure, tech hardware, and China internet into one trade.

themes.name: Global Steel & Metal Producers Recovery
themes.description: The main catalyst is this week’s Federal Reserve meeting and rate decision, which is driving positioning across markets and supporting metals prices ahead of Powell’s press conference. A softer oil backdrop after the U.S.-Iran de-escalation is also helping the risk tone and easing inflation pressure.

themes.name: AI-Augmented Business Process Outsourcing & IT Services
themes.description: EXLS G’s move higher this week is being driven primarily by follow-through from its stronger-than-expected recent quarterly earnings, which showed double-digit revenue and EPS growth and came with a raised full-year outlook. Management increased guidance for both revenue and adjusted EPS, reinforcing the growth story and sustaining momentum in the stock after the initial post-earnings surge. There is no new single-day headline catalyst this week; it’s an extension of the positive earnings/guide and AI-focused strategic narrative already in place.

themes.name: Smart Home Security & Comfort Systems
themes.description: Resideo (REZI) and Alarm.com (ALRM) have been moving higher primarily on company‑specific and structural catalysts rather than a single discrete headline this week. For REZI, the key drivers are the ongoing ADI spin-off process and related unsecured notes offering, plus accumulation by institutions such as Arrowstreet Capital and a still‑constructive Street view with upside to consensus targets. For ALRM, the move is largely sympathy and sector read‑through, as investors reposition into home security and smart‑home names that benefit from Resideo’s restructuring and improving sentiment in connected‑home/security peers.

themes.name: For-Profit & Vocational Post-Secondary Education Operators
themes.description: The primary catalyst this week is sector-specific: U.S. for-profit and career education names are catching a bid on renewed M&A/speculation and follow-through from Laureate’s announced $1.48B sale of Walden University to Adtalem, which has re-rated the group and highlighted embedded asset value across education franchises. Laureate (LAUR) is moving directly on that transaction headline, while peers LINC, LOPE, PRDO, STRA, and UTI are riding sympathy/rotation into education and training plays as investors position for consolidation and structurally higher demand for upskilling and non-traditional postsecondary programs. There is no single new company-specific print this week across all of them; it is a group move driven by that deal, prior positive expansion/earnings commentary, and thematic flows into the education/training space.

themes.name: B2B Marketing Automation & Customer Engagement SaaS
themes.description: HubSpot (HUBS) is trading higher on renewed AI enthusiasm around its CRM and marketing automation platform, with investors rotating back into AI-enabled software following positive megacap AI sentiment. Klaviyo (KVYO) is being bid up on accelerating revenue growth, record operating margins, raised full-year guidance, and an expanded share buyback program, which collectively signal improving profitability and stronger management confidence. Broader AI sector strength and CRM automation headlines are reinforcing the move in both names.

themes.name: Financial Compliance & Regulatory Reporting SaaS
themes.description: DFIN is catching a bid on the back of a recent institutional buy disclosure from Fifth Third Bancorp, which increased its stake and highlighted DFIN’s better‑than‑expected earnings, strong recurring revenue profile, and Buy‑rated analyst backdrop. WK is moving higher on its own strong earnings print and bullish 2026 outlook that came out this week, which is driving follow‑through buying in cloud/compliance names. Together, the combination of positive fundamental news and supportive analyst sentiment is the key catalyst for both names.

themes.name: Molecular Diagnostics & DNA-Based Genetic Testing
themes.description: QGEN is likely moving on a mix of recent corporate/news flow and positioning, especially Qiagen’s June 27 addition to the Russell 1000 Dynamic Index and the recent Goldman Sachs disclosure of a 3.65% voting interest. There’s also some support from recent analyst coverage/news such as Kepler’s Hold rating and the IngenuitySystems acquisition headline, but the Russell-index inclusion appears to be the clearest catalyst.

themes.name: Copper Mining & Production
themes.description: The main catalyst is a broad copper rally driven by stronger China industrial data, AI-related infrastructure demand, and renewed tariff/reshoring narratives that are pushing base metals and copper miners higher across the board. At the stock level, sentiment is being reinforced by recent positive operating/earnings commentary for copper producers (e.g., TECK’s output and government-support news) and a wave of analyst target hikes and “outperform” style pieces on smaller copper names like TGB, which is pulling up the whole group. There is no single company-specific headline this week; it’s a sector-wide copper theme that is lifting SCCO, HBM, FCX, and TGB simultaneously.

themes.name: Cruise Line & Ocean Travel Recovery
themes.description: NCLH and RCL are higher mainly on a broad cruise-sector rally after reports of a pause in U.S.-Iran hostilities pushed oil prices down, which eases fuel-cost pressure on cruise lines. NCLH is also getting an added lift from pre-earnings positioning ahead of its July 30 Q2 report, with investors looking for a potential beat and better cruise-demand commentary.

themes.name: Specialty Insurance Underwriting & Brokerage
themes.description: PLMR is moving higher on the back of raised 2026 adjusted net income guidance and a subsequent wave of positive commentary highlighting upside to earnings and price targets. RYAN is being supported by the recently expanded $600 million share repurchase authorization and disclosure of significant institutional buying (e.g., Fenimore Asset Management increasing its stake by over 80%), which together signal strong management and investor confidence.

themes.name: Tax Preparation & Consumer Financial Software Platforms
themes.description: INTU is moving higher this week primarily on follow-through from strong fiscal Q3 results and raised full-year revenue and earnings guidance, plus renewed focus on its longer-term growth story after a recent selloff. The launch of a new QuickBooks-integrated business credit card and expanded AI/strategic partnerships (including Anthropic and FedNow) are reinforcing the small-business ecosystem and improving sentiment. HRB’s move appears more modest, with the main recent catalyst being Stephens initiating coverage at Equal Weight with a $47 price target, which has put some incremental attention on the name.

themes.name: Defense Precision Components & Mission-Critical Subsystems
themes.description: Hexcel (HXL) is being bid up on aerospace optimism following its long-term composite materials partnership with Deutsche Aircraft for the D328eco regional turboprop, which has refocused investors on secular demand from next-gen commercial and defense platforms. Frequency Electronics (FEIM) is moving higher on the back of its July 23 announcement of approximately $18 million in new satellite contract awards, plus attention around its recent Q4 earnings call and contract win headlines.

themes.name: U.S. Apparel & Lifestyle Brand Recovery
themes.description: VSXY is being driven higher by ongoing enthusiasm around Victoria’s Secret’s turnaround story: strong Q1 earnings, raised FY26 guidance, and persistent short-covering/ momentum following the recent proxy victory and operational improvements, with no new single headline this week but continued bullish coverage and product/newsflow (e.g., PINK launches) keeping buyers engaged. OXM’s strength appears more technical than fundamental this week, as the stock rebounds from prior weakness and benefits from a positive short-term setup and improving sentiment in discretionary/apparel names, rather than a specific fresh company-level news catalyst.

themes.name: Consumer Fintech & Digital Credit Platforms
themes.description: Sezzle (SEZL) is being driven higher by a combination of strong growth fundamentals and capital return: recent reports highlight rapid revenue and EPS growth, attractive valuation metrics, and a new or expanded stock repurchase authorization that signals management’s confidence in the business. For Dave (DAVE), the main recent catalyst has been a shareholder vote tied to corporate actions, with the stock continuing to trade within its high-volatility uptrend supported by strong multi‑year revenue and margin expansion rather than a specific fresh news event this week.

themes.name: Industrial & Logistics REITs
themes.description: The move looks fundamentally driven by leasing and portfolio-growth headlines, especially TRNO’s recent lease announcements in Doral and other markets, plus a prior property acquisition update. I don’t see a distinct fresh company-specific catalyst for STAG, so the week’s strength likely reflects the broader industrial REIT bid and sector flow rather than one major new headline.

themes.name: Branded Packaged Food & Consumer Staples Producers
themes.description: CPB is up on defensive rotation into staples plus modestly positive sentiment around its steady earnings profile and pricing power, rather than a specific, stock‑specific headline. GIS is being driven higher by its recent fiscal Q4 beat, a large cost‑savings plan through 2030, and product innovation messaging that improved earnings and margin expectations. KHC strength is tied to its new multiyear Disney alliance expanding distribution and licensing opportunities, layered on top of restructuring, product launches, and positioning ahead of its upcoming earnings print.

themes.name: U.S. Multifamily & Residential Apartment REITs
themes.description: The main catalyst is the announced “merger of equals” between AvalonBay Communities (AVB) and Equity Residential (EQR), which is lifting multifamily REITs broadly and pulling closely correlated peers CPT, MAA, and UDR higher alongside sector optimism. In addition, improving multifamily fundamentals (strong national absorption, stabilizing rents/occupancy) and the read-through from recent earnings and guidance for these names are reinforcing the move as investors re-rate the apartment REIT group. Correlation data show these tickers tend to move in lockstep, so strength in AVB/EQR is mechanically supporting CPT, MAA, and UDR.

themes.name: Bitcoin Mining & Crypto Infrastructure Operators
themes.description: CIFR is moving higher mostly on a sector sympathy rally, not company-specific news, after Hut 8 landed a second $9.8 billion AI data-center lease and IREN raised its AI/cloud revenue outlook. That reinforced the market’s view that bitcoin miners pivoting into AI infrastructure can monetize their power and data-center assets. Cipher also got a lift from bargain-hunting and positioning ahead of its Q2 earnings.

themes.name: Powersports & Recreational Vehicle Manufacturers
themes.description: Harley-Davidson (HOG) is being driven higher mainly by a bullish analyst shift and earnings setup: Loop Capital upgraded the stock to Buy with a higher $32 target, and investors are positioning ahead of its Q2 print and a new financing partnership for HDFS. Polaris (PII) is moving on Bank of America’s positive earnings preview, with estimates held near the high end of full-year guidance and expectations for solid upcoming results for the powersports group.

themes.name: Vacation Ownership & Timeshare Resort Recovery
themes.description: HGV, TNL, and VAC are trading higher mainly on sector-level optimism after Goldman Sachs highlighted the timeshare space and specifically cited TNL and VAC as compelling investments, improving sentiment across the group. Additionally, HGV has supportive company-specific catalysts including recent balance sheet refinancing, a term note securitization, an expanded receivables facility, and the appointment of industry veteran Christine Duffy to its board, which collectively strengthen the growth and governance narrative. Anticipation around upcoming Q2 earnings for HGV, alongside broader expectations for lodging and timeshare outperformance, is also contributing to the move.

themes.name: Korean Financial Sector Recovery
themes.description: Shinhan Financial Group (SHG) is moving higher this week primarily on the back of its FY2025 profit growth and technical breakout above the 200-day moving average, which has attracted momentum and value investors. Recent disclosures around its 2026 value-up plan, higher payout intentions, and strategic moves such as weighing a Lotte Insurance acquisition are reinforcing the rerating trend in Korean financials. Sector-wide strength in South Korean banks and improving net interest income dynamics are adding a supportive macro tailwind to the move.

themes.name: Precious Metals Miners & Royalty Streamers
themes.description: The primary catalyst is a sharp move higher in spot gold prices, which has lifted the entire gold-mining complex. Rising bullion, driven by geopolitical tensions around the U.S.–Iran situation and its implications for inflation and Fed policy, is pushing NEM, KGC, AU, GFI, HMY and AGI higher in tandem. There does not appear to be a single, stock-specific news item this week; the move is largely macro and commodity-price driven.

themes.name: Precious Metals Royalty & Streaming Companies
