themes.description: I’m only seeing a clear company-news catalyst for CMCO: Columbus McKinnon has been trading higher on no obvious fresh headline, and the move looks more like a broad industrials/small-cap rebound than a specific company announcement. I’m not seeing a direct news driver for HRI either in the provided results.

themes.name: Enterprise HR & Workforce Management SaaS
themes.description: WDAY is being driven higher by a combination of pre-earnings positioning ahead of its late-August report, where Street models strong EPS growth, and a perceived valuation disconnect versus analyst targets alongside renewed enthusiasm for its AI-driven enterprise software story. PCTY is moving up on sector sympathy and improving sentiment toward cloud HCM/payroll names as investors rotate back into profitable SaaS and workforce-management plays, rather than on a single company-specific headline.

themes.name: Asset Management & Fund Administration Platform Ecosystem
themes.description: SS&C (SSNC) is moving higher on the back of strong Q2 results that beat expectations and came with raised full‑year revenue and EPS guidance, driving a repricing of the earnings and growth outlook. In addition, the stock is still reacting to late‑July news of a US$779m ESOP‑linked shelf registration following solid Q2 revenue and profit growth, which has drawn incremental institutional and media attention. Blackstone (BX) strength this week is more flow/sector driven rather than a specific fresh company‑level catalyst, with investors rotating into alternative asset managers on continued optimism about private credit and alternatives earnings leverage.

themes.name: U.S. Domestic Steel Producers
themes.description: The main catalyst pushing Nucor (NUE) and Steel Dynamics (STLD) higher this week is strengthening U.S. steel fundamentals, particularly the rebound in hot-rolled coil prices toward roughly $1,200/ton on tight supply, tariffs, and reduced imports, which improves pricing power and earnings visibility for domestic steelmakers. In addition, STLD just reported record Q2 2026 results driven by strong shipments and higher realized prices, while NUE is benefiting from positive analyst commentary and upgrades tied to its positioning in this tariff-supported environment. Investor positioning is rotating back into U.S. steel producers on the view that rising prices and disciplined capacity set up continued margin strength into the back half of 2026.

themes.name: Consumer Fintech & Digital Credit Platforms
themes.description: SEZL is higher this week mainly on momentum after hitting a fresh 52-week high, with traders also positioning ahead of its upcoming Q2 earnings report. DAVE is being lifted by a similar momentum trade, as it also reached a new 52-week high and investors are buying into continued business/earnings strength.

themes.name: Franchise Auto Dealership Groups
themes.description: PAG is moving higher on the back of a clean Q2 earnings beat, with revenue and adjusted EPS both coming in ahead of consensus and highlighting strength across automotive retail, commercial trucks, and service/parts. That report hit just after Penske Corporation and Mitsui submitted a non-binding proposal to acquire the remaining ~27% of PAG at $210 per share, keeping a potential take-private and deal upside front and center. Layered on top, multiple Wall Street firms have raised price targets and reiterated bullish views, reinforcing the perception that the buyout offer undervalues PAG and helping sustain upside momentum.

themes.name: Defense ISR & Unmanned Systems Intelligence
themes.description: HAWK (HawkEye 360) and AVEX (AEVEX Corp.) are both catching a bid on fresh defense and national security contract wins, with AVEX specifically rallying on the announcement of $88.1 million in new long‑range precision strike production orders from U.S. government customers. That award reinforces the broader geospatial/intelligence and defense-contracting theme, which is drawing incremental investor flows into names like HawkEye 360 alongside AVEX.

themes.name: Life Science Tools & Analytical Instruments
themes.description: TMO’s month‑to‑date strength is being driven primarily by its latest earnings beat and the decision to raise full‑year organic revenue growth guidance, which signaled improving biopharma demand and a stronger backlog. Additional support comes from a series of positive collaboration and partnership headlines (e.g., Arcturus mRNA/CF partnership, AustinPx KinetiSol collaboration, Nuvation Bio lung cancer work), reinforcing its role as a key tools and services provider into high‑growth therapeutics and clinical trials. A broadly bullish backdrop for the clinical trials and life sciences market is adding a sector tailwind to the move.

themes.name: U.S. Government/Defense Spending Surge
themes.description: All four are capturing accelerating government contract revenue: Palantir's U.S. government revenue grew 90% YoY, Telesat signed a transformative $2.3B CAD 15-year military satcom contract, Voyager reported record bookings and backlog with a raised defense-contract-driven outlook, and Ameresco's record project awards include significant government energy infrastructure work.

themes.name: Canadian Big Banks
themes.description: The main catalyst pushing TD, RY, CM, BNS, and BMO higher this week is a sector-wide bid into Canadian banks driven by improving sentiment on bank earnings, capital returns, and a more supportive regulatory backdrop, including the recent cut to the domestic stability buffer to spur lending. Investors are rotating into large Canadian financials as macro fears around credit quality and rate cuts ease, while strong recent quarters (profit growth, dividend hikes, and solid capital markets/wealth revenues) reinforce the “quality income” thesis for the group. Flows into TSX financials and the banks’ near-52-week-high technical momentum are amplifying the move.

themes.name: Senior & Long-Term Care Healthcare REITs
themes.description: OHI and VTR are being driven higher primarily by strong earnings beats and reaffirmed growth in senior housing and healthcare real estate fundamentals, with OHI’s Q2 results topping consensus on accretive investment activity and VTR’s recent beat and raised full-year guidance reinforcing the sector’s recovery. Broader rate and macro backdrop this week (central bank decisions, stabilizing long-end yields, and risk-on sentiment) is also supporting defensive, income-oriented healthcare REITs as a group. LTC is participating largely as a sympathy move within the senior housing/healthcare REIT complex, supported by prior positive catalysts (SHOP expansion, dividend stability) but without a distinct new company-specific headline this week.

themes.name: Smart Home Security & Comfort Systems
themes.description: Resideo (REZI) and Alarm.com (ALRM) have been moving higher primarily on company‑specific and structural catalysts rather than a single discrete headline this week. For REZI, the key drivers are the ongoing ADI spin-off process and related unsecured notes offering, plus accumulation by institutions such as Arrowstreet Capital and a still‑constructive Street view with upside to consensus targets. For ALRM, the move is largely sympathy and sector read‑through, as investors reposition into home security and smart‑home names that benefit from Resideo’s restructuring and improving sentiment in connected‑home/security peers.

themes.name: Electrical Infrastructure Products & Systems Installation
themes.description: ATKR is being driven higher by news that it agreed to merge with Italy’s Prysmian in a $3.8 billion deal to create a larger electrification and AI data-center infrastructure player. The stock is also reacting to strong quarterly results that beat earnings and revenue expectations, reinforcing the strategic rationale for the transaction.

themes.name: Professional Advisory & Business Services
themes.description: CBIZ (CBZ) is trading sharply higher this week on news that Grant Thornton Advisors LLC agreed to acquire the company in an all‑cash transaction valued at about $5 billion, with CBZ shareholders set to receive $55 per share, a sizable premium to recent trading levels. The announced buyout has driven CBZ toward its biggest single‑day gain in over two decades and a six‑month high. For CRA International (CRAI), the move higher is primarily tied to strong recent fundamentals and record revenue highlighted around its latest earnings, alongside ongoing positive analyst sentiment, rather than a single discrete news headline this week.

themes.name: Electrical Connectivity & Utility Network Hardware
themes.description: PLPC is trading higher this week on the back of a massive Q2 earnings beat and record financial results reported on July 29, with EPS and revenue coming in far above Street expectations. The company posted 25% year-over-year sales growth, 32% U.S. sales growth, margin expansion, and highlighted incremental growth from its Delta Star acquisition, all of which have driven a repricing of the stock higher. There is no single new headline this week; the move is an ongoing reaction to that strong quarterly print and outlook commentary.

themes.name: Global Crude & Product Tanker Fleet Operators
themes.description: The primary catalyst is a sharp move higher in spot and forward tanker rates driven by renewed geopolitical tensions and disruptions in key oil shipping lanes, which is lifting the entire crude and product tanker complex. In parallel, several bullish sell-side pieces and upgrades on VLCC and mid-size tanker names (including DHT and Teekay) are highlighting strong cash generation, low leverage, and still-attractive valuations, drawing in momentum and macro oil plays. There is no single stock-specific headline this week; the move is largely sector-wide rate and macro driven.

themes.name: For-Profit & Vocational Education Operators
themes.description: Cluster C shows five for-profit and vocational education stocks moving together with 0.84 correlation, suggesting early-stage sector rotation. Policy tailwinds around workforce retraining, trade school demand, and potential regulatory relief for vocational programs could be the catalyst as LINC, LOPE, PRDO, UTI, and CVSA all show improving price action from depressed RS levels.

themes.name: Industrial Equipment Rental & Material Handling
themes.description: Construction and industrial activity is driving renewed demand for equipment rental and material handling systems. HRI (aerial, earthmoving, trucks) and SUNB (construction/industrial equipment) are pure-play equipment rental operators both showing strong RS recovery from multi-week lows, while CMCO (hoists, rigging, material handling) addresses the adjacent lifting and movement market — all benefiting from the same infrastructure and industrial spending cycle.

themes.name: Senior & Mid-Tier Gold & Silver Miners
themes.description: Gold and silver prices are driving a broad sector rotation into producing miners, with Cluster A showing 28-stock correlation above 0.80. The largest unthemed producers — including NEM, AEM, KGC, and others — are all moving together on the same precious metals price catalyst. This is a distinct cohort from the already-covered junior miners (PPTA, FSM) and royalty streamers (FNV, RGLD), representing the higher-quality producing tier.

themes.name: U.S. Government/Defense Contract Surge
themes.description: Each company is reporting transformative growth in government/defense revenue: Palantir's U.S. government revenue surged 90% YoY, Telesat signed a record $2.3B CAD military satcom contract, Voyager posted record bookings driven by defense programs, and Ameresco's record project awards include significant federal energy project contracts.

themes.name: Government & Defense IT Services Providers
themes.description: A surge in U.S. government and defense IT modernization spending is driving outsized relative strength in companies that specialize in systems integration, engineering services, and IT solutions for federal and defense clients. EFOR's parabolic RS acceleration from 6 to 100 in four weeks is the clearest early signal, supported by LDOS, AMTM, and DXC all quietly turning from weak to improving RS. Government digital transformation budgets — including defense IT modernization — are providing a durable, contract-backed revenue catalyst that is distinct from commercial IT services.

themes.name: Mobile App Platform & Advertising Monetization
themes.description: Digital Turbine (APPS) is moving higher this week primarily on the back of a strong Q1 print that beat Street expectations on both EPS and revenue, reinforcing the view that its growth inflection is underway. The move is being reinforced by ongoing positive sentiment around its app discovery/ad monetization flywheel and recent AI/data partnerships (e.g., Databricks, Google Cloud) that support a higher medium-term revenue trajectory. In short, the catalyst is an earnings beat plus growing confidence that its new AI-driven platform deals can sustain above-consensus growth.

themes.name: Digital Insurance Distribution & InsurTech Platforms
themes.description: GSHD is moving higher this week on the back of a strong fundamental tape: back-to-back earnings beats in Q1 and Q2 with double‑digit revenue growth, EBITDA up high teens, and EPS up nearly 30%, which has reinforced the bull case and triggered renewed buying. Multiple sell-side firms have reiterated Overweight ratings and positive commentary following these results, and prior insider buying by the CEO and other executives continues to be viewed as a confidence signal that investors are leaning into as the stock recovers. The technical backdrop is supportive as well, with daily indicators flashing “buy” and momentum traders adding to the move.

themes.name: Cloud Data Storage & Analytics Infrastructure
themes.description: Snowflake (SNOW) is being driven higher by a combination of very strong recent earnings, AI Data Cloud momentum, and a blockbuster $6 billion AWS/Amazon AI infrastructure deal that has reset investor expectations for its growth and positioning as an AI winner. In addition, a wave of bullish analyst actions – notably Wells Fargo hiking its price target to $500 and other firms raising targets on the back of AI-driven workloads – has reinforced the narrative and pulled in momentum buyers. Backblaze (BLZE) is rallying on a blowout Q2 earnings print, with management highlighting surging AI-related demand, improving enterprise traction, and a record CoreWeave cloud deal that led to sharply higher price targets and a near-50% post-earnings spike.

themes.name: Family Dining & Quick-Service Restaurant Chain Recovery
themes.description: JACK appears to be moving on the debt refinancing announcement, while CBRL’s rally is tied to its post-earnings turnaround narrative. For CBRL, the main catalyst this week has been upbeat Q3 results and raised outlook, which sparked a sharp jump and follow-through buying.

themes.name: Cloud Contact Center & CCaaS Communication Platforms
themes.description: Five9 (FIVN) is trading higher this week mainly on the back of its recent inclusion in the S&P SmallCap 600 and related index-buying flows, combined with strong year‑to‑date performance and multiple recent price target hikes from Rosenblatt and Mizuho following a solid Q1 and AI‑driven backlog momentum. RingCentral (RNG) is moving higher alongside a broader SaaS rerating and lower-rate macro backdrop, with the latest leg tied to its late‑June additions to several Russell value-oriented indices and renewed interest in undervalued enterprise software.

themes.name: Traditional Staffing & Talent Placement Services
themes.description: MAN/RHI are both trading higher this week primarily on the back of stronger-than-expected Q2 earnings and revenue beats for the staffing names, with ManpowerGroup (MAN) and Robert Half (RHI) both posting upside surprises and positive guidance commentary. MAN has rallied sharply year-to-date and extended gains after its Q2 beat, which is lifting sentiment and multiples across the broader human capital and recruitment peer group, including RHI. There is no specific new company‑specific catalyst beyond ongoing earnings momentum and follow-through buying in the sector.

themes.name: Commercial, Office & Home Furniture Retailers and Manufacturers
themes.description: BOBS and MLKN are being driven higher by strong recent fundamentals and momentum: MillerKnoll (MLKN) just reported a return to profitability, better‑than‑expected Q4/FY26 results, and upbeat margin/2027 guidance, which pushed the stock to a new 1‑year high and attracted positive analyst commentary. HNI is reacting to its Q2 2026 earnings beat, where EPS topped estimates by nearly 20% and operating profit roughly doubled, shifting focus to improving profitability despite a slight revenue miss. BOBS, a momentum-based ETF, is likely benefiting from the broader risk‑on tone and continued strength in its underlying “best‑of‑breed” momentum constituents rather than a single name‑specific catalyst.

themes.name: Industrial Lifting, Material Handling & Equipment Rental
themes.description: CMCO is trading sharply higher this week on the back of a strong earnings-related SEC disclosure reporting record orders and sales in Q1 FY27 and an increase to full-year FY27 guidance. The company highlighted 125% year-over-year net sales growth driven by the Kito Crosby acquisition and solid growth across both legacy CMCO and Kito Crosby, plus a book-to-bill of 1.1x that positions it well for the second half. That combination of a material beat, robust demand metrics, and raised outlook is the key news catalyst driving the move.

themes.name: Cinema Exhibition & Premium Large-Format Recovery
themes.description: CNK is being driven higher by a clean beat on Q2 earnings and revenue versus consensus, reflecting record summer box office strength and market share gains. The move is being reinforced by bullish commentary on premium formats/consumer spend and follow‑through from analyst target hikes (e.g., Morgan Stanley lifting its CNK target to 40). IMAX is rallying on record global box office performance for Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” which is tracking nearly double “Oppenheimer,” producing multiple consecutive $50M+ IMAX weekends and pushing the stock to all‑time/52‑week highs amid fresh price‑target upgrades.

themes.name: Cloud Supply Chain & Warehouse Management Software
themes.description: MANH is higher this week because its Q2 2026 earnings beat expectations and management raised full-year guidance, which sparked a sharp rerating in the stock. For SPSC, the move is tied to the latest quarter’s stronger cash-flow profile and the market rethinking the company’s valuation after the report.

themes.name: Enterprise HR & Workforce Management SaaS
themes.description: WDAY and PCTY are moving higher on a combination of renewed enthusiasm for enterprise software and AI plays plus investors leaning on their recently strong earnings and raised guidance for subscription revenue and margins. For Workday specifically, the continued strength in AI-driven products, robust Q1 results (double‑digit revenue and EPS beats), and ongoing buyback/undervaluation narratives are attracting incremental demand from both fundamental and momentum buyers. Paylocity is benefiting from prior upside surprises, expanded share repurchase authorization, and fresh bullish positioning that has named it a top HR software pick ahead of its next earnings report, drawing in traders positioning for further upside.

themes.name: Inflammatory Disease & Immunology Biologics
themes.description: ORKA SYRE (Oruka Therapeutics) is being driven higher this week primarily by a cluster of bullish analyst actions and deal/news follow-through: multiple firms have recently raised price targets and reiterated strong buy/overweight ratings, with targets as high as $180–200, citing the company’s amended licensing agreement with Paragon Therapeutics and an AbbVie-related acquisition announcement. In the background, investors are still reacting to the strong Week 16 EVERLAST-A Phase 2a psoriasis data for ORKA-001, which underpins the upgraded outlook and supports momentum at new 52-week highs.

themes.name: Electrical Infrastructure Products & Systems Installation
themes.description: IESC is being driven higher by a blowout fiscal Q3 earnings beat, with revenue up ~40% year over year, net income nearly doubling, and demand for AI/data center infrastructure powering a 90%+ backlog increase. In addition, the board approved a 2-for-1 stock split with an August 14 record date, adding a mechanical and sentiment catalyst. ATKR is rallying on a definitive $3.8B all-cash acquisition agreement by Prysmian at $95 per share (roughly a 30% premium) alongside a stronger-than-expected fiscal Q3 print, pushing the stock toward the deal price.

themes.name: Peptide & Hormone Therapies for Metabolic & Endocrine Disorders
themes.description: CORT is being driven higher by a major Q2 earnings beat, a sharp raise to 2026 revenue guidance, and exceptional early sales of new oncology drug Lifyorli, which together prompted multiple analyst price target hikes. For PTGX, the key catalyst is ongoing enthusiasm around the recent FDA approval and early commercial ramp of partner JNJ’s psoriasis drug Icotyde, which underpins bullish peak-sales expectations and royalty/milestone upside for Protagonist. For MBX and XERS there is no clear, stock-specific news headline this week; the moves look more like momentum/positioning within the small-cap biotech/biopharma complex rather than a fresh, discrete catalyst.

themes.name: Specialty Pharmaceutical Commercialization & Rare Disease Drugs
themes.description: KNSA is being driven higher this week primarily by follow‑through from its recent raise to 2026 net product revenue guidance and positive commentary around its ARCALYST sales and broader pipeline, which triggered a roughly 30% upside move and sustained momentum. In parallel, multiple analysts have lifted price targets and reiterated bullish ratings, reinforcing the growth narrative and attracting incremental institutional interest, including a new investment disclosed by OMERS Administration Corp.

themes.name: Corporate Spend, Expense Management & Financial Operations Software
themes.description: WEX is trading higher this week primarily on the back of its strong Q2 2026 earnings beat, with revenue and EPS coming in ahead of consensus and showing double‑digit year‑over‑year growth. In addition, investor sentiment has been boosted by the launch of SecureFuel, its new AI‑powered fuel fraud prevention tool for fleet customers, which is being viewed as a software‑like growth and margin catalyst. Recent share repurchases and generally supportive analyst targets are reinforcing the move.

themes.name: AI-Powered Enterprise Analytics & Intelligent Workflow SaaS
themes.description: AVPT is being bid up on renewed interest in AI software after its recent AI governance research release and the commercial rollout of its AgentPulse Command Center platform, alongside a broader rebound in software names. AMPL’s move is technically driven, with the stock bouncing after last week’s pullback and screens shifting to a short-term “buy” bias despite mixed longer-term signals. INTA is catching a bid after disclosure that AMS Capital Ltda accumulated 147,567 shares, highlighting fresh institutional demand in a name that had been pressured on valuation.

themes.name: U.S. Passenger Airlines
themes.description: The primary catalyst lifting LUV, DAL, ALK, SKYW, UAL, and ALGT this week is the broad airline-sector rally driven by lower oil/jet fuel prices, which improves margin and earnings outlooks for carriers. Market commentary specifically highlights that airline stocks are “getting a big boost from drop in oil prices” and “bounce back in a big way as oil prices drop,” with United expected to report record revenue and Delta outperforming on strong trading days, reinforcing bullish sentiment across the group. A secondary tailwind is stock-specific optimism (e.g., upbeat earnings/revenue narratives and guidance) that is riding on top of this sector-wide fuel-cost relief.

themes.name: Electrical Connectivity & Utility Network Hardware
themes.description: PLPC is being driven higher by its blowout Q2 earnings report, where it posted EPS of $4.49 versus about $2.58 expected and record revenue of $212.7 million versus $193 million expected. The stock also got a boost from strong U.S. sales growth and management’s commentary that recent acquisition Delta Star should support future growth.

themes.name: SMB & Workforce Business Services Platforms
themes.description: The main catalyst driving NSP and LZ higher this week appears to be company-specific fundamental and positioning news rather than a single macro headline. For Insperity (NSP), the move is being supported by a strong Q2 print with EPS and EBITDA ahead of expectations, raised 2026 guidance pointing to a sharp earnings recovery, and growing attention to its HR platforms following the SHRM26 showcase, which together strengthen the recovery and cash-yield narrative. For LZ Technology (LZ), the recent 37% year-over-year revenue growth in its latest 20-F, the completed 1-for-20 reverse split, and changes to board/committees and governance are all contributing to a “turnaround/cleanup” story that is attracting speculative interest and short-covering.

themes.name: B2B Digital Financial Infrastructure & Payment Rails Modernization
themes.description: The move higher in ACI Worldwide this week is being driven primarily by positioning ahead of its June-quarter earnings, where Wall Street expects year-over-year growth in both revenue and EPS, reinforcing the “payments infrastructure winner” narrative. In the background, the stock is still benefitting from recent bullish coverage around its role in Europe’s instant payments via the EPI/Wero partnership and Rabobank integration, which has reset expectations for medium-term growth and valuation. Investor sentiment remains supported by the strong Q1 print and upwardly revised outlook earlier this year, so any further upside surprise on earnings is being bid in advance.

themes.name: Industrial HVAC, Plumbing & Fabricated Copper Products
themes.description: MLI is moving higher this week primarily on the announcement of a special shareholder payout: a $3 per-share special cash dividend plus $5 in principal amount of 6% notes due 2027 for each share owned, alongside a 33% increase in its regular quarterly dividend. This capital return package is being interpreted as a strong signal of balance sheet strength and management confidence, which is attracting incremental demand for the stock.

themes.name: Medical Device Mean-Reversion & Rotation Recovery
themes.description: TNDM is moving on anticipation of its August 6 Q2 earnings print and continued momentum around its diabetes tech pipeline and recent regulatory/partnership wins (CE Mark expansion, Abbott Libre 3 Plus compatibility, Control-IQ+ pregnancy clearance and Mobi platform progress). CNMD is rallying on a strong Q2 beat and raise, with adjusted EPS and revenue above expectations plus higher full-year guidance, along with ongoing speculation about a potential sale to private equity. INSP and XRAY are trading higher mainly on sector strength in medtech/dental and positioning ahead of upcoming earnings, without a single dominant company-specific headline this week.

themes.name: Cloud Observability & AIOps Monitoring Platforms
themes.description: PD and DDOG are both being driven higher mainly by renewed enthusiasm for AI and cloud observability going into Datadog’s upcoming earnings and off the back of its very strong Q1 print and raised full‑year guidance. For DDOG specifically, a cluster of bullish analyst actions and momentum coverage, plus continued AI-related contract wins and partnerships (like the Cloudaware tie‑up), are reinforcing the bid ahead of its August 6 report. PagerDuty is riding the same enterprise software/AI ops sentiment and expectations for resilient incident‑management demand in a strong tech tape.

themes.name: Containerboard & Corrugated Packaging Producers
themes.description: PKG and Smurfit WestRock are both being driven higher by the latest round of containerboard and kraft paper price hikes across North America, which tighten supply and support margin and earnings expectations for the sector. In particular, Smurfit WestRock’s announced $100/ton increase following Packaging Corp.’s earlier $140/ton move, alongside solid Q2 results and reaffirmed guidance, has reinforced the bullish narrative for paper/packaging names and lifted sentiment across peers. More broadly, investors are pricing in stronger Q4–2027 earnings power as these price increases roll through contracts, supporting PKG/SW/IP performance this week.

themes.name: Enterprise Server, Storage & Data Infrastructure Hardware
themes.description: The main catalyst is a broad AI-infrastructure rerating: investors are bidding up server, storage, and enterprise hardware names on stronger-than-expected demand signals and bullish read-throughs from peers like Super Micro and Micron. For DELL and HPE specifically, the move is being driven more by sector momentum and positive analyst commentary than by a single new company-specific headline. STX is also catching the AI-storage trade, with its recent earnings strength keeping sentiment elevated.

themes.name: Hospital & Behavioral Health Facility Procedure Volume Recovery
themes.description: The main catalyst pushing UHS and THC higher this week is positive policy and earnings-related news for hospital operators, particularly around Medicare and payment outlook. For UHS, the move has been driven by CMS’s proposed hospital payment increase, supportive analyst commentary, and better‑than‑peer revenue growth, which collectively improved sentiment toward the stock and the group. For THC, gains are being fueled by a recent Moody’s credit upgrade, strong earnings/EBITDA guidance tied to high-acuity and USPI growth, and a bullish setup into upcoming earnings, drawing in momentum and institutional interest.

themes.name: Wealth Management & Retail Brokerage Platforms
themes.description: The move across the wealth/asset manager complex this week is being driven primarily by strong Q2 earnings prints and outlooks from key players plus a supportive macro backdrop for fee-based assets. LPL (and peers by read-through) are getting a boost from better‑than‑expected Q2 numbers, advisor growth and high advisor‑satisfaction rankings, while Schwab is seeing renewed optimism around asset growth and earnings after its recent beat. Layered on top of that, steadier equity markets and modestly firmer yields are improving sentiment toward traditional broker‑dealers and RIAs, lifting SF, SEIC, LPLA, AMP, RJF and SCHW together as a group.

themes.name: Defense Electronics & Aerospace Subsystem Suppliers
themes.description: DFNS is mostly moving on a low-float momentum squeeze after its 1-for-125 reverse split, with recent operating headlines like the Tiltan simulation order and prior defense contract/news flow helping sustain the move. AADX, ARXS, and MRCY are not in the provided results, so I can’t verify their specific catalysts from this batch.

themes.name: European Bank Stocks
themes.description: The main driver is a sector-wide bid into European and UK banks after strong Q2 results, higher-for-longer rate expectations in Europe, and ongoing capital return stories, with stock-specific tailwinds on top. BBVA and Santander are getting a premium boost from upgraded profitability targets and large, ongoing share buyback programs, while ING has its own €1bn buyback and solid earnings beat, and UK names like NWG, BCS, and LYG are benefiting from improving analyst sentiment on UK banks’ capital returns and valuations. In short, it’s a combination of positive earnings/capital actions at the individual banks and a macro rotation back into undervalued European financials.

themes.name: Private Equity & Alternative Asset Management Platforms
themes.description: ARES and HLNE are both being pushed higher primarily by a broad risk-on move in asset managers and financials as indices rally on improved macro/geopolitical sentiment, rather than a single stock-specific headline this week. There is also residual support from Hamilton Lane’s strong June-quarter earnings beat and fee/asset growth, and from ongoing positive narratives around private markets, evergreen products, and digital distribution, which are benefitting both names as leveraged plays on alternative asset growth.

themes.name: Global Steel & Metal Producers Recovery
themes.description: Minerals Technologies (MTX) is moving higher this week primarily on the back of multiple analyst upgrades and increased bullish price targets, which have highlighted meaningful upside from current levels. Ratings have been raised to buy/strong buy by several firms and commentary has focused on the stock being undervalued relative to limestone market growth and expected earnings trajectory. There is no single company-specific event this week; it’s the accumulation of positive analyst sentiment and valuation-driven buying.

themes.name: Aerospace Precision Components & Supply Chain
themes.description: DPC BA is higher this week mainly because Moody’s upgraded DPC Holdings’ corporate family rating to Ba2 from B2 and raised the outlook to positive, citing a stronger balance sheet after its IPO and diversified revenue streams. That upgrade followed a series of bullish analyst initiations and price targets, which is likely adding to the move.

themes.name: Digital Payments Processing & Merchant Acquiring Networks
themes.description: PYPL is trading higher this week primarily on the back of its strong Q2 earnings beat and raised full‑year guidance, which reinforced the turnaround narrative in core businesses like Venmo and PSP volumes. In addition, lingering Stripe/Advent $53B buyout speculation and a recent Cantor Fitzgerald price‑target hike to $60 are sustaining positive sentiment and drawing in momentum and event‑driven flows.

themes.name: Commercial Real Estate Brokerage & Advisory Services
themes.description: JLL and CBRE are moving higher this week primarily on the back of strong Q2 2026 earnings beats with raised or reaffirmed full‑year guidance, signaling a broad-based recovery in leasing, capital markets, and critical infrastructure/data center services. For CBRE specifically, the market is repricing it as an AI infrastructure/data center play after very strong growth in Infrastructure and Data Center Services, while JLL is benefiting from surging advisory/leasing activity and solid office demand for prime assets. A supportive broader equity backdrop and follow‑through buying after these earnings reports are amplifying the move.

themes.name: U.S. Domestic Steel Producers
themes.description: STLD and NUE are being driven higher mainly by strong sector fundamentals: U.S. steel prices (especially HRC) remain elevated on tight domestic supply, lower imports under tariffs, and solid demand from infrastructure and reshoring. Additionally, both are still trading on the back of very strong recent earnings prints and upbeat guidance, which have prompted a series of price target hikes and positive analyst commentary. There is no single company-specific headline this week; it is more a continuation of the earnings/steel-price momentum trade across the U.S. steel complex.

themes.name: China Consumer Internet & Digital Marketplace Platforms
themes.description: BZ (Benz Mining) is being driven higher by continued speculative buying following its very strong multi-month run, as investors position ahead of further exploration and drilling updates on its granite-hosted gold targets in Quebec. ATHM (Autohome) strength this week appears more technical than fundamental, with the stock extending a recent multi-week uptrend in Chinese internet names rather than reacting to a specific, high-profile company news release. In short, BZ is moving on momentum and exploration expectations, while ATHM is rising with broader China tech sentiment and short-term trend-following flows.

themes.name: Building Envelope, Ceilings & Interior Construction Products
themes.description: Armstrong World Industries (AWI) and Carlisle Companies (CSL) are both trading higher primarily on the back of strong Q2 earnings from Carlisle that beat expectations on revenue, EPS, and margins, driving a relief rally across the building products space. Carlisle’s print featured record ~US$1.6bn revenue, double‑digit EPS beat, and a higher full‑year revenue growth outlook, which has pulled in buyers to related building envelope names. For AWI specifically, there is no stock‑specific newsflow this week beyond general sector sympathy to Carlisle’s results and broader risk‑on sentiment in cyclicals.

themes.name: Cyber Exposure Management & Vulnerability Assessment
themes.description: QLYS, RPD, and TENB are all being bid up on the back of a broader rotation into software and cybersecurity following easing geopolitical tensions and lower yields, which are pulling capital back into growth tech. For TENB specifically, the move is reinforced by a strong Q2 print (revenue and EPS beats, Tenable One at 50% of new business) and subsequent guidance/price-target raises, plus recent FedRAMP High/IL5 authorization and AI exposure-management positioning. QLYS and RPD are effectively riding the same macro/software bid and renewed interest in under-the-radar cyber names rather than a single stock-specific headline this week.

themes.name: Specialty Insurance Underwriting & Brokerage
themes.description: Ryan Specialty (RYAN) is being driven higher this week primarily by a clean Q2 beat on both revenue and adjusted EPS, which came in at $916.6m vs. ~$874–876m consensus and $0.74 vs. $0.60. The move is reinforced by capital return (completion of a $300m buyback and a quarterly dividend declaration) and multiple sell-side target raises (e.g., RBC to $55, Keefe Bruyette to $54) following the print. PLMR does not appear to have a specific company‑level catalyst; its strength looks more like a sympathy/sector move with E&S/specialty P&C brokers after RYAN’s results and guidance.

themes.name: Technology Intellectual Property Licensing
themes.description: Dolby (DLB) is being driven higher by its latest quarterly report, where it beat EPS expectations ($0.69 vs. $0.67) despite a slight revenue miss and guided to stronger Q4 and full-year growth. InterDigital (IDCC) is moving on a very strong Q2 print and guidance raise, with annualized recurring revenue hitting a record ~$626M and the company lifting full-year 2026 revenue outlook by $85M at the midpoint, supported by its new Amazon streaming/license agreement and recent patent injunction wins against Disney. Both names are effectively trading on better-than-expected earnings outlooks and strengthened licensing economics.

themes.name: Private Mortgage Insurance
themes.description: The move higher in RDN, ESNT, MTG and NMIH is being driven mainly by the second-quarter mortgage-insurer earnings season, with NMIH’s beat and higher Street price targets helping sentiment across the group. NMIH reported revenue up 8.1% year over year and EPS above consensus, while RBC and Truist both raised targets after the strong results.

themes.name: Defense ISR & Unmanned Systems Intelligence
themes.description: HAWK (HawkEye 360) and AVEX (AEVEX Corp.) are both catching a bid on fresh defense and national security contract wins, with AVEX specifically rallying on the announcement of $88.1 million in new long‑range precision strike production orders from U.S. government customers. That award reinforces the broader geospatial/intelligence and defense-contracting theme, which is drawing incremental investor flows into names like HawkEye 360 alongside AVEX.

themes.name: Life Science Tools & Analytical Instruments
themes.description: MTD and WAT are trading higher on the back of stronger-than-expected Q2 earnings and raised full‑year EPS outlook from Mettler‑Toledo, which is lifting sentiment across precision instrument and analytical lab suppliers. TMO’s move is being supported by a series of positive collaboration headlines in biopharma (e.g., Arcturus and Nuvation deals) and ongoing buy‑side positioning in life‑science tools ahead of sector conferences and second‑half demand. Overall, investors are rotating into high‑quality lab instrumentation and life‑science tools as earnings and guidance reassure on growth durability.

themes.name: Office REIT Recovery & Re-Rating
themes.description: The main catalyst is renewed optimism around office REITs on the back of improving leasing trends and analyst upgrades, with BXP’s recent upgrade to Outperform and higher price targets highlighting stronger demand and return-to-office momentum. For HIW, the extension and repricing of its $150M unsecured term loan and related balance sheet derisking have supported sentiment, while SLG is benefiting from the broader high‑quality office REIT bid and ongoing expectations for asset sales and debt reduction. CDP is generally trading in sympathy with the sector’s improved outlook as investors rotate back into beaten-down office names.

themes.name: Network Security & Zero-Trust Edge
themes.description: The main catalyst is a broad re-rating of cybersecurity after IBM’s warning that enterprise spending is shifting away from traditional IT infrastructure and toward security, which sparked a sector-wide rally. The move is also being reinforced by strong recent earnings/guidance and bullish analyst commentary from names like Fortinet and Palo Alto Networks, keeping the group bid. For CRWD, OKTA, NET, FTNT, VRNS, and PANW specifically, the market is treating cybersecurity as a relative winner in the AI/security trade.

themes.name: Property & Casualty Insurance Underwriters
themes.description: The group is moving higher mainly on stronger Q2 earnings and upbeat underwriting results in the P&C insurers, especially Hanover’s beat and Travelers’ solid setup. THG reported EPS well above estimates and record net income, while TRV has benefited from positive company-specific news flow and broader buying in the insurance space. HCI, WRB, AFG, CB and TRV are also likely getting a sector lift from the same “better-than-expected earnings / underwriting margin” narrative, not one single headline.

themes.name: Industrial Process Equipment, Automation & Flow Control
themes.description: The main catalyst pushing EMR, FLS, and LECO higher this week is strong industrial earnings and outlooks, led by Lincoln Electric’s record Q2 results and raised 2026 sales growth guidance, which are reinforcing confidence in the broader industrial and automation cycle. LECO reported double‑digit sales growth to about $1.22B, expanded margins, and a 13% increase in adjusted EPS to $2.93, while highlighting strengthening Americas demand, improving automation activity, and a record backlog, all of which support higher valuations across peer names. In addition, multiple upward price target revisions and “buy/overweight” ratings on LECO are adding momentum to the group and contributing to sector-wide rerating.

themes.name: Industrial Fluid Control, Filtration & Water Infrastructure Equipment
themes.description: FELE is higher on a Q2 beat: Franklin Electric reported adjusted EPS of $1.55 versus $1.44 expected and revenue of $622.9 million versus $605.9 million, with sales up 6% and adjusted EPS up 18% year over year. IEX and DCI are likely being driven by their own stock-specific catalysts rather than a shared news story; IEX has been supported by stronger traded-volume and profit updates, while DCI has been helped by contract/news flow such as its fuel-supply MoU.

themes.name: Insurance Brokerage & Distribution Services
themes.description: BRO, AJG, and AON are being driven higher mainly by strong fundamental and sentiment tailwinds in the insurance brokerage space plus fresh sell-side support. AJG is benefiting from positive analyst actions (UBS just raised its price target and reiterated Buy) and ongoing M&A-driven growth, which tends to pull correlated peers like BRO higher as investors bid up the group. AON is getting support from a clean Q2 beat, multiple recent price-target hikes across major brokers, and continued confidence in its capital-return and earnings-growth story, lifting the whole large-cap broker complex.

themes.name: U.S. Petroleum Refining & Downstream Processing
themes.description: The group is being driven higher by a powerful refining-margin and supply-tightness theme: crack spreads have widened sharply as geopolitical tensions around Iran and the Strait of Hormuz disrupt product flows and tighten global refined product supply, while refineries outside the conflict zones run at or near full tilt with little spare capacity, supporting higher fuel prices and margins. PBF has an added kicker from a massive Q2 earnings beat and the Martinez refinery back at full capacity, which is reinforcing the bullish read-through for peers like MPC, VLO, DINO, and PSX via their high historical correlation and shared exposure to the same margin dynamics. Investor positioning is shifting toward refiners as one of the clearest beneficiaries of the current “physical-logistics” energy shock described on the Aramco call, amplifying the move across the complex.

themes.name: U.S. Regional & Mid-Cap Commercial Banks
themes.description: The move in these regional banks is being driven mainly by sector-wide catalysts rather than stock‑specific news: ongoing steepening at the long end of the yield curve, improving credit metrics, and continued rotation into value/financials ahead of Q2 earnings and capital return updates. Within that backdrop, you’ve also had a series of analyst price target raises and positive fundamental commentary on names like MTB, FHN, and ZION that reinforce the earnings recovery and capital return story for the group. In short, it’s a macro/sector trade: better net interest income expectations, benign credit, and investors re‑risking into regional banks rather than any single headline this week.

themes.name: Quantum Computing Hardware & Software
themes.description: RGTI, QBTS, and the broader quantum group are moving higher on a cluster of sector-wide catalysts: D‑Wave’s new fraud‑detection partnership with Nasdaq Verafin, its expanded AT&T network-operations deal, and bullish “buy” initiations and reinstatements from Benchmark and Wedbush that highlight a near-term commercial tipping point for quantum computing. In addition, reports that the Trump administration is considering multi‑billion‑dollar grants and even minority equity stakes in several quantum firms have further intensified speculative interest and momentum across the space, pulling smaller names like QUBT and XNDU along with the leaders. There is no major company-specific headline for QUBT or XNDU this week; they are mainly riding the sector rally and momentum spillover from the higher-profile names.

themes.name: Copper Mining & Production
themes.description: The main catalyst is a broad rally in copper driven by stronger global demand, a tightening structural supply/demand balance, and a weaker dollar/loosening Fed stance, which is lifting copper producers across the board. For FCX specifically, the move is being reinforced by upbeat Q2 earnings and multiple recent analyst target hikes, while SCCO is benefiting from robust production updates and narrative around record earnings and low-cost reserves. HBM is riding the same copper tape, helped by company-specific positives like its Copper World financing and buyback program, but the dominant driver for all three this week is macro copper strength rather than idiosyncratic news.

themes.name: Professional Advisory & Business Services
themes.description: CBIZ (CBZ) is trading sharply higher this week on news that Grant Thornton Advisors LLC agreed to acquire the company in an all‑cash transaction valued at about $5 billion, with CBZ shareholders set to receive $55 per share, a sizable premium to recent trading levels. The announced buyout has driven CBZ toward its biggest single‑day gain in over two decades and a six‑month high. For CRA International (CRAI), the move higher is primarily tied to strong recent fundamentals and record revenue highlighted around its latest earnings, alongside ongoing positive analyst sentiment, rather than a single discrete news headline this week.

themes.name: U.S. Apparel & Fashion Recovery
themes.description: UA (United Airlines), RVLV (Revolve), and CROX (Crocs) are all benefiting from a broad bid into consumer-discretionary and travel names tied to lower oil prices and expectations for resilient U.S. consumer spending. For UA specifically, the catalyst is the sharp drop in crude plus optimism around record revenue commentary into earnings and continued strong travel demand. CROX and RVLV are moving on the same sector rotation tailwind, with CROX also supported by recent earnings beat/positive guidance and footwear strength, and RVLV by improving sentiment around online apparel retailers and social-commerce growth.

themes.name: Government & Defense IT Services Providers
themes.description: A surge in U.S. government and defense IT modernization spending is driving outsized relative strength in companies that specialize in systems integration, engineering services, and IT solutions for federal and defense clients. EFOR's parabolic RS acceleration from 6 to 100 in four weeks is the clearest early signal, supported by LDOS, AMTM, and DXC all quietly turning from weak to improving RS. Government digital transformation budgets — including defense IT modernization — are providing a durable, contract-backed revenue catalyst that is distinct from commercial IT services.

themes.name: Bitcoin Mining & Crypto Infrastructure Operators
themes.description: CIFR and HUT are moving higher this week on the back of Hut 8’s massive long-term AI data center lease deals at its Beacon Point Texas campus, which fully commercialize the 1 GW site and highlight Nvidia as the anchor tenant, reinforcing the sector’s AI infrastructure re-rating. Those announcements have triggered a broader rally in former bitcoin miners pivoting to AI/data center infrastructure, with Cipher Mining benefiting as a perceived peer and beneficiary of the same theme. Analyst target hikes for CIFR and HUT ahead of earnings are adding incremental fuel to the move.

themes.name: Consumer Fintech & Digital Credit Platforms
themes.description: SEZL is higher this week mainly on momentum after hitting a fresh 52-week high, with traders also positioning ahead of its upcoming Q2 earnings report. DAVE is being lifted by a similar momentum trade, as it also reached a new 52-week high and investors are buying into continued business/earnings strength.

themes.name: Department Store Retail Recovery
themes.description: KSS is likely being lifted by Kohl’s recent earnings-related momentum, including a narrower-than-expected loss and a stock jump after the Q1 report. For DDS, the catalyst appears to be Dillard’s strong Q1 beat on earnings and sales, with comps up 3% and management citing improved merchandise newness as a demand driver.

themes.name: Franchise Auto Dealership Groups
themes.description: PAG is moving higher on the back of a clean Q2 earnings beat, with revenue and adjusted EPS both coming in ahead of consensus and highlighting strength across automotive retail, commercial trucks, and service/parts. That report hit just after Penske Corporation and Mitsui submitted a non-binding proposal to acquire the remaining ~27% of PAG at $210 per share, keeping a potential take-private and deal upside front and center. Layered on top, multiple Wall Street firms have raised price targets and reiterated bullish views, reinforcing the perception that the buyout offer undervalues PAG and helping sustain upside momentum.

themes.name: Life Insurance & Annuity Providers
themes.description: UNM, PRU, and MET are all being supported by sector-specific catalysts in life and health insurance rather than a single macro headline. For UNM, the main driver is the $3.8B long-term care reinsurance deal with Fortitude Re that de-risks the balance sheet, plus subsequent analyst price target hikes and favorable valuation commentary. PRU and MET are benefiting from the broader rotation into defensive financials amid higher yields, with MET specifically seeing momentum from its recent dividend increase and strong net investment income outlook.

themes.name: AI Data Center Infrastructure Buildout
themes.description: All three are directly benefiting from explosive AI data center demand: Bitdeer signed a $4.7B 16-year data center lease, Ameresco reported $1.2B of its record $1.8B new project awards driven by data center energy projects, and Backblaze is accelerating cloud storage revenue as data center workloads expand.

themes.name: Precious Metals Miners Rotation
themes.description: SBSW is grinding higher mainly on continued bullish sentiment toward precious metals and a technical uptrend, with the ADR trading above key moving averages and supported by prior earnings strength and improving balance sheet narratives, rather than a specific new headline catalyst this week. HYMC’s strength is being driven by ongoing momentum from recent high‑grade gold/silver exploration results, a fresh position initiated by the Swiss National Bank, and positive technicals after its extended rally. AUGO is benefiting from its preliminary Q2/H1 2026 production update, which showed solid operating performance and is attracting bid in a firm gold tape.

themes.name: Global Crude & Product Tanker Fleet Operators
themes.description: The primary catalyst is a sharp move higher in spot and forward tanker rates driven by renewed geopolitical tensions and disruptions in key oil shipping lanes, which is lifting the entire crude and product tanker complex. In parallel, several bullish sell-side pieces and upgrades on VLCC and mid-size tanker names (including DHT and Teekay) are highlighting strong cash generation, low leverage, and still-attractive valuations, drawing in momentum and macro oil plays. There is no single stock-specific headline this week; the move is largely sector-wide rate and macro driven.

themes.name: AI GPU Compute Infrastructure & Cloud Services
themes.description: Explosive AI workload demand is driving a parallel build-out of both GPU compute hardware systems and cloud/colocation services that host them. Hyperscaler capex and enterprise AI adoption are forcing a new layer of infrastructure providers — from purpose-built AI compute hardware to GPU-as-a-service hosting — to scale rapidly. These names are benefiting from the same demand surge upstream of the application layer.

themes.name: Alphabet (Google) Platform Re-Rating
themes.description: All four Alphabet share classes (GOOG, GOOGL, GOOGM, GOOGN) are moving in near-perfect lockstep (0.97 correlation, RS 71-73) as investors re-rate the stock following Gemini AI momentum, Google Cloud share gains, and YouTube advertising recovery. The cluster signals institutional accumulation across the capital structure as the market prices in a search-plus-AI monetization premium that was previously discounted.

themes.name: Dermatology & Atopic Immunology Biologics
themes.description: APGE is trading higher on continued M&A enthusiasm after AbbVie agreed in late June to acquire Apogee Therapeutics for roughly $10.9–$11 billion, validating the value of its eczema and immunology pipeline and keeping takeover/speculation premium in the name. FBRX is rallying on the definitive all-cash agreement for argenx to acquire Forte Biosciences for $77 per share, a roughly $2.2 billion deal that represents a sizable premium to its prior trading levels and locks in an exit value for shareholders.

themes.name: Hotel REIT Recovery & Re-Rating
themes.description: XHR is being driven higher by its Q2 2026 earnings release, where investors are focusing on solid operating metrics and funds-from-operations rather than the headline GAAP EPS and revenue misses, against a backdrop of strong prior momentum and raised full-year guidance earlier in the year. RLJ is rallying on sector strength and its own track record of positive earnings surprises plus fresh 52-week highs that are attracting momentum and technical buyers. Both are also benefiting from a supportive macro tape and resilient lodging REIT fundamentals, particularly in upscale segments.

themes.name: Industrial Construction Execution & On-Site Supply Chain
themes.description: DNOW is being bid up mainly on renewed deal/speculation interest around its completed combination with MRC Global and ongoing earnings re-rating as investors focus on post-merger synergies. TPC is moving higher on bullish analyst commentary highlighting improved profitability, a high-margin backlog converting to revenue, and a “Strong Buy” consensus rating. RYZ is rallying on a clean Q2 earnings beat, strong merger-driven growth with Olympic Steel, and a newly declared dividend, all reinforcing the Olympic Steel synergy and guidance story.

themes.name: Smart Utility Metering & Water Infrastructure Hardware
themes.description: ITRI is being driven higher by a blowout Q2 earnings print: EPS of $1.59 far above consensus, record gross margins over 41%, and a meaningful raise to full‑year earnings guidance, all highlighting strong demand from utilities for grid modernization and resiliency solutions. MWA (Mueller Water) is moving in sympathy with the same infrastructure and water-utility capex theme, as investors rotate into water technology/resource management names benefiting from elevated spending and resilient demand across water networks.

themes.name: Canadian Big Banks
themes.description: The main catalyst pushing TD, RY, CM, BNS, and BMO higher this week is a sector-wide bid into Canadian banks driven by improving sentiment on bank earnings, capital returns, and a more supportive regulatory backdrop, including the recent cut to the domestic stability buffer to spur lending. Investors are rotating into large Canadian financials as macro fears around credit quality and rate cuts ease, while strong recent quarters (profit growth, dividend hikes, and solid capital markets/wealth revenues) reinforce the “quality income” thesis for the group. Flows into TSX financials and the banks’ near-52-week-high technical momentum are amplifying the move.

themes.name: Uniform Rental & Managed Workwear Services
themes.description: CTAS is being bid up ahead of its upcoming Q4/FY26 earnings webcast, with investors positioning on the back of strong multi‑year returns and expectations for another solid print and potential guidance support. VSTS is trading higher as investors re-rate the name on its strong year-to-date performance and continued post-spin recovery in the workwear/uniform rental space, with no single discrete news headline this week but ongoing sentiment and analyst focus driving flows.

themes.name: U.S. Government/Defense Contract Surge
themes.description: All four are capturing accelerating government contract revenue: Palantir's U.S. government revenue grew 90% YoY, Telesat signed a transformative $2.3B CAD 15-year military satcom contract, Voyager reported record bookings and backlog with a raised defense-contract-driven outlook, and Ameresco's record project awards include significant government energy infrastructure work.

themes.name: Clinical-Stage Oncology Biotech
themes.description: ELVN is being driven higher this week by continued enthusiasm around its updated Phase 1 ENABLE trial data for ELVN-001 in previously treated chronic myeloid leukemia, which clarified an FDA-aligned path toward Phase 3 and boosted perceived approval odds. That clinical momentum is reinforced by the recently completed ~$460M upsized equity offering, which de-risks funding for development, and by multiple analyst price target hikes (into the mid‑60s to $70 range) following the data update. TGTX strength is tied to positive Phase 3 ENHANCE trial results for its multiple sclerosis therapy, supporting its commercial trajectory and sentiment across the hematology/oncology and neurology space.

themes.name: Junior Precious Metals Miners Rotation
themes.description: PPTA is trading higher on ongoing momentum from the opening of its U.S. Army-backed antimony pilot plant and related strategic loan/government support for the Stibnite project, which has re-rated the stock as a key critical-minerals play. FSM and PAAS are being bid up primarily on the back of stronger precious metals prices and bullish positioning ahead of upcoming production/earnings catalysts, with silver and gold miners broadly catching a bid as metals continue to hold elevated levels. Secondary support comes from positive analyst sentiment and technical strength in PAAS, plus Fortuna’s resource and portfolio-optimization news that improve medium-term cash flow leverage to metal prices.

themes.name: Small Modular & Advanced Nuclear Reactor Development
themes.description: The move higher in OKLO, NNE, SMR and CEG this week is being driven primarily by renewed enthusiasm for advanced nuclear as a key power source for AI data centers and broader AI-driven power demand. Sector sentiment improved after reports of federal initiatives (including the DOE Reactor Pilot Program and a Trump-led acceleration effort) and high-profile SMR and nuclear-powered data center projects, which collectively reinforce the commercialization and policy support narrative for SMRs and advanced reactors. Options-driven speculative flows and ongoing AI-related long-term power contract announcements in the nuclear space are amplifying the bid.

themes.name: Gold & Precious Metals Miners Rotation
themes.description: The primary driver this week is a broad move higher in gold and precious metals on the back of easing Fed rate hike fears and supportive inflation/PCE data, which has lifted the entire gold-miner complex. On top of that macro tailwind, several of these names have seen incremental fundamental positives: Harmony (HMY) has benefited from multiple analyst upgrades and ESG rating improvements, while IAMGOLD (IAG) and others are supported by recent resource, credit facility, and “buy” rating news that improve balance sheets and growth visibility. Together, the macro gold bid plus name-specific upgrades and project/resource headlines are pushing HMY, SBSW, KGC, NEM, GFI, and IAG higher.

themes.name: Senior & Long-Term Care Healthcare REITs
themes.description: OHI and VTR are being driven higher primarily by strong earnings beats and reaffirmed growth in senior housing and healthcare real estate fundamentals, with OHI’s Q2 results topping consensus on accretive investment activity and VTR’s recent beat and raised full-year guidance reinforcing the sector’s recovery. Broader rate and macro backdrop this week (central bank decisions, stabilizing long-end yields, and risk-on sentiment) is also supporting defensive, income-oriented healthcare REITs as a group. LTC is participating largely as a sympathy move within the senior housing/healthcare REIT complex, supported by prior positive catalysts (SHOP expansion, dividend stability) but without a distinct new company-specific headline this week.

themes.name: Truckload & LTL Freight Carriers
themes.description: ArcBest (ARCB) is being driven higher by bullish analyst actions this week, including new coverage with an outperform rating and multiple price target hikes tied to a perceived end to the multi‑year trucking downturn and strong pre‑earnings revenue/tonnage trends. Hub Group (HUBG) and Schneider (SNDR) are moving with the broader freight/trucking group on the same “freight recovery” narrative and rotation into truckload/intermodal names ahead of earnings, as investors position for improving pricing power and volume. There is no company‑specific positive news for HUBG this week; its move is largely sector beta against that recovery theme despite ongoing accounting‑probe overhang.

themes.name: Open-Air & Strip Mall Retail REITs
themes.description: The main driver is a sector-wide bid into open‑air shopping center and strip‑center REITs on the back of falling long-term yields and a defensive rotation into income-oriented real assets. For these specific names, incremental support is coming from index inclusion/flows (KIM’s addition to Russell 1000 defensive/value indexes), rising expectations into Q2 earnings (KRG, PECO and peers), and generally positive leasing/fundamentals commentary from recent REIT and ICSC/NAREIT conference appearances. There is no single stock-specific headline this week moving just one of KRG, FRT, KIM, SKT, BRX, or PECO; they are trading as a group on the macro rate/defensive and earnings-setup narrative.

themes.name: Online Insurance Comparison & Digital Marketplace Platforms
themes.description: MAX EVER’s strength this week is being driven primarily by company-specific news: MediaAlpha (MAX) is rallying into its scheduled Q2 2026 earnings release, which is increasing speculation about improved profitability and a continued recovery in insurance customer acquisition spending. Separately, Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions (often tagged as MAX EVER/Max Ever in some feeds) recently hit an all-time high after announcing a major renewable energy partnership with Meta to build 837 MW of solar and wind capacity, with Meta buying all green attributes from these projects, which remains a key sentiment tailwind. Broadly supportive AI- and tech-led equity momentum is providing a constructive backdrop but is secondary to these direct catalysts.

themes.name: Consumer Staples Packaged Food & Snack Brand Recovery
themes.description: LW is trading higher this week mainly on anticipation around its July 24th Q4/FY26 earnings release and Starboard Value’s activist involvement pushing for an Investor Day and a 25% EBITDA margin target by FY2029. There is also a defensive bid as investors focus on operational efficiency moves like the planned closure of the Broekhuizenvorst, Netherlands plant and cost-savings/capex discipline highlighted in recent results and guidance. CAG’s move higher is being driven by value and yield interest after the stock crossed a double‑digit dividend yield, alongside insider buying and a new CEO that is prompting a contrarian turnaround narrative despite recent negative sentiment and estimate cuts.

themes.name: Precious Metals Royalty & Streaming Companies
themes.description: The main catalyst is the continued strength in gold and silver prices combined with very strong recent fundamentals and growth guidance across the royalty/streaming group, which is pulling the whole space higher as a defensive way to play the metals rally. Wheaton Precious Metals, Franco-Nevada and Royal Gold all recently posted record or beat-and-raise quarters and updated asset handbooks/outlook highlighting multi‑year production growth, which is reinforcing bid for the model versus traditional miners. There is also some positioning ahead of upcoming earnings (WPM and FNV) and index/ETF flows into precious metals that are supporting the group.

themes.name: US-China Tariff Truce — Consumer Goods & Digital Beneficiaries
themes.description: The announced US-China tariff de-escalation directly re-rates brands with heavy China-based manufacturing (HAS, MAT, SONO) and lifts Chinese consumer-facing digital platforms (BZ) as US-China sentiment improves and capital rotates back into Chinese ADRs — a cross-sector catalyst binding consumer leisure, tech hardware, and China internet into one trade.

themes.name: Smart Home Security & Comfort Systems
themes.description: Resideo (REZI) and Alarm.com (ALRM) have been moving higher primarily on company‑specific and structural catalysts rather than a single discrete headline this week. For REZI, the key drivers are the ongoing ADI spin-off process and related unsecured notes offering, plus accumulation by institutions such as Arrowstreet Capital and a still‑constructive Street view with upside to consensus targets. For ALRM, the move is largely sympathy and sector read‑through, as investors reposition into home security and smart‑home names that benefit from Resideo’s restructuring and improving sentiment in connected‑home/security peers.

themes.name: For-Profit & Vocational Post-Secondary Education Operators
themes.description: The primary catalyst this week is sector-specific: U.S. for-profit and career education names are catching a bid on renewed M&A/speculation and follow-through from Laureate’s announced $1.48B sale of Walden University to Adtalem, which has re-rated the group and highlighted embedded asset value across education franchises. Laureate (LAUR) is moving directly on that transaction headline, while peers LINC, LOPE, PRDO, STRA, and UTI are riding sympathy/rotation into education and training plays as investors position for consolidation and structurally higher demand for upskilling and non-traditional postsecondary programs. There is no single new company-specific print this week across all of them; it is a group move driven by that deal, prior positive expansion/earnings commentary, and thematic flows into the education/training space.

themes.name: B2B Marketing Automation & Customer Engagement SaaS
themes.description: HubSpot (HUBS) is trading higher on renewed AI enthusiasm around its CRM and marketing automation platform, with investors rotating back into AI-enabled software following positive megacap AI sentiment. Klaviyo (KVYO) is being bid up on accelerating revenue growth, record operating margins, raised full-year guidance, and an expanded share buyback program, which collectively signal improving profitability and stronger management confidence. Broader AI sector strength and CRM automation headlines are reinforcing the move in both names.

themes.name: Financial Compliance & Regulatory Reporting SaaS
themes.description: DFIN is catching a bid on the back of a recent institutional buy disclosure from Fifth Third Bancorp, which increased its stake and highlighted DFIN’s better‑than‑expected earnings, strong recurring revenue profile, and Buy‑rated analyst backdrop. WK is moving higher on its own strong earnings print and bullish 2026 outlook that came out this week, which is driving follow‑through buying in cloud/compliance names. Together, the combination of positive fundamental news and supportive analyst sentiment is the key catalyst for both names.

themes.name: Net Lease Single-Tenant REIT Recovery
themes.description: The main catalyst this week is a broad risk-on move into rate-sensitive real estate and net-lease REITs following increasingly dovish Fed commentary and growing expectations for near-term rate cuts, which improves the relative appeal of long-duration, high-yield REIT cash flows. In that backdrop, the group is also getting a tailwind from solid recent earnings, dividend growth (e.g., NNN’s dividend raise and acquisition guidance) and tightening credit spreads that support valuation multiples and acquisition economics. There is no single stock-specific headline driving ADC, EPRT, NNN, O, and WPC individually; they are primarily rallying as part of a sector-wide re-rating of net-lease REITs tied to the changing rates narrative.

themes.name: Regulated Water Utility Infrastructure
themes.description: The main catalyst is the advancing all-stock merger between American Water Works (AWK) and Essential Utilities (WTRG), which has recently secured multiple key state regulatory approvals (Kentucky, Ohio, Virginia), increasing confidence the deal will close and driving a bid across the regulated water space. In addition, American Water’s stronger-than-expected Q2 2026 results, reaffirmed EPS guidance, and visible capital investment/regulatory pipeline are supporting sentiment and lifting peers via sector read-through. Broader rotation into defensives/low-beta utilities in a choppy tape is adding incremental demand for names like AWR, CWT, HTO, and WTRG.

themes.name: Molecular Diagnostics & DNA-Based Genetic Testing
themes.description: QGEN is likely moving on a mix of recent corporate/news flow and positioning, especially Qiagen’s June 27 addition to the Russell 1000 Dynamic Index and the recent Goldman Sachs disclosure of a 3.65% voting interest. There’s also some support from recent analyst coverage/news such as Kepler’s Hold rating and the IngenuitySystems acquisition headline, but the Russell-index inclusion appears to be the clearest catalyst.

themes.name: Cruise Line & Ocean Travel Recovery
themes.description: NCLH and RCL are higher mainly on a broad cruise-sector rally after reports of a pause in U.S.-Iran hostilities pushed oil prices down, which eases fuel-cost pressure on cruise lines. NCLH is also getting an added lift from pre-earnings positioning ahead of its July 30 Q2 report, with investors looking for a potential beat and better cruise-demand commentary.

themes.name: Department Store Retail Recovery
themes.description: KSS is likely being lifted by Kohl’s recent earnings-related momentum, including a narrower-than-expected loss and a stock jump after the Q1 report. For DDS, the catalyst appears to be Dillard’s strong Q1 beat on earnings and sales, with comps up 3% and management citing improved merchandise newness as a demand driver.

themes.name: Tax Preparation & Consumer Financial Software Platforms
themes.description: INTU is moving higher this week primarily on follow-through from strong fiscal Q3 results and raised full-year revenue and earnings guidance, plus renewed focus on its longer-term growth story after a recent selloff. The launch of a new QuickBooks-integrated business credit card and expanded AI/strategic partnerships (including Anthropic and FedNow) are reinforcing the small-business ecosystem and improving sentiment. HRB’s move appears more modest, with the main recent catalyst being Stephens initiating coverage at Equal Weight with a $47 price target, which has put some incremental attention on the name.

themes.name: For-Profit & Vocational Education Operators
themes.description: Cluster C shows five for-profit and vocational education stocks moving together with 0.84 correlation, suggesting early-stage sector rotation. Policy tailwinds around workforce retraining, trade school demand, and potential regulatory relief for vocational programs could be the catalyst as LINC, LOPE, PRDO, UTI, and CVSA all show improving price action from depressed RS levels.

themes.name: Branded Packaged Food & Consumer Staples Producers
themes.description: CPB is up on defensive rotation into staples plus modestly positive sentiment around its steady earnings profile and pricing power, rather than a specific, stock‑specific headline. GIS is being driven higher by its recent fiscal Q4 beat, a large cost‑savings plan through 2030, and product innovation messaging that improved earnings and margin expectations. KHC strength is tied to its new multiyear Disney alliance expanding distribution and licensing opportunities, layered on top of restructuring, product launches, and positioning ahead of its upcoming earnings print.

themes.name: U.S. Multifamily & Residential Apartment REITs
themes.description: The main catalyst is the announced “merger of equals” between AvalonBay Communities (AVB) and Equity Residential (EQR), which is lifting multifamily REITs broadly and pulling closely correlated peers CPT, MAA, and UDR higher alongside sector optimism. In addition, improving multifamily fundamentals (strong national absorption, stabilizing rents/occupancy) and the read-through from recent earnings and guidance for these names are reinforcing the move as investors re-rate the apartment REIT group. Correlation data show these tickers tend to move in lockstep, so strength in AVB/EQR is mechanically supporting CPT, MAA, and UDR.

themes.name: Vacation Ownership & Timeshare Resort Recovery
themes.description: HGV, TNL, and VAC are trading higher mainly on sector-level optimism after Goldman Sachs highlighted the timeshare space and specifically cited TNL and VAC as compelling investments, improving sentiment across the group. Additionally, HGV has supportive company-specific catalysts including recent balance sheet refinancing, a term note securitization, an expanded receivables facility, and the appointment of industry veteran Christine Duffy to its board, which collectively strengthen the growth and governance narrative. Anticipation around upcoming Q2 earnings for HGV, alongside broader expectations for lodging and timeshare outperformance, is also contributing to the move.
