themes.name: Nuclear Fuel Cycle & Microreactor Development
themes.description: A tight correlation cluster (NNE, OKLO, SMR, UUUU) plus rotation-candidate STDN points to accumulation across the advanced nuclear fuel supply chain — from uranium feedstock (UUUU) to fuel fabrication (STDN) to microreactor and SMR developers (NNE, OKLO, SMR). This is a more specific fuel-cycle sub-theme than the broader reactor-technology basket, capturing the buildout narrative ahead of DOE/utility contract announcements.

themes.name: Optical Interconnect & Photonics for AI Data Center Networking
themes.description: LITE, COHR, and CRDO all supply optical components, photonics, and high-speed connectivity chips that address the interconnect bottleneck inside AI data centers, distinct from the broader semiconductor equipment/materials names lumped into the general AI interconnect supply chain theme. Rising bandwidth needs from AI clusters are driving demand for optical transceivers and DSPs.

themes.name: Power Generation & Grid Infrastructure for AI Data Centers
themes.description: FRMI (private electric grid infrastructure for AI computing), GEV (power generation and grid electrification), EROC (distributed power generation deployment), and AMRC (energy efficiency and renewable solutions) are all levered to the same catalyst: surging electricity demand from AI data centers straining grid capacity. This is distinct from the nuclear-fuel cluster, focused instead on near-term power delivery and grid buildout solutions.

themes.name: Semiconductor Components & Optical Interconnect
themes.description: CEVA, COHR, ENTG, GFS and RMBS form a high-correlation cluster of semiconductor IP, materials and optical/interconnect component suppliers tied to AI data center and advanced chip build-out demand.

themes.name: U.S. Oil & Gas E&P Recovery
themes.description: TALO, CRK, OVV, NOG and APA are independent oil & gas exploration and production companies showing renewed RS strength as commodity prices and production economics improve.

themes.name: Enterprise Unstructured Data Storage Infrastructure
themes.description: QMCO is higher this week mainly on its fiscal Q1 earnings beat: Quantum reported revenue of $80.8 million versus $71.5 million expected and adjusted EPS of $0.18 versus a loss forecast, then raised optimism around its outlook. The rally was also reinforced by Northland Securities upgrading the stock to outperform with a $24 target.

themes.name: Cyber Exposure Management & Vulnerability Assessment
themes.description: QLYS, TENB, and RPD are being lifted mainly by strong Q2 earnings/guidance from the cybersecurity group, with Qualys and Tenable both beating expectations and raising outlooks. Rapid7 is also moving on better-than-expected Q2 sales, while broader risk-on buying in SaaS/cybersecurity stocks is adding support.

themes.name: Cloud Contact Center & CCaaS Communication Platforms
themes.description: FIVN and RNG are moving on the same broad catalyst: strong SaaS/AI earnings and upbeat guidance, with Five9’s Q2 beat and a larger revenue outlook driving the clearest upside. For FIVN specifically, the biggest news was its better-than-expected Q2 results, higher full-year revenue guidance, and a roughly $100 million new customer win; RingCentral’s move looks more like sympathy trading from the broader cloud-calling/AI rerating.

themes.name: Software Development & DevOps Collaboration Platforms
themes.description: TEAM’s move higher this week is mainly being driven by a strong post-earnings rally: Atlassian beat Q2 expectations and issued upbeat guidance, with investors especially focused on accelerating cloud adoption and Rovo AI traction. The stock is also getting a broader software-sector lift from the recent AI-led surge in peers.

themes.name: Cloud Data Storage & Analytics Infrastructure
themes.description: SNOW is being driven higher by upbeat analyst and AI-demand news, especially Evercore’s higher price target and commentary around strong enterprise demand for Snowflake’s AI tools. BLZE is also up on the same broad AI/storage theme, with the recent CoreWeave deal and solid Q2 results continuing to support the move.

themes.name: Programmatic Digital Advertising Platforms
themes.description: MGNI is moving higher mainly on its Q2 earnings beat and raised full-year outlook, with investors also reacting to stronger CTV growth and margin expansion. QNST is higher for the same broad catalyst: a strong earnings report and upbeat guidance that beat expectations.

themes.name: Digital Insurance Distribution & InsurTech Platforms
themes.description: GSHD’s move appears tied to the recent insider buy: Director Peter R. Lane purchased 1,600 shares on July 31, a bullish signal that likely helped sentiment this week. For LIFE, the catalyst is Ethos Technologies’ strong Q2 results, with revenue up 113%, guidance raised, and a buyback announced.

themes.name: Genomics & DNA Sequencing Tools
themes.description: The common catalyst is a broad biotech rerating on company-specific earnings/guidance beats: TWST rallied after a strong quarter and raised full-year outlook, while TXG jumped on an earnings beat and analyst target hikes. ILMN also firmed on a Zacks upgrade to Strong Buy, and BRKR’s move appears tied more to sector sympathy than a single major company-specific headline.

themes.name: Semiconductor Components & Optical Interconnect
themes.description: Auto-retired 2026-08-13: absorbed/superseded by 'AI Chip & Interconnect Supply Chain Enablement' (prior stage Nascent, 5 tickers).

themes.name: Cloud Supply Chain & Warehouse Management Software
themes.description: For MANH, the main catalyst this week is its Q2 2026 earnings beat plus raised full-year guidance, which sparked a sharp rally. For SPSC, the only clear recent catalyst in the provided results is Renaissance Technologies’ new $5.53 million stake, but that is more of a stock-specific news item than a broad re-rating driver.

themes.name: AI-Powered Enterprise Analytics & Intelligent Workflow SaaS
themes.description: The main catalyst is the Q2 earnings/guidance beat: AVPT reported revenue and ARR growth above expectations and management raised full-year ARR and revenue outlook, with especially strong demand for its AI-governance product AgentPulse and Control bundles. For the rest of the group, the move is also being helped by the same “AI software upside” tape: APPN, PATH, MNDY, AMPL and INTA are catching sympathy bids as investors rotate into software names tied to AI adoption, workflow automation, and better-than-feared earnings/guidance.

themes.name: Enterprise HR & Workforce Management SaaS
themes.description: The move is mainly an earnings-driven re-rating in software/HCM: PAYC and PCTY are higher on strong quarterly beats, raised guidance, and margin/recurring-revenue strength, while the group is also getting a tailwind from softer rate expectations that help long-duration software valuations. ADP and PAYX are likely being pulled up by the same sector rotation and sympathy bid rather than a company-specific headline, with PAYX additionally outperforming on a strong trading day in the payroll/software tape.

themes.name: Mobile App Platform & Advertising Monetization
themes.description: BSP is being driven mainly by pre-earnings positioning ahead of its first-ever quarterly report as a public company on August 13. The other major catalyst is the recently announced $1.285 billion all-cash Airtable acquisition, which is reinforcing the growth narrative and keeping sentiment elevated.

themes.name: Cloud Observability & AIOps Monitoring Platforms
themes.description: The common catalyst is AI-linked earnings momentum: DDOG is rallying on a strong Q2 beat and renewed demand for observability tied to AI workloads, while DT is benefiting from the market’s broader re-rating of AI observability software. PD is also moving with the same theme, as investors rotate into software names seen as leveraged to AI spending and enterprise demand.

themes.name: Life Sciences & Healthcare Data/CRM Platforms
themes.description: TEM, DOCS, and VEEV are being lifted mainly by a broader healthcare/software momentum trade, with company-specific support from solid recent earnings and upbeat AI/product-growth narratives. For VEEV, the clearest catalyst is its June 3 Q1 FY2027 earnings beat, plus added sentiment from the Aug. 11 Eli Lilly Vault CRM win; DOCS has been moving on strong AI-driven execution and earnings momentum, and TEM is likely riding similar AI/health-data enthusiasm.

themes.name: Network Security & Zero-Trust Edge
themes.description: The main catalyst is a sector-wide cybersecurity rally driven by renewed AI-security enthusiasm and bullish analyst commentary, especially after a Black Hat-related wave of attention and reports that AI models are creating more real-world threat concerns. PANW, CRWD, NET, FTNT, VRNS, and RBRK are all being lifted by the same trade: higher enterprise security budgets and investors rotating into cyber names ahead of upcoming earnings, rather than a single company-specific headline.

themes.name: Restaurant Chain Recovery
themes.description: The main catalyst is a fresh wave of restaurant-sector earnings upside: CAKE, TXRH, and BLMN all got boosted by strong quarterly results and/or raised guidance, which is also lifting sentiment around DRI. CAKE and TXRH are being helped by beat-and-raise reports, while BLMN jumped after a sharp post-earnings rally on better-than-expected results and an improved outlook. For DRI, the move looks more like sympathy strength with the broader casual-dining rerating than a single company-specific headline.

themes.name: Consumer Fintech & Digital Credit Platforms
themes.description: The move is mostly being driven by a broader earnings-and-analyst-upgrade tape: PGY’s stronger Q2 results and raised estimates, CHYM’s multi-day momentum/run-up, and BFH’s upbeat Q2 earnings plus follow-on analyst target/rating support. For KLAR, AFRM, and DAVE, the common catalyst is investor rotation into fintech after improving growth/profitability signals and short-covering around the group, rather than one single company-specific headline.

themes.name: Enterprise Server, Storage & Data Infrastructure Hardware
themes.description: The common catalyst is a broad rerating of enterprise hardware and infrastructure names tied to AI/data-center spending, amplified by Morgan Stanley upgrades on HPE and NTAP and sector-positive commentary on compute/storage demand. ANET is also moving on AI-networking strength after earnings/outlook updates, while DELL and STX are being lifted by the same “AI infrastructure / storage refresh” trade. A separate report also pointed to IBM’s revenue warning shifting enterprise budgets toward servers and memory, which helped the whole group bid up.

themes.name: Corporate Spend, Expense Management & Financial Operations Software
themes.description: The main catalyst is WEX’s upbeat messaging at its Bank of America SMID Cap Virtual Conference: management said growth is steady, margins should improve, and share buybacks have resumed now that leverage is back below target. The stock is also getting support from recent Q2 earnings strength and the newly authorized $1 billion repurchase program.

themes.name: Medical Device Mean-Reversion & Rotation Recovery
themes.description: CNMD, INSP, and TNDM are being pushed higher by the same broad healthcare/device catalyst: strong Q2 earnings and improving margins, with TNDM’s move specifically tied to record sales, 57% gross margin, and faster PayGo pharmacy adoption. For INSP and CNMD, the likely driver this week is sympathy buying in medical-device names rather than a single company-specific headline.

themes.name: Commercial, Office & Home Furniture Retailers and Manufacturers
themes.description: BOBS looks to be moving on its Q2 2026 earnings release from August 6, which the company said was the catalyst in its latest 8-K filing. For MLKN, the clearest news driver this week is the August 8 filing showing Sei Investments increased its MillerKnoll stake by 208.6%, a large ownership boost that often lifts shares. HNI’s move is likely tied to the same furniture-sector read-through rather than a company-specific headline, but I don’t see a distinct catalyst in the results provided.

themes.name: Private Equity & Alternative Asset Management Platforms
themes.description: The main catalyst is renewed optimism around the alternative-asset managers trade after Nvidia’s $500 billion AI-financing announcement, which lifted sentiment for firms tied to private credit, infrastructure, and AI-related capital deployment. For BAM specifically, the move is also supported by its own strong Q2 results and record fundraising, while OWL has an added boost from analyst target hikes and recent fund-raising/fee-growth headlines.

themes.name: AI GPU Compute Infrastructure & Cloud Services
themes.description: CRWV and SMCI are higher this week because both reported blowout earnings that reinforced the AI infrastructure demand story. CoreWeave posted strong revenue growth plus a huge backlog and raised guidance, while Super Micro beat expectations and gave a much stronger revenue forecast tied to AI server demand. There’s also a broader tailwind from the July CPI print coming in tame, which helped tech and growth stocks extend the move.

themes.name: Electrical Connectivity & Utility Network Hardware
themes.description: PLPC is being pushed higher by upbeat Q2 results and follow-on analyst upgrades, especially Freedom Capital’s move to a strong-buy and higher target after the company posted record second-quarter sales. The latest move also appears tied to renewed buying interest after those earnings and upgrade headlines.

themes.name: Peptide & Hormone Therapies for Metabolic & Endocrine Disorders
themes.description: XERS is higher on Q2 earnings: record revenue, raised 2026 guidance, and completion of its convertible note retirement, which cleaned up the balance sheet. PTGX is being driven by strong Q2 profitability/commercial launch momentum plus analyst upgrades tied to Icotyde and pipeline optimism. For MBX and CORT, the likely catalyst is the same broad biotech bid, but I don’t have enough sourced company-specific news in the results to pin down a single headline.

themes.name: U.S. Government/Defense Contract Surge
themes.description: PLTR’s move this week is mainly being driven by its blowout Q2 earnings, with revenue up about 93% year over year and results well above expectations, which sparked a multi-day momentum rally. Additional support came from bullish analyst actions, including Bank of America raising its price target, plus broader strength in AI/software stocks.

themes.name: AI data center infrastructure buildout
themes.description: All three are benefiting directly from hyperscaler/AI data center capital spending: Backblaze secured a multi-exabyte AI storage deal with CoreWeave, Fluence was named a battery storage partner in Nvidia/Siemens' AI data center power architecture, and Monolithic Power's record revenue was driven by 164% YoY growth in its Enterprise Data segment tied to AI compute power delivery.

themes.name: Oilfield Equipment & Contract Drilling Services
themes.description: NESR is higher this week on a blowout Q2 2026 earnings report: revenue of $520.8 million beat expectations by a wide margin, with stronger-than-expected earnings, cash flow, and EBITDA. Investors are also reacting to a governance update showing PricewaterhouseCoopers will replace Grant Thornton as independent auditor starting in FY2027.

themes.name: Government & Defense IT Services Providers
themes.description: LDOS is higher this week mainly on its Q2 2026 earnings beat and management’s raised full-year 2026 guidance, which cited strong defense demand. Investors are also reacting to new defense/AI contract wins and recent bullish analyst target increases, including Citigroup’s and BNP Paribas’s hikes.

themes.name: Hospital & Behavioral Health Facility Procedure Volume Recovery
themes.description: The main catalyst is better-than-expected Q2 earnings and raised full-year guidance across the group, especially Encompass Health, which reported a strong beat and lifted its 2026 outlook. EHC also got a boost from guidance increases and a recent analyst price-target raise, while UHS and THC are likely moving in sympathy with the positive read-through for hospital and rehab operators.

themes.name: Cinema Exhibition & Premium Large-Format Recovery
themes.description: The main catalyst is strong box-office momentum, especially Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, which has driven record IMAX ticket sales and lifted sentiment across theater names like CNK and IMAX. Cinemark is also benefiting from a very strong Q2 North American box office and premium-format demand, while IMAX got an extra boost from a recent earnings beat and record IMAX revenues.

themes.name: IT Consulting & Business Process Outsourcing Services
themes.description: The main catalyst is Cognizant’s late-July Q2 earnings beat and raised FY2026 guidance, which showed better revenue, higher EPS outlook, and a new $2 billion buyback. ACN and IT are moving in sympathy with the stronger consulting/IT-services tape, helped by the same AI-execution narrative and risk-on momentum in the group.

themes.name: Inflammatory Disease & Immunology Biologics
themes.description: SYRE, ORKA, and CLYM look like they’re moving mostly on sector/peer momentum rather than a single company-specific headline, with biotech breadth and “cluster-wide strength” cited as the main driver for SYRE and ORKA. DNTH is being lifted by analyst bullishness after HC Wainwright kept a Buy rating and raised its price target to $158, while CLYM has also had a fresh Buy reiteration from William Blair.

themes.name: Specialty Pharmaceutical Commercialization & Rare Disease Drugs
themes.description: OMER is moving on its Q2 earnings release today, with the company having already flagged the report and conference call as the near-term catalyst. KNSA, LQDA, HRMY, RYTM, and ETON are also being bid ahead of or around earnings/updates, with ETON specifically lifted by a higher H.C. Wainwright price target and revised model ahead of its Thursday earnings.

themes.name: Insurance Brokerage & Distribution Services
themes.description: The move is mostly being driven by a positive read-through on the insurance-brokerage group: stronger pricing, steady demand, and consolidation/M&A tailwinds are supporting AJG, BRO, WTW, and BWIN. For WTW specifically, recent bullish analyst actions and its strong Q2 organic growth are also helping, while AJG has a fresh earnings beat behind it and BWIN is getting some support from its embedded-insurance growth story.

themes.name: B2B Digital Financial Infrastructure & Payment Rails Modernization
themes.description: ACIW is higher this week mainly on its Q2 earnings beat and raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to about $1.895–$1.925 billion, which signaled stronger execution in its payments software business. The upside is also being helped by supportive analyst action, including a price-target raise to $66 from DA Davidson.

themes.name: Life Insurance & Annuity Providers
themes.description: The common catalyst is a broader rally in U.S. life and health insurers, likely driven by rotation into defensive financials and strength in the group rather than company-specific news. UNM, MET, PRU, EQH, CRBG, and LNC are all in the same sector, so a sector-wide move is the most plausible explanation; if you want, I can pin down the exact headline or rating upgrade behind the move.

themes.name: Wealth Management & Retail Brokerage Platforms
themes.description: The common catalyst is a broader rates/markets tailwind: a weak U.S. jobs report pushed Treasury yields lower and strengthened expectations that the Fed will stay on hold, which lifted financials and wealth managers broadly this week. Reuters also noted strong earnings season momentum helping major indexes post their biggest weekly gains since mid-April, and that backdrop is supporting LPLA, RJF, SF, and SCHW. AMP has its own company-specific kicker from a strong half-year earnings beat plus a new share buyback, which is amplifying the move there.

themes.name: Building Envelope, Ceilings & Interior Construction Products
themes.description: CSL is being lifted by Carlisle’s latest dividend hike — its 50th straight annual increase — which reinforced cash-flow confidence and coincided with post-earnings strength. AWI and OC are higher on the broader housing/building-products rebound and the same “roofing/replace cycle” optimism, with Carlisle’s move and related sector sentiment spilling over into peers.

themes.name: Precious Metals Miners Velocity Breakout
themes.description: WPM is being lifted by its blowout Q2 results: revenue and profit both jumped sharply, the company beat estimates, and management kept the 2026 outlook intact. PPTA is moving on its new Stibnite project news, where it identified higher-grade gold/antimony targets plus potential tungsten zones; for SKE, ASM, SA, and AYA, the likely common driver is spillover strength in gold/silver/miners rather than a single company-specific catalyst.

themes.name: U.S. Passenger Airlines
themes.description: The main catalyst is a broader airline rally driven by lower oil prices, which improves margins for carriers like UAL, DAL, SKYW, and ALK. There’s also specific support from upbeat airline industry demand and recent earnings/guidance strength, especially for United and Delta.

themes.name: AI Data-Center Power & Physical Infrastructure Buildout
themes.description: Surging AI compute demand is driving capital into the physical power and siting infrastructure that feeds data centers — private electric grids, colocation/interconnection real estate, and advanced/SMR nuclear generation are all being bid up as enablers of AI power supply, not as compute/chip plays themselves.

themes.name: European Bank Stocks
themes.description: The main catalyst is a sector-wide rally in European banks, helped by strong results, upbeat capital returns, and share buyback announcements from lenders like BBVA. BBVA is also getting a direct boost from its own higher profitability outlook and new buyback plan, while NatWest, Barclays, Lloyds, ING, and Deutsche Bank are likely moving with the same group trade.

themes.name: Industrial Construction Execution & On-Site Supply Chain
themes.description: DNOW is moving higher mainly on its Q2 earnings beat and raised full-year outlook: revenue and EPS topped estimates, operating cash flow hit a record, and management lifted guidance on stronger U.S. demand and faster MRC Global synergy gains. The stock’s jump also reflects optimism that the MRC integration is translating into better cash generation and cost savings sooner than expected. ROAD’s catalyst appears to be analyst support plus infrastructure-related tailwinds: Raymond James reiterated a Strong Buy and added it to its Analyst Current Favorites list, while S&P SmallCap 600 inclusion and the Ellsworth acquisition are adding to sentiment.

themes.name: Containerboard & Corrugated Packaging Producers
themes.description: The move in PKG, IP, and GPK this week is mainly being driven by a broader packaging-sector rebound tied to stronger pricing-cycle and earnings commentary, not a single company-specific headline. For IP and SW, the recent Q2 prints and upbeat sector notes around linerboard/pricing momentum helped sentiment, while GPK has also been supported by its Q2 update and reaffirmed 2026 sales outlook.

themes.name: SMB & Workforce Business Services Platforms
themes.description: Auto-retired 2026-08-13: dropped during merge/absorption (no successor found) (prior stage Fading, 2 tickers).

themes.name: U.S. Oil & Gas E&P Recovery
themes.description: Auto-retired 2026-08-13: absorbed/superseded by 'Oilfield Services & Drilling Rigs' (prior stage Nascent, 5 tickers).

themes.name: Space & Unmanned Defense Systems
themes.description: The main catalyst is a strong wave of space/defense earnings and contract news: Voyager raised guidance after record bookings and revenue, Redwire posted a big revenue beat with record backlog, and Rocket Lab got a major Space Force award, which is lifting the whole group. Karman’s move likely ties to sector rotation plus anticipation around its own results, while SPCX is benefiting from the broader re-rating of recently listed space names. AVAV’s and KTOS’s strength is more likely spillover from the same defense-space bid rather than a single company-specific headline.

themes.name: Defense Electronics & Aerospace Subsystem Suppliers
themes.description: The main catalyst is strong aerospace/defense earnings and guidance: ATI jumped after a Q2 beat and raised outlook, and Embraer lifted its 2026 free cash flow guidance. BA and RTX are also benefiting from the same defense/aviation demand theme, while AADX got a bullish BofA call tied to space and missile demand. I don’t see a separate company-specific headline in the results for DPC or EMBJ beyond Embraer’s guidance update.

themes.name: AI Chip & Interconnect Supply Chain Enablement
themes.description: The main catalyst is a sector-wide rerating in optical/AI networking names after reports that U.S. regulators are considering restrictions on new Chinese optical transceivers, which is boosting domestic suppliers like AXTI, SITM, COHR, AEHR, ONTO, and COHU. For COHR and AEHR in particular, the move is also being reinforced by strong AI/datacenter demand and earnings momentum, with COHR trading ahead of its report and AEHR benefiting from its burn-in/silicon photonics story. AXTI’s rally is additionally supported by a recent earnings beat and raised guidance tied to indium phosphide demand.

themes.name: Industrial Equipment Rental & Material Handling
themes.description: CMCO’s move is being driven by a Citi note adding it to a 30-day upside catalyst watchlist, with the bank citing stronger copper prices and positive earnings revisions. SUNB is rallying on a U.S. Department of Defense/Office of Strategic Capital conditional loan commitment of up to $400 million for its scandium project. HRI appears to be following company-specific strength tied to its Q2 turnaround and a completed buyback, not a broad sector move.

themes.name: Life Science Tools & Analytical Instruments
themes.description: The main catalyst is earnings beats and raised guidance: MTD, WAT, TMO, RGEN, and ATECH are all getting bid on company-specific upside from recent quarterly reports or upbeat outlooks. The clearest examples in the feed are Watts Water’s blowout Q2 beat plus higher full-year guidance and T-Mobile’s rally after Deutsche Telekom lifted its outlook tied to TMUS strength. For the others, Thermo Fisher and Mettler-Toledo are also being treated as post-earnings/sector momentum names, while ATECH’s move appears to be part of the broader tech/AI rally and not a single idiosyncratic headline in the results provided.

themes.name: Private Mortgage Insurance
themes.description: The move in MTG, NMIH, and ESNT this week is mainly being driven by strong Q2 mortgage-insurer earnings and upbeat post-earnings momentum, especially for ESNT after it beat estimates and hit a 52-week high. NMIH’s latest call also pointed to continued insured-portfolio growth, disciplined expenses, and stable credit quality, which is supporting the group.

themes.name: Copper Mining & Production
themes.description: The main catalyst is the ongoing copper rally: copper is near record highs on tight supply and strong demand from electrification, AI/data-center buildout, and grid spending, which is lifting copper names broadly. For ERO and TECK specifically, recent earnings/operational strength and upbeat guidance are amplifying the move, while FCX has also been helped by stronger realized copper prices and cost discipline. HBM is likely being pulled higher by the same copper/commodity risk-on tape rather than a company-specific headline.

themes.name: Silver-Focused Primary Miners
themes.description: The main catalyst is a broad rally in precious-metals miners, with silver/gold strength lifting names like AG, CDE, EXK, HL, SVM, and PAAS this week. PAAS and EXK also have earnings-related attention, which is adding to the move.

themes.name: Industrial Equipment & Flow Control – Capex Cycle Recovery
themes.description: The main catalyst is a wave of upbeat analyst actions after strong Q2 results: Morgan Stanley upgraded LECO on improved growth outlook, UBS initiated at Buy on the capex cycle, and several names like ITT also got higher targets after solid earnings. For FLS, EMR, PH, and ITT, the broader industrial group is being bid on expectations for stronger industrial demand, automation/capex spending, and better execution.

themes.name: AI-Driven Power & Grid Infrastructure Boom
themes.description: EMCOR and Quanta Services both posted record revenues and dramatically raised guidance driven by surging demand for electrical construction, grid modernization, and data center power infrastructure tied to AI and electrification megatrends.

themes.name: Quantum Computing Hardware & Software
themes.description: The main catalyst is earnings and guidance, led by IonQ’s strong Q2 print and raised FY2026 outlook, which is lifting sentiment across the quantum group. QBTS and RGTI are also getting a sympathy bid from the sector rotation, while INFQ is moving on the same broader quantum/AI speculation and follow-through from IonQ’s positive read-through. For RGTI specifically, the extra support is coming from government-contract/CHIPS Act funding headlines and the market viewing quantum names as near-term beneficiaries of federal spending.

themes.name: Building Products & Home Improvement Suppliers
themes.description: LII (HVAC systems), MAS (faucets/cabinets), PPG (paints/coatings) and SITE (landscape/building supply distribution) are all levered to residential repair-remodel and new construction capex cycles, moving together as housing activity data improves.

themes.name: Development-Stage Gold Exploration & Project Juniors
themes.description: A subset of gold miners in Cluster A — HYMC, NG, and AUGO — are pre-production or early-restart development companies advancing single flagship gold projects (Hycroft, Donlin, respectively) rather than established multi-mine producers. Their price action is more levered to project financing/permitting news and gold price optionality than current cash flow, differentiating them from the senior producer cohort in the broader gold rotation theme.

themes.name: U.S. Domestic Steel Producers
themes.description: The move is being driven less by company-specific news and more by a sector-wide steel rally, with investors rotating into domestic steel names on expectations that strong pricing, solid demand, and tariff protection will support margins. Recent headlines also point to Steel Dynamics’ own strength and broader bullish sentiment spilling over to Nucor and Cleveland-Cliffs.

themes.name: Property & Casualty Insurance Underwriters
themes.description: The main catalyst is better-than-expected Q2 earnings across the group, especially TRV’s big beat and SKWD’s Q2 EPS/revenue beat, which is lifting sentiment in property-and-casualty insurers. TRV also got a boost from a larger buyback authorization, while SKWD’s rise was helped by Truist raising its price target to $75 and keeping a buy rating. ALL, AFG, THG, and HCI are moving with the same insurer/earnings momentum rather than a company-specific headline.

themes.name: Gold & Precious Metals Miners Rotation
themes.description: The common catalyst is strength in the gold-mining complex after a wave of company-specific positives: SSRM on Q2 results, reinstated dividend/buybacks, and portfolio cleanup; EQX on strong Q2 results plus higher guidance after the Orla merger; and the group is also being supported by firmer gold prices and improved sector sentiment. For IAG, HYMC, EGO, and CGAU, the likely driver is the same broad “gold upside” trade rather than one single shared headline, with investors rotating into producers and developers after stronger earnings/guidance and balance-sheet updates across the sector.

themes.name: U.S. Apparel & Fashion Recovery
themes.description: The main catalyst is a Barclays apparel-sector re-rating: Barclays upgraded ANF to Equal Weight from Underweight and lifted its target to $114, citing lower tariff pressure, better promotional trends, and manageable inventory. That upbeat read-through is also helping SHOO and URBN as investors rotate into stronger apparel names. A broader retail/consumer-discretionary bid is adding support, but the Barclays note is the clearest trigger.

themes.name: Oilfield Services & Drilling Rigs
themes.description: APA, NOG, OVV, and the broader E&P group are higher mainly because crude is being lifted by renewed Middle East/Strait of Hormuz risk premium, with Brent holding in the mid-$80s after reports of disrupted shipping and escalating tensions. NAT, INSW, and TNK are moving on the same oil/shipping disruption theme, plus tanker-specific headlines around stronger spot rates, tighter vessel availability, and in NAT’s case plans to raise its dividend on stronger market conditions.

themes.name: Canadian Big Banks
themes.description: The main catalyst is a broadly bullish turn on Canadian banks: TSX financials are near record highs, with investor sentiment helped by expectations for stable rates and solid earnings growth. Analyst target-price upgrades are also supporting the group, which is lifting BMO, BNS, TD, CM, and RY together.

themes.name: U.S. Regional & Mid-Cap Commercial Banks
themes.description: The week’s move in HWC, FITB, EWBC, UMBF, CFG, and PNC is being driven mainly by a broad regional-bank rally on softer rate-hike expectations plus a favorable earnings read-through from big-bank results. Investors are also reacting to strong Q2 bank prints and improving sentiment on margins/deposit costs, with PNC getting an extra boost from its own strong quarterly beat and higher analyst targets.

themes.name: Office REIT Recovery & Re-Rating
themes.description: The main catalyst appears to be the broad real estate rally tied to softer inflation data and lower rate expectations, which is supporting office REITs like BXP and its peers. For BXP specifically, recent strength also lines up with its strong Q2 leasing/revenue beat and higher 2026 outlook, plus a new $1.2 billion construction loan for the 343 Madison project.

themes.name: Precious Metals Royalty & Streaming Companies
themes.description: The main catalyst is the late-week Q2 earnings/rally in gold royalty and streaming names, especially Wheaton Precious Metals’ stronger-than-expected results and higher realized gold prices, which is lifting sentiment across the group. Royal Gold also got a boost from its own strong Q2 print and raised full-year volume guidance, reinforcing the move in RGLD. themes.name: AI-Driven Power & Grid Infrastructure Boom
themes.description: The common catalyst is the same broad theme: AI/data-center power demand and grid electrification, which is lifting electrical and industrial contractors like PWR, EME, BE, EROC, and ETN. Recent notes also point to stronger-than-expected results, raised guidance, and analyst target increases for some of these names, with Eaton and Quanta specifically highlighted as beneficiaries of data-center and grid-spending growth.

themes.name: Gold & Precious Metals Miners Rotation
themes.description: The main catalyst is the surge in gold prices, which is lifting gold miners broadly this week. EQX, AEM, HMY, KGC, GFI, and ARIS are also getting a boost from company-specific updates like stronger earnings/guidance, but the common driver is the sharp move in bullion above $4,300/oz.

themes.name: Industrial Equipment & Flow Control – Capex Cycle Recovery
themes.description: IEX is likely being lifted by a Mizuho upgrade after its strong Q2 beat and raised outlook, while LECO is higher on broker upgrades, including Morgan Stanley and UBS, after its solid earnings and cash-generation update. PH, EMR, DCI, and FLS also look tied to the broader industrial/data-center demand theme and stronger order/backlog commentary, but the clearest named catalyst in the results is the analyst upgrade wave.

themes.name: U.S. Apparel & Fashion Recovery
themes.description: The main catalyst is a sector-wide apparel/risk-on move: Barclays upgraded ANF to Equalweight and raised its target, citing better tariff, promotional, and inventory trends, which is lifting sentiment across retail apparel names. URBN, CROX, SHOO, and VSXY are moving higher largely on the same read-through from improving apparel/consumer-discretionary momentum and a softer inflation backdrop that supports growth and retail multiples.

themes.name: U.S. Passenger Airlines
themes.description: The main catalyst is a broader airline-sector rally tied to lower jet-fuel expectations and still-strong summer travel demand, with premium-cabin and loyalty-revenue trends also helping sentiment. United’s stronger guidance and premium-capacity push have added to the move, while SkyWest is getting extra support from fleet/aircraft-deal news.

themes.name: Digital Payments Processing & Merchant Acquiring Networks
themes.description: PYPL is being driven mainly by takeover speculation after reports that PayPal’s board rejected a $60.50/share bid, reportedly from Stripe, which reinforced the market’s view that PYPL may be undervalued. FLYW is moving on its Q2 2026 earnings, raised full-year guidance, and ongoing share repurchases, with the buyback and outlook upgrade giving the stock a clear catalyst.

themes.name: Development-Stage Gold Exploration & Project Juniors
themes.description: AUGO’s move is being driven mainly by its recent Q2 earnings beat, dividend/buyback updates, and renewed buying in gold/copper miners rather than a single new company headline. HYMC is likely being pulled higher by the same broad precious-metals/mining rotation, but the provided results don’t show a specific HYMC-only catalyst this week. If you want, I can also break down whether the move is more earnings-driven or sector-driven for each name.

themes.name: Property & Casualty Insurance Underwriters
themes.description: The common catalyst is a strong Q2 earnings/reaction-to-results move in specialty and property-casualty insurers: SKWD and TRV are explicitly higher on earnings beats, while RLI and AFG are also being lifted by the same “better-than-expected results / higher profit outlook” trade in the group. THG and SLDE appear to be moving with the broader insurance/risk sector strength rather than a single company-specific headline, so this looks like a sector rerating on solid earnings and improving sentiment.

themes.name: Canadian Big Banks
themes.description: The main catalyst is broad analyst optimism on Canadian banks ahead of third-quarter earnings, with multiple price-target upgrades across BMO, BNS, RY, TD, and CM this week. The rally is also being supported by sector strength and expectations that several banks can deliver better-than-feared earnings, loan growth, or margin expansion.

themes.name: Precious Metals Royalty & Streaming Companies
themes.description: The main catalyst is the broad gold rally, driven by softer U.S. jobs data that pushed down Treasury yields and the dollar, boosting gold and the royalty names with it. FNV also got a boost from its Q2 update/earnings-related news flow, while RGLD and WPM were helped by upbeat quarterly results and stronger precious-metals pricing.

themes.name: U.S. Regional & Mid-Cap Commercial Banks
themes.description: The move is mostly being driven by a broad regional-bank rally, not one single company-specific headline. The clearest near-term catalyst in the tape is better-than-expected Q2 earnings and analyst follow-through across the group, which has kept names like ZION, EWBC, and MTB bid, while recent bank-specific headlines have been mostly neutral-to-supportive rather than transformational.

themes.name: Containerboard & Corrugated Packaging Producers
themes.description: GPK and PKG are being helped mainly by a packaging-sector rerating after Graphic Packaging’s Q2 beat, reaffirmed full-year guidance near the high end, and a fresh round of price increases. The clearest single catalyst this week for GPK specifically is the dividend hike: Graphic Packaging raised its quarterly dividend by 33%, which also lifted the stock. Packaging Corp. of America (PKG) has also been supported by earlier news of record shipments and a containerboard price hike.

themes.name: Copper Mining & Production
themes.description: The main catalyst is the ongoing copper rally: copper is near record highs on tight supply and strong demand from electrification, AI/data-center buildout, and grid spending, which is lifting copper names broadly. For ERO and TECK specifically, recent earnings/operational strength and upbeat guidance are amplifying the move, while FCX has also been helped by stronger realized copper prices and cost discipline. HBM is likely being pulled higher by the same copper/commodity risk-on tape rather than a company-specific headline.

themes.name: AI Data-Center Power & Physical Infrastructure Buildout
themes.description: NNE is being lifted mainly by its Q3 earnings beat: the company reported a smaller-than-expected loss of $0.19 per share, and management also highlighted progress on nuclear licensing, regulatory milestones, and commercial partnerships. A secondary boost came from news that the NRC accepted its construction permit application for the KRONOS MMR, which keeps the project moving through formal regulatory review.

themes.name: U.S. Domestic Steel Producers
themes.description: The move is being driven less by company-specific news and more by a sector-wide steel rally, with investors rotating into domestic steel names on expectations that strong pricing, solid demand, and tariff protection will support margins. Recent headlines also point to Steel Dynamics’ own strength and broader bullish sentiment spilling over to Nucor and Cleveland-Cliffs.

themes.name: Office REIT Recovery & Re-Rating
themes.description: The main catalyst appears to be the broad real estate rally tied to softer inflation data and lower rate expectations, which is supporting office REITs like BXP and its peers. For BXP specifically, recent strength also lines up with its strong Q2 leasing/revenue beat and higher 2026 outlook, plus a new $1.2 billion construction loan for the 343 Madison project.

themes.name: Global Steel & Metal Producers Recovery
themes.description: MTX is higher mainly on a recent earnings-related move: Minerals Technologies posted a beat and the stock was up after-hours, with the latest coverage also noting a downgrade that likely adds to volatility rather than driving the move. If you meant MT (ArcelorMittal) instead of MTX, the catalyst is different: the stock has been supported by stronger operating profit, lower debt, and a better-than-expected dividend, with recent coverage also pointing to favorable macro and steel-demand conditions.

themes.name: Electrical Infrastructure Products & Systems Installation
themes.description: IESC’s move appears tied to its recent robust earnings report, which pushed the stock up sharply after the announcement. ATKR’s rally is being driven by Prysmian’s agreed all-cash acquisition at $95/share, with a roughly 30% premium.

themes.name: Industrial HVAC, Plumbing & Fabricated Copper Products
themes.description: The main catalyst is CSW Industrials’ late-July fiscal Q1 2027 beat, with revenue and EPS coming in above expectations and management reaffirming an active acquisition/share-repurchase strategy. The stock also got a lift from analyst upgrades and bullish price-target revisions in early August.

themes.name: For-Profit Postsecondary Education
themes.description: LOPE, PRDO, and STRA are likely being lifted by a renewed move in the for-profit/education group, with PRDO specifically boosted by last week’s earnings beat and 13.3% dividend hike. PRDO also said first-half 2026 operating income growth was 14.4% and raised full-year EPS guidance, which can spill over to peers like LOPE and STRA. STRA appears to be moving more with sector sympathy than a company-specific headline.

themes.name: Automotive Dealership Groups
themes.description: ABG’s move this week is tied mainly to its strong Q2 beat and aggressive buybacks, which helped lift the stock after earnings. AN’s catalyst is the latest quarterly results showing record finance profit and stronger wholesale parts revenue, while GPI’s tape looks more like analyst noise than a fresh company-specific news driver.

themes.name: Regulated Electric Utility Holding Companies
themes.description: The main catalyst is a broad utility-sector bid tied to a strong Q2 earnings season and upbeat guidance, especially AEP’s large capex plan and reaffirmed outlook, which are supporting the group. AEE and ED also beat Q2 earnings estimates, and CMS/CNP/DTE are likely rising with the same defensive rotation into regulated utilities.

themes.name: Uranium Feedstock & Mining Supply
themes.description: UEC and UUUU are uranium (and byproduct rare-earth/titanium) miners showing sustained multi-week RS acceleration, reflecting renewed investor interest in uranium feedstock supply as nuclear power demand expectations rise. Both are pure-play domestic uranium miners rather than reactor technology developers, forming a distinct upstream supply theme.

themes.name: Apartment & Residential REITs
themes.description: The main catalyst is renewed rate-cut optimism after the latest macro/news flow, which has boosted REITs broadly and helped AVB, ELS, EQR, and UDR move higher together. EQR has also been singled out as benefiting from investor optimism tied to the recent 90-day pause on reciprocal tariffs, while UDR has additional support from its raised 2026 FFO guidance and buyback/dividend actions after earnings.

themes.name: Skilled Nursing & Senior Housing REITs
themes.description: The main catalyst is Q2 earnings: CTRE posted record investment activity and raised 2026 guidance, while NHI beat EPS and increased its dividend, both of which are supporting the entire healthcare REIT group. LTC and OHI are also being helped by the same sector rotation into defensive income names, with OHI getting an additional lift from expectations that its earnings/FFO trend is stabilizing.

themes.name: Industrial & Logistics Warehouse REITs
themes.description: EGP, FR, PLD and TRNO are all bulk industrial/logistics warehouse landlords moving together on e-commerce and supply-chain reshoring demand for distribution space, distinct from office, apartment or hotel REIT baskets already covered.

themes.name: Building Products & Home Improvement Suppliers
themes.description: LII (HVAC systems), MAS (faucets/cabinets), PPG (paints/coatings) and SITE (landscape/building supply distribution) are all levered to residential repair-remodel and new construction capex cycles, moving together as housing activity data improves.

themes.name: Trucking & Freight Logistics
themes.description: HUBG, JBHT, ODFL, SNDR and XPO are all major trucking/intermodal freight logistics operators moving together on early signs of freight cycle recovery and rate stabilization.

themes.name: Electronics Manufacturing & Semiconductor Packaging Supply Chain
themes.description: AMKR (OSAT packaging), SANM (electronics manufacturing services), TTMI (PCB manufacturing) and AMSC (grid/superconductor tech) form a correlated supply-chain cluster benefiting from reshoring and AI hardware assembly demand.

themes.name: Bitcoin Mining & HPC Compute Pivot Operators
themes.description: Bitcoin miners are increasingly repurposing power infrastructure and data centers toward AI/HPC hosting contracts, driving correlated price action across the group even as pure mining economics diverge. This cluster captures the crypto-to-AI infrastructure pivot trade distinct from the pure AI cloud compute names.

themes.name: Emerging Bitcoin & AI Cloud Compute Miners
themes.description: CLSK, CORZ, IREN, MARA, NBIS, RIOT and WULF form a distinct high-correlation cluster of crypto-mining operators pivoting toward AI/HPC cloud compute hosting, separate tickers from the existing narrower Bitcoin Mining theme.

themes.name: Lodging & Hotel REITs
themes.description: DRH, HST, PEB, and SHO are all hotel-focused REITs moving together on travel demand and RevPAR trends, showing high residual correlation ahead of any broad hospitality narrative. This is a distinct, more specific cluster than generic office/commercial REIT themes already tracked.

themes.name: Emerging Defense & Aerospace Hardware Suppliers
themes.description: A cohort of small-cap hardware makers serving defense/aerospace supply chains — metal additive manufacturing (VELO), positioning-navigation-timing infrastructure (NN), precision optics (LPTH), and commercial drones (UMAC) — are all showing sustained multi-week RS acceleration ahead of broader recognition, likely tied to rising defense/aerospace capex and drone procurement momentum.

themes.name: Nuclear Fuel Cycle & Microreactor Development
themes.description: A tight correlation cluster (NNE, OKLO, SMR, UUUU) plus rotation-candidate STDN points to accumulation across the advanced nuclear fuel supply chain — from uranium feedstock (UUUU) to fuel fabrication (STDN) to microreactor and SMR developers (NNE, OKLO, SMR). This is a more specific fuel-cycle sub-theme than the broader reactor-technology basket, capturing the buildout narrative ahead of DOE/utility contract announcements.

themes.name: Optical Interconnect & Photonics for AI Data Center Networking
themes.description: LITE, COHR, and CRDO all supply optical components, photonics, and high-speed connectivity chips that address the interconnect bottleneck inside AI data centers, distinct from the broader semiconductor equipment/materials names lumped into the general AI interconnect supply chain theme. Rising bandwidth needs from AI clusters are driving demand for optical transceivers and DSPs.

themes.name: Optical Transceiver & Interconnect Components for AI Networking
themes.description: AAOI, LITE, COHR and CRDO all make optical transceivers/interconnect modules that are the physical layer enabling AI datacenter networking bandwidth scaling. AAOI is a newly emerging RS leader in this specific optical-component niche, distinct from the broader chip/equipment supply chain theme it would otherwise be lumped into.

themes.name: Power Generation & Grid Infrastructure for AI Data Centers
themes.description: FRMI (private electric grid infrastructure for AI computing), GEV (power generation and grid electrification), EROC (distributed power generation deployment), and AMRC (energy efficiency and renewable solutions) are all levered to the same catalyst: surging electricity demand from AI data centers straining grid capacity. This is distinct from the nuclear-fuel cluster, focused instead on near-term power delivery and grid buildout solutions.

themes.name: Rare disease/specialty pharma earnings beats
themes.description: Each is a commercial-stage specialty/rare-disease biopharma posting explosive product-sales growth and raised guidance following a recent approval or launch inflection.
